Unlike existing insider attacks that inject misleading information directly into the current collaboration, misinformation stored in shared memory can later appear as successful team experience and gain greater credibility and influence. We propose MIMPA (Multi-Agent Insider Memory Poisoning Attack), which exploits this vulnerability using only normal participation privileges, without direct memory access. During an earlier task, the malicious agent embeds a target-specific payload while helping the team answer correctly, allowing the payload to be retained in a successful collaboration record. When retrieved for a later target task, this poisoned record can steer benign agents toward a designated wrong answer, further amplified by malicious triggering. Across three benchmarks and two LLM backbones, MIMPA substantially outperforms existing insider attacks and remains effective under hierarchical memory management, while auditing only partially mitigates it. These results reveal that shared memory intended to accumulate team experience can become a persistent channel for insider attacks. Our code is available at https://github.com/ahnji0520/MIMPA-code.

papers.title: Set-based comprehensive learning and particle swarm optimization with memory for discrete optimization problem
papers.abstract: This paper describes a novel algorithm of set-based comprehensive learning and particle swarm optimization with memory for discrete optimization problem. Our algorithm is an approach of searching for the best position in a set by referring to the current position when updating the solution. In order to show the validity of our algorithm, we examine numerical experiments compared to existing algorithms.

papers.title: Differential evolution with perturbation for continuous function optimization
papers.abstract: This paper presents differential evolution with perturbation (DEP) for continuous function optimization. Differential evolution is a simple and efficient algorithm. Perturbation is the phenomenon that the motion by the contribution of the main force is disturbed by the influence subsidiary power. In order to show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, we compare it to existing algorithms by CEC2017 datasets.

papers.title: Beyond Quantum Mechanics: From Nonlinear to Emergent and Solitonic Approaches
papers.abstract: This thesis investigates the role of nonlinearity in approaches beyond standard quantum mechanics, following a path from modifications of quantum dynamics to the possibility of an emergent statistical description. We first examine Weinberg's nonlinear formulation and its implications for the statistical interpretation of quantum states. We then discuss de Broglie-Bohm theory and the Madelung formulation, which provide a framework for comparing guided trajectories with ensemble descriptions involving momentum fluctuations. The Hall-Reginatto exact uncertainty approach identifies the fluctuation energy associated with the quantum potential. We then investigate whether quantum dynamics can emerge from the collective statistics of solitons in a fluctuating background, using a Galilean formulation of the complex sine-Gordon model. Within a weak-noise approximation, we identify a regime in which the statistics of the soliton centres reproduce the Schr{ö}dinger equation, with an effective action scale determined by the background fluctuations. This correspondence is established for Gaussian ensembles and potentials at most quadratic. These results provide a concrete setting for exploring how quantum dynamics can emerge as a statistical description of underlying nonlinear field dynamics.

papers.title: Exact nonstationary heat-excess statistics in the weakly asymmetric Kipnis--Marchioro--Presutti model
papers.abstract: Exact nonstationary large-deviation statistics remain scarce for interacting many-body systems. Here we employ the macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) to determine the complete long-time statistics of heat excess produced by an initially localized heat pulse in the weakly asymmetric Kipnis--Marchioro--Presutti model. We find a remarkable nonlocal canonical transformation which maps the weakly asymmetric MFT problem, including its initial and terminal conditions, onto the symmetric problem, previously solved exactly. The resulting rate function is an explicit nonlinear deformation of its symmetric counterpart. We also extend the solution to heat measured beyond an arbitrary observation point.

papers.title: Towards Efficient Attack Tree Generation from Attack Graphs for Unobservable Target Analysis
papers.abstract: Attack trees provide a structured approach to security analysis but traditionally require prior knowledge of the attacker's objective. In practice, this objective often remains hidden, even when some attacker actions are partially detected. This paper presents a methodology for generating attack trees without assuming a predefined target by modeling the threat environment as a constraint-weighted graph and applying temporal reachability analysis. The approach identifies probable attacker locations from partial observations and a time budget, carrying traversal cost as an attack-tree attribute. It then extracts target-oriented subgraphs that preserve feasible attack paths while eliminating irrelevant nodes. We demonstrate the framework across three scenarios: a single office building, a multi-building industrial complex, and a real IoT device-communication network recovered from the CICIoT2023 attack dataset. Compared with the baselines, our approach achieves a lower reduction factor while maintaining complete target preservation, substantially outperforming topology-only methods that ignore temporal constraints. We further perform a sensitivity analysis across 66 weight configurations, showing that target identification is stable when strategic value receives at least 20\% of the weight in the single building and at least 50\% in the multi-building complex, while additional experiments reveal sensitivity to perturbations of the underlying strategic-value prior.

papers.title: MOZAIC: An Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark for Telling What Is Fake
papers.abstract: Audio-video (AV) deepfakes can fake the face, the voice, or both. Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces. We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly. Fakes cover inner-face swapping, whole-frame video diffusion and voice conversion. MOZAIC has 137,745 clips from 15,014 source pairs and four tasks: T1 AV authenticity, T2 manipulation type, T3 identity verification and T4 explanation. We evaluate 12 AV multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), train four detectors and fine-tune MLLMs with LoRA. Overall, the best MLLM reaches only 35.6% on the four-way T1 and catches far more video-only fakes than voice-only fakes (43.6% vs 7.5%). Trained detectors reach 98.4% on T1, and LoRA fine-tuning raises explanation scores (OmniVinci 4.17 to 7.40, Qwen2.5-Omni 4.42 to 6.98), but the best T1 detector falls to 78.3% when the face-swap generator is held out of training, so generalization and explanation remain open. We release the dataset, the compact MOZAIC-SMALL split, the code and the prompts. https://vectorinstitute.github.io/mozaic/

papers.title: Power-Law Lower Bounds for Edges in Odd Induced Subgraphs
papers.abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $g(G)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an induced subgraph of $G$ in which every vertex has odd degree. Motivated by Scott's question of whether $g(G) \geq cm$ for every graph with $m$ edges, we prove that $g(G) \geq cm^{4/7}$ for every finite simple graph with $m \geq 1$ edges, where $c > 0$ is an absolute constant. For bipartite graphs, we obtain the stronger bound $g(B) \geq cm^{2/3}$.

papers.title: PEACE-TEST-PROTOCOL: Polarization-Keyed Examination Papers and Mandatory Issued Eyewear that Displace AI Glasses and Extend Universal Design
papers.abstract: Camera-equipped AI glasses turn an examination page into a query for a remote vision-language model. Device detection targets possession, and our companion work SEOYUN targets the model. PEACE-TEST-PROTOCOL instead changes who owns the eyewear. Every candidate wears authority-issued glasses for the whole session, and the question paper is printed so that it can be read only through them. As in cinema stereoscopy, a patterned laminate encodes the text in the handedness of circular polarization rather than in brightness. The page looks uniformly grey to the naked eye and to unfiltered cameras, and the issued circular analyzer reveals the text. Compulsory issued eyewear turns the smart-glasses form factor against itself. The face position is occupied by a device the authority supplies and collects, and a camera anywhere else needs its own analyzer. Spectacle wearers receive prescription inserts in the issued frame, low-vision candidates may use an offline assistive mixed-reality tier, and blind candidates keep braille, audio, and screen-reader formats. We derive the luminance and contrast budget and show why circular keying tolerates head tilt. A simulation study supports the analysis. A spectral Mueller model confirms tilt invariance and invisibility to linear-polarization cameras, but a 1 degree axis misregistration leaks a few percent of contrast. A capture-and-OCR experiment on English and Korean text shows that video averaging can recover leakage too weak to read in a single frame, so leakage must be bounded against the adversary's total photon budget. Data from 151 observers and 28 cameras show that spectral (metameric) keys are visible to all of them. The key carries no secrecy, and filtered covert cameras remain possible. All results are simulations; no prototypes, physical measurements, or human-subject results are reported.

papers.title: The Defect Is in the Arithmetic Between the Files: Static Detection of Exactly-Once Violations in Payment Pipelines
papers.abstract: Whether a streaming payment pipeline charges a customer twice after a restart turns on a comparison nobody performs: how long the provider remembers an idempotency key, against how stale a record can be when the pipeline processes it for the second time. The first number is in the provider's documentation. The second is not written anywhere. It is assembled from a checkpoint interval in one file, a recovery assumption in a runbook, a restart delay in a third and a source's lateness bound in a fourth. Each file is defensible alone; the fault is in the relation between them. We give a checker that gathers those facts and states the relations, and a synthesiser that turns 335 of the 515 findings into a runnable scenario: these records, kill the job here, bring it back after this long, and this is the observable. 245 of them produce two charges. The central measurement is how far apart the evidence lies. Across a corpus of 630 pipelines we generated, 210 of them cannot be derived from fewer than three artifacts, and no single artifact yields more than 35 of the 305 duration findings. Executing the witnesses corrected our own rules: two were demoted after their scenarios produced a repeated call the provider's idempotency absorbed rather than a second charge. All 16 selected live witnesses reproduced their predicted observable against a real Kafka broker with a real process kill, and a matched control in which the provider never forgets the key did not, attributing the second charge to the key lifetime, not the replay. Fault injection finds the same defects only if the tester already assumed a long enough outage: one willing to simulate five minutes finds 15% of them, and 12 hours is needed for all. A sweep also locates a configuration with no application-level fix, where above a 14-minute recovery assumption the transaction timeout required to survive it exceeds the broker's own cap.

papers.title: Predictive Self-Entropy in Dirichlet Universal Coding: A Factor-Two Central Limit Theorem and a Markov Extension
papers.abstract: Sequential universal coders produce both a realized log-loss and, before each symbol is observed, a predictive distribution with its own Shannon entropy. We compare the realized arithmetic code length with the cumulative predictive self-entropy, the prequential sum of the self-expected logarithmic scores of the issued forecasts. This forecast-only quantity is neither a plug-in entropy estimate nor a posterior entropy functional. For finite-alphabet memoryless sources and Dirichlet (add-$α$) sequential predictors, we prove a joint central limit theorem for the two normalized quantities. They have the same first-order entropy limit but different second-order fluctuations: for every nonuniform i.i.d. source, cumulative predictive self-entropy has exactly twice the leading asymptotic variance of realized code length, and the ordinary mean-square-error ratio converges to two. We also give its logarithmic bias coefficient. For fixed finite-order Markov sources with context-wise Dirichlet predictors, the factor-two result becomes a context/innovation covariance decomposition, recovering the i.i.d. factor two when only the innovation component contributes.

papers.title: Single-Photon Detectors for Optical Wireless Communications: A Tutorial
papers.abstract: Photon-counting receivers extend optical wireless communication (OWC) into regimes in which only a few detected photons are available per information bit, but the detector can no longer be treated as an interchangeable ideal counter. This tutorial develops a communication-oriented, port-to-bit framework for single-photon detection in indoor, terrestrial, airborne, space, underwater, non-line-of-sight, and integrated communication-and-sensing links. It compares SPADs, silicon photomultipliers, CMOS SPAD arrays, superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, PMT/MCP-PMT receivers, upconversion detectors, and emerging technologies through photon-detection efficiency, timing, active area, dynamic range, spectral coverage, readout, cooling, and integration requirements. Beginning with the ideal Poisson channel, the tutorial then develops communication-level models for dead time, recovery, finite-pixel occupancy, saturation, background counts, afterpulsing, crosstalk, nonuniformity, and event loss. These models are connected to modulation, likelihood-based detection, synchronization, channel estimation, soft decoding, and detector-aware receiver processing, with numerical studies that compare algorithms under a common detector and detectors under a common algorithm. Finally, a unified link-budget and system co-design methodology is used to relate photons per bit, sensitivity, bandwidth, data rate, and link margin, and representative demonstrations are normalized to expose practical tradeoffs. The central conclusion is that useful photon efficiency is an end-to-end property of the optical front end, detector, readout, and digital receiver, rather than a detector metric in isolation.

papers.title: One Release for All: Private Simple Linear Regression Via Improved Simplex Mapping
papers.abstract: We present a single-release extension of DP-RSS for private simple linear regression when both input and output are bounded in $[0,1]$. Rather than privately releasing several related sufficient-statistic estimates, we encode the required information in one unit-sensitivity vector and apply the Laplace mechanism once at the full privacy budget. The required least-squares sufficient statistics are then recovered by deterministic post-processing and used directly in an ordinary least-squares solve. We obtain variance reductions of $1.67$--$2.67\times$ relative to DP-RSS for several statistics. Experiments show that the benefit is most pronounced in the high-privacy regime, while the methods converge as privacy noise becomes negligible.

papers.title: Information Security Risk Preparedness in Electronic Data Interchange: A Comparative Assessment of General IT and Healthcare Environments
papers.abstract: Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) supports the exchange of structured information across business and healthcare environments, making information security and organizational risk management critical to reliable digital transactions. This study empirically assesses security-control preparedness and organizational risk-taking ability in EDI-related environments through a comparative analysis of General IT Professionals (GIT) and Healthcare EDI Professionals (HEP). A quantitative, cross-sectional survey was conducted with 100 respondents, equally divided between the two groups. Security Control Preparedness (SCP) and Threat Perception (TP) were validated using reliability and exploratory factor analyses, followed by group comparisons, correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression. HEP respondents reported significantly higher SCP than GIT respondents (M = 4.70 vs. 3.89, p < 0.001, d = 1.06) and higher Organizational Risk-Taking Ability (ORTA) (M = 6.14 vs. 5.28, p = 0.001, d = 0.66). In contrast, GIT respondents reported higher threat perception (M = 2.95 vs. 2.04, p < 0.001, d = 0.72). SCP was positively associated with ORTA (r = 0.479, p < 0.001), whereas TP showed a significant negative association (r = -0.610, p < 0.001). A parsimonious regression model incorporating SCP and TP explained 41.6% of the variance in ORTA (R^2 = 0.416, adjusted R^2 = 0.404, p < 0.001). Based on these empirical findings, an EDI Risk Management Framework (EDI-RMF) is proposed integrating governance, human and organizational security, technical safeguards, physical protection, and continuous monitoring. The findings provide empirical evidence for strengthening information-security risk management in EDI-enabled environments, particularly within developing-economy contexts.

papers.title: Copying versus self-construction in cellular automata: an algorithmic-information approach to self-reproduction
papers.abstract: What distinguishes an object that reproduces itself from one that is merely copied by its environment? We propose an answer based on algorithmic information and interventions, in cellular automata. Copies of an object are identified by the algorithmic information they share with it. Its code and its machine are identified by perturbations: changes to the code are inherited by the offspring, changes to the machine are not, since the offspring's machine is rebuilt from the code. An object is a self-reproducer if it proliferates, admits such a decomposition, its machine can be decoded from its code, and removing the machine stops the code from being copied. The definition uses only counts, interventions and upper bounds on information, so it is not undermined by exhaustive search. We prove that it excludes trivial "infection" dynamics and rules that copy every pattern, and reduce the claim that it includes the construction of von Neumann and Burks, but not its constituents, to explicit hypotheses. We measure the amount of self-reproduction by the length of the shortest proof, in a fixed formal theory, that some machinery can stand in for the object's machine; its lower bounds are decidable and immune to search. In an abstract model of reproduction we show that both ingredients are necessary: no criterion computed from the observed run alone distinguishes a machine built from its description from one that is copied, and criteria that ignore the dynamical law attribute to the object information the law supplies. We also show that conditional Kolmogorov complexity is, up to logarithmic terms, the only effective notion of determination compatible with counting and with charging re-encodings by their description length. Finally, we show that separate weak dependence of a function on its arguments implies joint weak dependence only non-effectively, with a loss governed by the halting problem.

papers.title: Hidden Clues in WM-811K: Uncovering the Spatial Signals Behind Wafer Map Prediction
papers.abstract: WM-811K (also known as LSWMD) is a wafer map dataset first made publicly available in a 2015 paper by Wu et al. Convolutional neural networks have been used to achieve high classification accuracy on this dataset, yet it's not easy to decipher which features of the dataset are driving that performance. This study attempts to answer this specifically for WM-811K: how much of the predictive performance results from the wafer layout, the count of failed dies, their distance from the center and their exact 2-D location. After analyzing duplicate wafer maps, removing same wafer maps with conflicting labels and ensuring that the same manufacturing lot or exact same map doesn't appear in training, validation and test data, we were left with 25,513 defect-labeled wafer maps from eight classes. We then constructed four variations of each wafer map. The Original was the actual wafer map present in the dataset. The Layout-only kept only the layout of the non-background dies. The Global-shuffle kept the count of failed dies while shuffling them around. The Radial-shuffle randomized the locations of failed dies only in their radial bin, which was chosen out of 8 radial bins based on distance from the center. The data split, preprocessing and CNN architecture remained the same for all four of them. Macro-F1 progressed like this: 0.3829 (Layout-only), 0.5803 (Global-shuffle), 0.7439 (Radial-shuffle) and 0.8563 (Original). These results show that WM-811K contains useful information at several levels: wafer layout, number of failures, distribution of failed dies in a given radius, and exact 2-D locations of the failed dies. Therefore, high classification performance on this benchmark does not come only from learning the exact defect configuration.

papers.title: Black hole evaporation: From frontier physics to the classroom
papers.abstract: Half a century ago, Stephen Hawking discovered that black holes have a temperature, emit thermal radiation, and evaporate. Although Hawking temperature has been widely discussed in this journal, the evaporation process has received less attention. This work presents an accessible analysis of black hole evaporation, addressing the main questions raised by this phenomenon through intuitive ideas and heuristic calculations. It is shown that a problem situated at the frontier of physics can be reformulated in terms accessible for exploration in the classroom. In this sense, the article constitutes an educational resource that enables the integration of concepts from thermodynamics, relativity, and quantum mechanics within a meaningful learning context.

papers.title: Ramsey numbers of fixed-length cycles, paths and stars in set-colored triple systems
papers.abstract: Let $R_3(H;r,s,t)$ be the least order of a complete triple system in which every assignment of $s$ of $r$ colors to each triple forces a copy of $H$ whose edges share at least $t$ colors. Fix $r\ge s\ge t\ge1$ and let $n$ count edges. We prove that the Ramsey numbers of the linear path and the linear cycle of fixed length $n$ are both $γn+o(n)$ as $n\to\infty$, with $γ=2$ if and only if $r=s$. For tight paths the corresponding formula is $τn+o(n)$, with the same coefficient for tight cycles when $3\mid n$. To obtain exactly $n$ edges in a linear cycle, we choose the parity of the connections and vary the lengths of the paths they join. For a linear star $S_n$, whose edges meet only at the center, $R_3(S_n;r,s,t)=cn+O(n^{2/3})$ for fixed colors. For fixed $n\ge2$ and $s,t$ as $r\to\infty$, it is asymptotic to $\sqrt{6a_n\binom{r}{t}/\binom{s}{t}}$, where $a_n=n(n-1)$ for odd $n$ and $a_n=n(2n-3)/2$ for even $n$. For a tight star, whose edges share a pair, the leading term is $(n-1)\binom{r}{t}/\binom{s}{t}$ in both regimes. For a fixed linear path of $n\ge3$ edges and fixed $s\ge t\ge2$, the upper bound is $(2000h/1307+o(1))\binom{r}{t}/\binom{s}{t}$ as $r\to\infty$, where $h=\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$.

papers.title: Minor--Skein Spatial Negami Splitting Vectors and a Gluing Formula for Marked State Sums
papers.abstract: We organize the edge states of a decorated spatial graph by the minors of their underlying abstract graphs. For pieces with disjoint edge sets, Negami's component formula and functorial ribbon evaluation express each marked sector as a boundary pairing, provided the local data determine its marker. We give two explicit rules for this last step. A two-terminal rule for $3$-connected targets tests each piece with and without a virtual edge. At arbitrary finite vertex boundaries, records of partial branch sets determine the occurrence of each fixed simple target. The rules assign a weight once per edge state, even when the state contains several minor models.

papers.title: The $γ= 1/2$ Problem: A Unified Viability Criterion for f(R) Gravity in the Solar System
papers.abstract: A novel framework for addressing both the accelerated expansion of the cosmos and the inflationary epoch involves modifying the Einstein-Hilbert action through a function $f(R)$. While these $f(R)$ gravity theories can, under certain conditions, replicate phenomena described by scalar-tensor theories, this is only viable if the associated scalar field can operate within the Solar System without violating stringent observational constraints. A significant challenge is that within this theoretical equivalence, the post-Newtonian parameter $γ$ is fixed at $γ= 1/2$, a value that deviates substantially from the experimentally established result of $γ\approx 1$. Recent discussions have questioned the genuine equivalence between $f(R)$ gravity and scalar-tensor formulations. Furthermore, recent findings, independent of this equivalence, have demonstrated that the field equations for $1/R$ theory predict $γ= 1/2$ in a vacuum for spherical mass distributions. In this work, we extend these results to a broader class of $f(R)$ functions, aiming to delineate the specific conditions that lead to the prediction of $γ= 1/2$. This investigation provides a unified framework for identifying which classes of $f(R)$ gravity can satisfy Solar System constraints, deriving a general viability criterion that moves beyond previous case-by-case analyses. We derive a unified viability criterion that provides a necessary condition for any $f(R)$ theory to satisfy Solar System constraints, moving beyond case-by-case analyses toward a systematic classification framework.

papers.title: Constraints on Finsler cosmology from observational data
papers.abstract: We investigate current constraints and conditional detectability of Finslerian ΛCDM (FΛCDM) cosmology using supernova, cosmic chronometer (CC), and baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data. We adopt PantheonPlus SH0ES, CC and BAO data with a free acoustic scale. Supplementary tests with DES supernovae and PantheonPlus without SH0ES absolute calibra?tion verify result robustness. We compare FΛCDM model against ΛCDM and wCDM and find that FΛCDM improves the fit compared to ΛCDM, but the degree of fit is not superior to that of the wCDM model with the same number of parameters. We find that the background variations introduced by FΛCDM can be absorbed to some extent by ΛCDM through adjusting its own parameters. We then use parametric bootstrap calibration and Monte Carlo power estimation to assess the detection power of residual background deviation that ΛCDM cannot absorb. We find no statistically significant ev?idence for a residual background deviation in the main data configuration. For an injection background fixed at the maximum likelihood estimate, the conditional detection power is relatively low. We examine the sensitivity of the detection power of this signal to the injected background. We find that the detection power of this deviation is significantly dependent on the injection context.

papers.title: The Industrialization of Noise: Why Automated Proof-Solving is the Same Old Dead End
papers.abstract: Nearly fifty years ago, DeMillo, Lipton, and Perlis argued that mathematical proofs are not static, isolated structures of formal logic, but the products of a vibrant, evolving social process of human critique, internalization, and shared intuition. In October 2026, OpenAI challenged this thesis by releasing a massive repository of 722 automated mathematical manuscripts, claiming full or partial solutions to 372 longstanding open problems. This paper examines the immediate crisis through the lens of the original DLP framework. We argue that the sudden, automated overproduction of dense, unreadable proofs represents an industrial pollution of the mathematical ecosystem. By examining the three fatal structural pillars of this automated approach (Specification, Regress, and Utility), we demonstrate that decoupling the act of mechanical solving from the human social process of understanding produces a sterile repository of dead logical artifacts. The resulting industrialization of unexamined manuscripts is self-fulfilling. Flooding the literature guarantees that the finite supply of human attention will lose the race to separate signal from noise. In this sense, posting a result is not the same act as submitting it to the community processes by which mathematics is vetted, digested, and incorporated into shared knowledge.

papers.title: Reheating Constraints on the $α$-Starobinsky Model and Implications for Inflation Decays
papers.abstract: We constrain the $α$-Starobinsky model of inflation with an explicit reheating sector, in which the number of $e$-folds $N_*$ is computed for every sampled point from the reheating equation of state $w_{\mathrm{rh}}$ and temperature $T_{\mathrm{rh}}$, using a fully numerical pivot-scale matching in $\mathtt{CLASS}$. We analyze six combinations of Planck, Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) DR6 and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data. The CMB sees reheating only through $\ln R_{\rm rad}\simeq N_*-N_{\rm inst}$, the shift of $N_*$ from its instantaneous-reheating value. At $α=1$, Planck gives $n_s=0.9656^{+0.0015}_{-0.0017}$ and is consistent with instantaneous reheating, $\ln R_{\rm rad}=0.4\pm2.7$. Planck, ACT and DESI together (P-ACT+DESI) give $n_s=0.9689^{+0.0012}_{-0.0016}$ and $\ln R_{\rm rad}=6.5^{+2.5}_{-3.1}$, which prefers a stiff phase ($w_{\mathrm{rh}}>0.47$ at 95$\%$). With $α$ free they give $\log_{10}α=1.0^{+0.5}_{-0.8}$, $n_s=0.9706^{+0.0016}_{-0.0020}$ and $\ln R_{\rm rad}=6^{+3}_{-4}$. This preference is not in agreement with the bound on the primordial gravitational-wave contribution. Imposing that bound approximately removes about half of the preferred stiff region. Comparing to an otherwise identical analysis in which $N_*$ is a free parameter, we find that the reheating sector acts mainly as a prior on $N_*$: at $α=1$ it narrows the inflationary posteriors, and with $α$ free it removes the largest values of $N_*$ and doubles the preferred $r$ for P-ACT+DESI. Finally, we briefly discuss the connection between these phenomenological constraints and representative perturbative inflaton decay scenarios, highlighting the limitations of this interpretation for stiff reheating histories.

papers.title: Irreducible Governance Structure for Autonomous Agent Systems: Fair Allocation, Strategy-Proofness, and Multi-Scale Composition
papers.abstract: Autonomous agent governance is commonly framed as a problem of enforcing correct execution. However, in multi-agent systems, an equally fundamental question precedes execution: which agents are allowed to act. In this paper, we show that allocation is not an auxiliary concern but a structural component of governance. When multiple agents compete for execution under constrained resources, any allocation mechanism introduces unavoidable trade-offs between fairness, efficiency, and resistance to strategic manipulation. We formalize this through a set of impossibility results, including Sybil amplification and the incompatibility of desirable allocation properties. We then show that these allocation constraints cannot be resolved within a single layer of control. Instead, they propagate across the system, interacting with execution atomicity, state enforcement, and behavioral drift. This leads to a multi-scale governance structure composed of four orthogonal dimensions: temporal (atomicity), state (enforcement), behavioral (drift monitoring), and population (allocation). Our main result is an irreducibility theorem: under finite observability, no governance architecture can collapse these dimensions without loss of correctness or stability. Allocation, in particular, acts as a first-class constraint that prevents simplification of the governance stack. We validate these results through a series of analytical constructions and empirical ablations, showing that removing or approximating any layer leads to systematic failure modes. This work reframes agent governance as a structural problem: not only how actions are executed, but how access to execution is determined, and why these decisions impose irreducible architectural requirements.

papers.title: CPL dark energy: exact pressure-density relation and limits on cosmic acceleration
papers.abstract: The Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) parametrization, $w=w_0+w_a(1-a)$, is widely used to assess current indications of evolving dark energy. We ask what the parametrization itself imposes, independently of the data. First, we invert its pressure-density relation in closed form using the real branches of the Lambert $W$ function, and classify its positive-density histories with $w_a\ne0$ into six classes. Every history that crosses $w=-1$ reduces, in normalized variables, to one parameter-free curve, folded at a density extremum: the equation of state has two parameters, and the third only locates the present on the curve. No single-valued barotropic fluid follows the curve through the fold, so a crossing requires a continuation prescription. Second, we prove that a separately conserved, positive-density component accompanied by dust, radiation and collisionless massive species produces at most one accelerating epoch on a connected expanding branch, for any spatial curvature, if $w$ is nondecreasing and convex in $\ln a$, or nonincreasing; counterexamples delimit these hypotheses. For CPL with $w_a<0$, the case relevant to the DESI mean values, we give the exact dust-limit condition for an accelerating window to exist and an accurate approximation to its edges. At the DESI DR2 mean values the window is still open today for the three combinations that include supernovae, and closed at $z\simeq0.07$ for BAO+CMB alone. Conditional on $w_a<0$ and continued CPL evolution, any accelerating window is bounded; observations constrain its existence and location.

papers.title: CosmoMap: Predicting Hot Gas Temperature and Density from Dark Matter with a Conditioned 3D U-Net
papers.abstract: Mock X-ray observations of hot gas in galaxy groups, clusters and the cosmic web require its temperature and density over large volumes and many cosmologies, for which hydrodynamical simulations are expensive. We present CosmoMap, a 3D U-Net FiLM-conditioned on cosmological and feedback parameters that predicts gas temperature $T$ and electron density $n_{\rm e}$ from dark matter density and velocity. On the CAMELS IllustrisTNG Latin hypercube, CosmoMap reaches $R^2 = 0.765$ for $\log T$ and $0.934$ for $\log n_{\rm e}$ at $z=0$, reducing the error of gradient-boosted trees by 22-23 per cent. Temperature is predicted best in the densest regions, mostly galaxy- and group-scale haloes ($R^2 = 0.88$), but the electron density of the brightest X-ray-emitting gas is biased low by $0.12$ dex. One model outperforms the baselines at every redshift up to $z=2$, and using inputs from gravity-only simulations costs little accuracy. The predictions reproduce scaling relations, surface brightness profile shapes and most of the cosmological information in the gas. They produce box-integrated luminosities with a median bias of $-0.16$ dex, sensitive at the $0.2$ dex level to the inference scheme unless batch normalisation is used. Training for per-voxel uncertainties with a heteroscedastic likelihood costs accuracy and lowers luminosities by a further $0.1$-$0.3$ dex; the composite-loss variant, CosmoMap-$σ$, provides uncertainties that are calibrated at 68 per cent after rescaling by predicted emissivity, except for the density of the brightest gas. Compact structures are smoothed: mock X-ray lightcones recover 89 per cent of the brightest tenth of sources but 28 per cent of all sources.

papers.title: Strong-lensing tests of angular structure in the radial acceleration relation
papers.abstract: The radial acceleration relation (RAR) links the radial acceleration inferred from galaxy rotation curves to that predicted from the observed baryonic distribution. Whether it has a counterpart in the angular structure of gravitational fields remains unknown. We develop an observational framework to test for such a non radial correspondence using strong gravitational lenses, without assuming that a generalized RAR exists. The singular perturbative approach reconstructs two angular fields from lensed image morphology without imposing a parametric mass profile. We separate contributions from projected mass inside and outside the Einstein circle, normalize the inner baryonic and total fields, and define statistical comparisons of their radial and tangential components. We also derive higher order potential multipoles for a smooth elliptical, off centered projected halo and evaluate their dependence on NFW and Einasto profiles. The inner outer separation isolates the projected internal contribution most directly relevant to the RAR comparison. The inner dipole coefficients can be recovered without the source position contribution when both reconstructed fields are used. The quadrupole phase provides a measure of projected orientation, while the higher order moments quantify departures from a smooth elliptical profile. For the profiles and parameter ranges considered, the predicted higher order ratios remain small and vary only moderately with the Einstein radius to scale radius ratio. The framework provides a model independent observational test of whether a three dimensional non radial baryonic Total field correspondence leaves a statistical imprint after projection. The large strong lens population expected from Euclid could provide the sample needed for this test, subject to image quality, photometric, and selection function requirements.

papers.title: Mass equidistribution and fluctuations for random holomorphic sections of big line bundles with continuous metrics
papers.abstract: We study mass equidistribution and fluctuations of random holomorphic sections of big line bundles over compact complex manifolds, equipped with continuous Hermitian metrics and Bernstein-Markov measures. For arrays of centered coefficients that are independent and identically distributed within each row, we establish sharp moment conditions for mass equidistribution, covering a broad class of distributions, including Gaussian and certain discrete laws. On compact Kähler manifolds, we also show that mass equidistribution implies equidistribution of zeros under a natural condition on the equilibrium measure. We further establish central limit theorems beyond the Gaussian setting, show that fluctuations may depend on the choice of orthonormal basis, and determine their limiting variances for Haar-almost every sequence of bases.

papers.title: Gravitational-Wave Signatures of Compact Extra Dimensions and Their Detectability with Third-Generation Interferometers
papers.abstract: We investigate gravitational-wave dynamics in theories of gravity formulated in $D=4+N$ dimensions, with matter localized on a four-dimensional brane or coupled to the effective four-dimensional metric obtained after compactification. We consider four representative geometries, namely toroidal and Calabi--Yau compactifications, and the warped Randall--Sundrum I and II models, which cover the principal discrete and continuous Kaluza--Klein spectra. We derive the modifications of binary dynamics, propagation, quasinormal modes and polarization content, and use them as a feasibility screening for third-generation interferometers, with particular attention to the Einstein Telescope. The screening shows that the direct effects of the heavy Kaluza--Klein towers are strongly suppressed and are expected to be inaccessible to third-generation detectors. Indeed, the effective-field-theory corrections scale as $(\hbarω/m_1c^2)^2$$\sim$$10^{-23}$--$10^{-22}$, while the explicit conservative inspiral-phase correction of RS2 remains below the ET measurability threshold over the region allowed by laboratory bounds. Nevertheless, the screening identifies additional phenomenological channels that may remain testable: a tidal-charge deformation of the black-hole background, which shifts the QNM frequencies and damping times; a continuum-inspired phase deformation; and a radion-induced scalar polarization. We treat these channels as phenomenological benchmarks and formulate a Fisher-matrix Monte Carlo forecast based on the Earth-fixed geometry of the candidate sites, comparing the triangular and double-L Einstein Telescope configurations within an idealized common-noise setting.

papers.title: Easing H0 tension with Constrained Cosmological Parameters in f(R,Lm) Gravity
papers.abstract: We constrain two f(R,Lm) gravity models formulated through power-law and exponential curvature--matter couplings to evaluate their late-time dynamics and capacity to alleviate the H0 tension. Using MCMC sampling within the Cobaya framework, we confront both models against Cosmic Chronometer, Pantheon+ Type Ia Supernovae, and DESI-DR2 Baryon Acoustic Oscillation data under uniform and local SH0ES Gaussian H0 priors, benchmarking performance against flat Lambda_CDM via Delta_AIC, Delta_BIC, and Delta_DIC. In the unanchored joint analysis, both extensions are statistically favored over Lambda_ CDM (Delta_BIC = -6.60 and -2.91, respectively) and drive a smooth transition to late-time acceleration at z_t between 0.62-0.67 for the power-law model and z_t between 0.56-0.60 for the exponential model. Relative to the unanchored LambdaCDM constraint of H0 = 68.24 \pm 0.39\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} which is around $4.3σ$ tension with SH0ES, the power-law model yields $H0 = 67.00 \pm 1.04\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ ($4.1σ$), whereas the exponential model modestly elevates H0 to $69.46 \pm 0.70\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, easing the tension to $2.9σ$ without local calibration. Under the SH0ES prior, the power-law model exhibits dataset-dependent phantom excursions $q \to -1.21$, $ω_{\mathrm{eff}} \to -1.14$ in $CC+H0$ and incurs a strong Bayesian penalty in the full joint fit Delta_BIC = +7.42. Conversely, the exponential model maintains strict quintessence-like stability, converging smoothly to the de Sitter attractor ($q \to -1$, $ω_{\mathrm{eff}} \to -1$) while reducing the SH0ES discrepancy to $1.8σ$ ($H0 = 70.60 \pm 0.86\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$) with positive Akaike support (Delta_AIC = -4.29) and only a mild Bayesian complexity penalty (Delta_BIC = +1.17).

papers.title: LLM Genetic Feature Engineering
papers.abstract: Feature Engineering is the (traditionally manual) process of constructing derived variables from an existing dataset by combining, transforming, or otherwise manipulating the original data fields to reduce statistical noise and extract meaningful, domain-specific quantities of interest from the raw dataset. Recent work demonstrates promising progress toward the au tomation of this process through the integration of large language models (LLMs) and various metaheuristics to guide the search for useful features. We build on this approach by introducing a novel genetic algorithm that implements selection, crossover, and mutation at the individual feature level, rather than at the level of the entire engineered feature set. In doing so, we enable in-process statistical analysis of newly-generated features, thereby enabling the genetic algorithm to simultaneously integrate individual and group-level feature metrics into its selec tion process. We demonstrate this capability using state-of-the-art feature importance metrics, and show that this approach yields superior predictive performance while driving meaningful improvements in feature relevance, algorithm robustness, and overall model interpretability.

papers.title: Lexical Tone and Word Order Matter in Translation: Prosodic Correspondence Across Languages
papers.abstract: Prosody conveys emphasis, emotion, and intent, yet its correspondence across translation remains underexplored, especially when languages differ in lexical tone and word order. To our knowledge, we present the first systematic word-level analysis of prosodic correspondence in translated speech spanning tonal and non-tonal Asian languages, with comparisons to European-language findings and explicit analyses of lexical tone and word reordering. Building on prior evidence of fine-grained prosody correspondence in European-language pairs, we investigate how these linguistic factors relate to word-level pitch and energy correspondence between English and five languages: Mandarin Chinese, Thai, and Vietnamese, which have lexical tone, and Japanese and Korean as additional comparisons. Correspondence is generally lower than previously reported European-language estimates. Adjusting for lexical tone increases pitch correspondence for English-Mandarin Chinese, English-Thai, and English-Vietnamese. However, English-Japanese and English-Korean also exhibit lower correspondence than the European-language estimates, indicating that tonal status alone does not explain the observed pattern. Greater word reordering is associated with weaker local correspondence even under semantic alignment, suggesting that semantic alignment does not fully account for differences in prosodic organization. These findings characterize the limits of fine-grained acoustic correspondence across translation and motivate prosody modeling that accounts for lexical pitch constraints and the structural context of translated content.

papers.title: Agentic Optimization: LLM Agents Select and Configure Algorithms for Engineering Design
papers.abstract: Engineers solving new multi-objective design problems commonly commit to a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA) before seeing a result. The best MOEA differs from benchmark to benchmark. We propose agentic optimization, placing an LLM agent outside the optimization loop, where it reads a natural-language problem description to configure and launch algorithms, drawing on parametric knowledge rather than on a performance history that a novel problem lacks. We compare five LLMs in a fixed harness on four engineering benchmarks and a real-world SARS-CoV-2 molecular docking task, using hypervolume (HV) and IGD+ with multiple comparison-corrected tests. Three models (GPT, DeepSeek, Qwen) dominate every baseline on combined HV and IGD+, and each is significantly better than the best baseline on at least one benchmark, sometimes by applying the same baseline algorithm they surpass, showing the importance of both algorithm configuration and selection. Agent behavior is strongly model-dependent, but even the weakest agents dominate three of the four baselines overall.

papers.title: GeoCANO: A Geometry-Conditioned Adaptive Neural Operator for Physical-Field Prediction on Varying Domains
papers.abstract: Industrial design requires repeated evaluation of candidate configurations. Integral performance measures alone do not resolve critical local phenomena, while high-fidelity simulation remains costly. Existing physical-field surrogates often couple geometry representation and coordinate evaluation through prescribed mesh topologies, limiting reuse across resolutions. We propose the Geometry-Conditioned Adaptive Neural Operator (GeoCANO), which maps a sampled complete three-dimensional geometry to a coordinate-dependent field function. An attention-based encoder extracts a geometry state from unordered surface coordinates. A multiresolution axis-factorized hash encoding and query-wise sparse mixture-of-experts decoder enhance multiscale expressiveness. GeoCANO constructs the field representation before introducing output coordinates, allowing one geometry encoding to be reused across regions without rebuilding the graph for each output topology. We evaluated GeoCANO on transonic aerodynamic-field prediction over complete aircraft configurations using a Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes dataset of 10,484 wing-body-nacelle geometries. For unseen configurations within the sampled design family, GeoCANO outperformed baselines in complete-surface prediction, high-gradient pressure reconstruction, and pressure-drag recovery. It reduced pressure-coefficient mean absolute error by 77.9% relative to the strongest baseline and retained an advantage over a finite range of wall-normal distances. Ablation studies showed that geometry-modulated coordinate encoding achieved comparable accuracy with substantially fewer parameters than conventional three-dimensional hash encoding. Routing analysis indicated spatially structured, query-dependent expert specialization. These results demonstrate a reusable continuous-coordinate representation for rapid physical-field evaluation over varying geometries.

papers.title: Magnetar driven Dainotti relation with up to 56\% reduced uncertainties: probing the Expansion History of the Universe
papers.abstract: The persistent tension in Hubble constant measurements and recent DESI hints of dynamical dark energy motivate extending the distance ladder beyond Type~Ia supernovae (SNe~Ia) and Cosmic Chronometers (CC) into the largely unexplored range $z\sim2$--$6$. We use X-ray plateau emission of long gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), standardized through the two-dimensional Dainotti relation, as a probe of this gap. We analyze two samples: a platinum sample (P50, 50~GRBs, light-curve quality cuts) and a magnetar sample (M23, 23~GRBs, selected by requiring the magnetar spin-down model to be statistically preferred over the Willingale parametrization). We calibrate the Dainotti relation anchored independently to the Master SNe~Ia compilation and to Cosmic Chronometers, and propagate the result into a joint flat-$Λ$CDM inference via MCMC. Despite containing less than half the GRBs of P50, M23 yields an intrinsic scatter $\sim41\%$ smaller, demonstrating that physically motivated selection outperforms quality cuts. Both samples give nearly identical cosmological constraints once combined with SNe~Ia and CC: M23 gives $H_0=69.45\pm0.32\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $Ω_m=0.34^{+0.01}_{-0.02}$; P50 gives $H_0=69.46\pm0.33$ and $Ω_m=0.34\pm0.02$, both in $3$--$3.5σ$ tension with Planck and SH0ES. We further introduce a novel joint likelihood that simultaneously fits individual plateau light curves and the Dainotti correlation, reducing the intrinsic scatter by $\sim56\%$ relative to the platinum sample and avoiding local maxima from sparse light-curve data. These results establish magnetar-selected GRB plateaus as a robust, high-redshift complement to existing distance-ladder probes, with a clear path toward improved constraining efficiency as sample sizes grow.

papers.title: In-in formalism & $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-product: no contribution from total time derivatives
papers.abstract: In the in-in formalism, total time derivatives are sometimes argued to contribute nontrivially to inflationary correlators at the evaluation point, i.e., at the end of inflation. In this paper, we disprove this claim based on the path integral. After formulating the canonical quantization and the regulated path integral of systems with total time derivatives, we derive the $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-ordering, the correct operator ordering on the closed time path. In the $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-ordering, the evaluation point, or the turning point of the in-in contour, is merely an intermediate point and is never an endpoint of the generalized path integral contour. As a result, any apparent boundary contributions at the turning point of the forward and backward branches completely cancel out. We demonstrate this cancellation by re-analyzing examples in the literature, with an emphasis on contact terms associated with the $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-ordering overlooked previously.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Is Not Explainability
papers.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) allows language models to verbalise multi-step rationales before producing their final answer. While this technique often boosts task performance and offers an impression of transparency into the model's reasoning, this position paper argues that rationales generated by current CoT techniques can be misleading and are neither necessary nor sufficient for trustworthy interpretability. We analyse faithfulness as whether CoTs are not only human-interpretable but also reflect the model's underlying reasoning well enough to support responsible use. By synthesising evidence from prior work, we systematically show that verbalised chains are frequently unfaithful, diverging from the critical hidden computations that drive a model's predictions. As CoT is increasingly relied upon in application domains, including high-stakes ones such as medicine, law, and autonomous systems, we further argue that this unfaithfulness is not taken seriously enough in these settings: our analysis of 1,000 recent CoT-centric papers finds that approximately 21.7% explicitly treat CoT as a load-bearing interpretability technique, building pipelines or safety arguments that would not hold if CoT is unfaithful to the model's actual reasoning. They include papers in high-stakes domains that heavily hinge on such interpretability claims. Building on prior work, we make three proposals: (i) avoid treating CoT as being sufficient for interpretability without additional verification, (ii) adopt rigorous methods that assess faithfulness for downstream decision-making, and (iii) report such assessments alongside any interpretability claims based on CoT, while continuing to use CoT for its communicative and monitoring benefits.

papers.title: Reliability-Aware and Anatomy-Preserving Replay for Continual Echocardiographic Segmentation
papers.abstract: Continual echocardiographic segmentation remains challenging due to catastrophic forgetting, domain shifts, and heterogeneous anatomical supervision. Existing continual-learning methods often struggle to preserve previously acquired knowledge while adapting to new imaging distributions, particularly under limited replay memory and incomplete anatomical annotations. To address these challenges, we propose the Reliability-Aware Replay Network (RAR-Net), a continual segmentation framework integrating multi-factor exemplar prioritization, protected task-aware memory, forgetting-conditioned adaptive replay, and structure-aware supervision. RAR-Net combines class, boundary, image, anatomical, and temporal reliability criteria to prioritize informative historical examples, while adaptive replay regulates their contribution during sequential training. Structure-aware supervision further reinforces previously learned anatomical knowledge when subsequent datasets provide incomplete annotations. Extensive experiments performed on CAMUS, CardiacNet, and EchoNet-Dynamic demonstrate that our RAR-Net achieves the highest final average accuracy among the evaluated continual-learning methods, with competitive historical knowledge retention and segmentation performance approaching the offline joint-training reference. These findings indicate that coordinating reliability-guided memory management, forgetting-conditioned replay, and anatomy-specific supervision can support knowledge retention and adaptation under the evaluated sequence of heterogeneous echocardiographic datasets.

papers.title: Reliability of Language-Model Judges for Quantitative Scientific Question Answering: Evidence from Perovskite Photovoltaics
papers.abstract: Evaluating retrieval-augmented language models increasingly relies on automated model judges, yet their reliability on quantitative scientific synthesis remains largely unmeasured. Here, we evaluate automated grading on a quantitative benchmark for perovskite photovoltaics, where all 755 ground-truth answers are deterministically computed from 45,441 experimental device records. We evaluate a frontier judge (Claude Opus 5.5) alongside two local open-weight judges (Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-8B) across 4,530 free-text answers from six retrieval architectures under three regimes: reference-augmented (with the computed key), evidence-augmented (with retrieved passages and query logs), and unassisted (question and answer alone). Equipped with the reference key, Claude Opus reproduces ground truth near-perfectly (Cohen's $κ= 0.982 \pm 0.003$) and preserves exact architectural rankings ($τ= 1.00$). Withholding the reference causes evaluation fidelity to collapse: frontier agreement drops to $κ= 0.557 \pm 0.022$, and providing retrieved literature passages yields virtually no improvement ($κ= 0.576 \pm 0.024$). Without reference keys, local judges degrade to near-random agreement ($κ= 0.087$ and $0.112$), inverting the leaderboard to rank a hallucinating closed-book baseline first ($τ\le 0.20$). Furthermore, SQL-augmented generations induce severe evaluative blind spots: absent a reference, the frontier judge accepts 46.6% of erroneous SQL answers, overestimating architecture accuracy as 66.4% against its true 52.6%. These findings demonstrate that model-based evaluation in the physical sciences cannot rely on unstructured text inspection; rigorous benchmarking requires reference ground truth precomputed from structured measurement records.

papers.title: AhaPro: A Process-level Rebus benchmark for probing Aha moments in LLM reasoning
papers.abstract: Existing research on Aha moments in large language models has largely focused on reflective expressions or final revision outcomes, leaving their role in the visible reasoning process insufficiently characterized. Rebus puzzles encode answers through character forms, spatial arrangements, and homophony. Reinterpreting key details may trigger Aha moments and shifts in the reasoning process and candidate answers. We introduce AhaPro, a process-level benchmark that uses rebus puzzles to examine how models reorganize evidence and revise answers through Aha moments. The framework represents CoT as sequences of candidate answers, evidence, and verification states, using hierarchical metrics to assess conflict detection, state improvement, and subsequent adoption. Across eleven models, we observe frequent failures to adopt better states discovered during Aha moments, alongside adopted revisions that leave state quality unchanged or reduce it. Models also detect conflicts without subsequently achieving an effective revision. Further paired interventions suggest that prior reasoning context may hinder effective revision after conflict detection, while multi-branch search highlights answer selection as a bottleneck between correct-answer discovery and successful correction.

papers.title: ToneMamaba: Learning Contextualized Tonal Contours with Boundary-Reset State Space Models
papers.abstract: Mandarin tone recognition in connected speech is challenging because contextual and durational variation reshapes F0 contours. We propose ToneMamba, a boundary-aware state space model that replaces static boundary embeddings with bidirectional state resets at syllable, word, and IPU levels. Fixed weights fuse multi-level representations, while shared-weight bidirectional scans use channel-wise directional fusion to reduce parameters. Dynamic syllable pooling forms tonal contours, and rhythm-conditioned gating incorporates durational information. ToneMamba achieves 97.9% and 74.8% accuracy on FCU-VOICE-360 read and MCDC-8 conversational speech, outperforming the baseline (ToneNet) by 0.9 and 15.9 percentage points, respectively. Ablations show that word-level resets are particularly effective, while rhythm conditioning provides greater gains in conversational speech, underscoring the role of durational variation in spontaneous speech.

papers.title: Agentic Systems Need Multi-Run Evaluation: A Study of Retrieval and Response Variability in a Deployed Enterprise RAG System
papers.abstract: Previous RAG systems have mostly been evaluated in a single-run setting, and with the advent of agentic RAG, systems are still often evaluated the same way. However, agentic RAG systems introduce a source of run-to-run variability, since several of their components make decisions non-deterministically. Such systems typically comprise a retrieval stage followed by a generation stage, and the retrieval stage in particular can behave differently across runs. For example, the agent might issue a different number of parallel searches from one run to the next, which alters the retrieved documents and therefore the final answer. In this paper we study this behavior in a deployed agentic RAG system for product-documentation questions, running each of 739 questions ten times and analyzing the execution traces to find where different runs first diverge. We find a substantial gap between success in any run and success in every run: the retrieval hit rate is 69.4% when the correct page is found in at least one run, but 50.9% when it must be found in all ten. Responses also stay similar in meaning while varying in wording, with an average BERTScore of 0.90 and a BLEU of 0.49. Trace-level analysis shows that retrieval is the largest source of divergence (43.9%), and the number of parallel searches at the first retrieval step alone accounts for 20.1% of divergent pairs. Taken together, these results show that single-run evaluation can hide reliability and consistency issues in agentic RAG systems, and that multi-run evaluation is necessary to reveal them.

papers.title: SD-Cache: Learnable Memory Consolidation with State-Guided Dynamic Caching
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as persistent services that must reason over large volumes of external knowledge. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds model responses in relevant documents, but the retrieved content must still be encoded and stored in the key-value (KV) cache. As this content accumulates, the cache grows linearly, increasing memory consumption and inference cost. Existing memory-compression methods address this problem either by retaining a subset of cached states or by learning context compressors that map documents to compact latent representations. Despite these advances, consolidating information under tight memory budgets while preserving its usefulness for future queries remains challenging. We investigate how the model's native KV states can be selectively consolidated into a fixed-size working memory without access to future queries. To this end, we introduce SD-Cache (State-guided and Dynamically updated Cache), a query-agnostic KV-memory consolidation framework that operates alongside a frozen generator LLM. SD-Cache learns to consolidate layer-wise KV states into fixed-size memory through selective anchor-based pooling and state-guided refinement, processing new contexts in a single forward pass without context-specific optimisation. Experiments on retrieval-augmented question answering and synthetic long-context benchmarks show that SD-Cache maintains competitive downstream performance under constrained memory budgets.

papers.title: How Persona Conditioning Changes Open-Ended Task Execution: A Paired Evaluation of Behavioral Gains and Reliability Costs
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are often prompted with role- or persona-based instructions, yet persona conditioning has mainly been evaluated through character fidelity or aggregate benchmark accuracy. We study persona conditioning as a task-execution steering signal that changes how models interpret, structure, and sustain responses. Using paired instances derived from real user role-play logs and expanded into simulated multi-turn continuations, we compare with-persona and no-persona conditions while fixing task content, constraints, user simulation, and evaluation criteria. Across eight models, persona conditioning improves expert content depth and procedural fidelity, and these gains survive length control. At the same time, it lowers strict instruction-following accuracy by 17 to 30 points in every model evaluated, and increases unsupported real-world specificity through persona-induced elaboration. These results suggest that persona prompting is not a general-purpose performance improvement technique, but a selective task-execution policy shift with both behavioral gains and reliability risks.

papers.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Iranian Doctoral Entrance Exams in Electrical and Computer Engineering
papers.abstract: We evaluate four large language models (LLMs) on multiple-choice questions from the 2024 and 2025 Iranian national Ph.D. entrance examinations in Electrical Engineering (EE) and Computer Engineering (CE). Of the 440 questions in the four official booklets, 7 were excluded because the question statement or its figure was ambiguous, leaving 433 questions (186 EE, 247 CE), of which 171 (39.5\%) depend on a figure. Each question was presented in the original Persian and in an English translation, giving 3,464 scored responses. GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Grok 4 were queried zero-shot, with reasoning enabled, through a single commercial web interface (Perplexity) in October 2025, using an automated script. Because every model answers the same items, all inferences use paired tests or question-clustered models. Accuracy separates into two tiers: GPT-5 (79.9\%, 95\% CI 76.6--83.1) and Gemini 2.5 Pro (78.4\%, 74.8--81.9) are statistically indistinguishable, and both outperform Grok 4 (71.7\%) and Claude Sonnet 4.5 (71.3\%) by 6.7--8.7 percentage points (Holm-adjusted $p < 0.001$). The English--Persian accuracy difference is small for every model ($-0.2$ to $+2.5$ points; exact McNemar $p \ge 0.28$). For three models the 90\% confidence interval lies within $\pm 5$ points, so differences larger than this can be excluded. Questions with figures are much harder: the odds ratio is 0.30 (95\% CI 0.21--0.43) after adjusting for discipline. The apparent EE deficit of two models disappears once the larger share of figure-based EE items is accounted for. We describe the dataset, the protocol and its limitations, including the uncontrolled web-retrieval and decoding settings of the interface, and release item-level responses and analysis code.

papers.title: RegioZH: Unveiling Comprehension Disparities across Regional Chinese Varieties in LLMs
papers.abstract: Current evaluations often treat Chinese varieties as monolithic, obscuring failures for regional users. We introduce RegioZH, a 2,607-item multiple-choice benchmark for regional lexical reasoning across Mainland China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Malaysia. Built by region-specific annotators and expert-validated, it targets localized idioms, slang, code-mixing, politeness conventions, and sociocultural expressions. Zero-shot results on eleven LLMs show large disparities, including a 29.4-point average accuracy gap between Taiwan and Singapore. Persona and structured chain-of-thought prompts for five models yield selective gains, suggesting that some errors stem from retrieval or framing rather than only missing knowledge. Representation, attention, calibration, and surface-feature analyses show a dissociation between marker attention and semantic grounding, overconfident forced-choice errors, and localized lexical density as a consistent difficulty predictor. Qualitative analysis finds terminology misunderstandings, sociocultural inference gaps, and cross-regional semantic divergence. RegioZH demonstrates that apparent Chinese proficiency can mask uneven understanding across regional varieties, motivating intra-language robustness evaluation alongside multilingual generalization.

papers.title: Does Item Response Theory Generalize Across Languages? Evidence from Cross-Lingual LLM Benchmarks
papers.abstract: The application of Item Response Theory (IRT) for data selection in benchmarks has mostly been limited to monolingual settings. In this work, we ask: how does IRT generalize when the same benchmark is translated across languages? We conduct experiments on Multilingual GSM and Global MMLU, covering over 100 language models and 11 languages. Fitting 1PL, 2PL, and 3PL IRT models per language, we assess cross-lingual consistency of parameters and whether IRT-filtered subsets preserve model rankings across languages: item difficulty emerges as the most stable parameter followed by guessing and then discrimination. A differential item analysis also shows that lack of stability can be tracked to specific items shifting under translation across languages. Our findings suggest IRT-based selection in multilingual settings must be both parameter-aware and item-aware, validating model choice and screening individual items before assuming cross-lingual generalization.

papers.title: Capability and Interpretability of Transformers on Multi-task Recurrence
papers.abstract: Transformers are widely used in various language tasks, with limited understanding of their internal mechanisms. Motivated by the recurrent structure of many linguistic rules, we study the capability and interpretability of Transformers through a controlled family of linear recurrence tasks over finite cyclic groups. These tasks range from executing a single fixed rule to identifying a latent rule from context and switching between explicitly specified rules, with and without input masking. Through extensive experiments across different configurations, we find that switching specified rules is simpler than identifying latent rules for Transformers in general. We also identify how several key factors affect the generalization capability of Transformers, including the depth, width, and the algebraic structure of the linear recurrence. Curriculum training is extremely useful when the number of rules is large. With standard tools in mechanistic interpretability like linear probing and input patching, our study reveals how Transformers represent, identify, and execute multiple rules.

papers.title: RecipeADQA: A User-aware Question-Answering Dataset for Multi-Constraint Recipe Recommendation
papers.abstract: Question-answering recipe recommendation tasks lack datasets with ground-truth labels. Existing methods often generate datasets from simple combinations of ingredient or tag constraints, leading to unnatural expressions and unreasonable constraints that are hard to reflect users' real preferences. This paper proposes a construction method for a benchmark-style QA dataset for natural-language recipe recommendation. Driven by real user behavior, our method integrates external user query and review data to extract fine-grained preference signals by LLMs and maps them onto a knowledge-graph-based tag schema, thereby constructing QA data consisting of preference and ingredient constraints. Besides, a greedy strategy for constraint selection is also used to control the answer size, while tag-based re-ranking is applied to improve data quality. The generated dataset RecipeADQA contains natural-language questions, structured constraints, and answer sets, resulting in 128,465 instances. Experiments compare RecipeADQA with baseline datasets from two perspectives: data quality and retrieval-recommendation performance. The results show that ours outperforms existing methods on the same recipe knowledge graph in coverage, higher question quality in naturalness and constraint rationality, and better queryability. Moreover, we design a noise-augmented retrieve-and-rerank model, in which a lightweight parser first retrieves candidate recipes, and a small language model then selects and ranks relevant recipes from a noisy candidate pool. The model trained on RecipeADQA outperforms the same model trained on the baseline datasets. The relevant construction code and data have been open-sourced at a GitHub repository https://github.com/MorimoLab/RecipeADQA.

papers.title: RECAP: Training Long-horizon LLM Agents with Context Compaction
papers.abstract: Context compaction enables large language model agents to tackle long-horizon tasks within limited context budgets by replacing interaction histories with compressed summaries. However, learning effective compaction jointly with the agent policy remains challenging, as summaries affect task success over many subsequent interactions. We introduce RECAP, a reinforcement learning (RL) framework based on the principle that a summary should preserve the behavior induced by the original interaction history. We formalize this principle with a behavior distortion objective that measures the divergence between the agent's subsequent behavior under compressed and original contexts. We show that the gradient of the distortion objective decomposes into two complementary learning signals: distortion-based reward for summary generation and self-distillation for subsequent actions. Experiments on Qwen3.5-4B show that RECAP consistently outperforms the task-reward-only RL baselines on both environments, leading to an absolute improvement of 4.6% and 4.3% on BrowseComp-plus and SWE-bench Verified, respectively. Ablations further highlight the value of jointly supervising summary generation and post-compaction behavior for RECAP.

papers.title: scOPD: Routed On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM-Based Single-Cell Annotation
papers.abstract: Motivation: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for single-cell annotation, but existing training methods mainly rely on scalar outcome rewards that provide limited supervision for intermediate biological reasoning. Batch-level annotation is particularly challenging because it requires jointly resolving local cell identities and a global one-to-one matching constraint, such that one local error can affect the entire assignment. Moreover, a single inference pass provides insufficient evidence for locating uncertain predictions. These limitations call for fine-grained reasoning supervision during training and uncertainty-aware refinement during inference. Results: To address these challenges, we propose scOPD, an on-policy self-distillation framework for LLM-based single-cell annotation. After reasoning fine-tuning, scOPD adaptively routes qualified rollouts to reward-based optimization, while erroneous rollouts receive privileged token-level supervision from successful sibling trajectories. During inference, rollout disagreement triggers constraint-aware pairwise refinement of uncertain assignments. Across CellPuzzles and four out-of-domain disease datasets, scOPD consistently improves the performance of diverse LLM backbones, achieving average cell-level and batch-level accuracies of 81.71% and 44.49% with Qwen3-8B. Availability and Implementation: Code and data are available at https://github.com/YuZhiyin/scOPD.

papers.title: Directly Maximizing On-policy Expected Accepted Length for Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by using a lightweight draft model to propose tokens for verification by a target model. Draft training commonly optimizes token-level distribution alignment, but this does not directly optimize the length of the accepted prefix: once a draft token is rejected, all subsequent draft tokens are discarded. We propose FreDraft, an on-policy training method that directly maximizes the expected accepted length of drafts sampled from the current draft model. This objective accounts for first-rejection truncation and induces prefix-aware credit assignment, weighting each token by its contribution to the acceptance of the current and subsequent tokens. To optimize the objective efficiently, we analytically marginalize token-level acceptance rate, using the target model's vocabulary distribution to reduce gradient variance. We further redistribute part of this distribution-level gradient into an explicit penalty for sampled tokens whose probabilities are overestimated by the draft model, while preserving the expected gradient. Experiments across multiple benchmarks and target models show that FreDraft improves accepted length and decoding speedup over strong baselines, achieving faster on-policy training convergence.

papers.title: INCLUDE-2.0: Disentangling Knowledge Gaps in Multilingual LLM Evaluation
papers.abstract: Current multilingual benchmarks cover only a fraction of the languages represented in modern pretraining corpora and often conflate language proficiency with the ability to answer questions grounded in specific regions and communities. We introduce INCLUDE-2.0, a large-scale benchmark for region-aware multilingual factual evaluation, which covers 91 languages from 86 countries (127 total language--country pairs), comprising over 220K curated samples drawn from native regional sources. Unlike existing benchmarks that often treat language as a proxy for region, IINCLUDE-2.0 distinguishes between questions whose answers are independent of context, vary by country, concern widely documented facts about a place, or depend on knowledge primarily expressed through local linguistic and cultural sources. Each item is annotated with its regional knowledge type and domain, and paired with an English translation, enabling controlled analysis of the relationship between language proficiency and possession of regional knowledge. Evaluating frontier and open-weight models on IINCLUDE-2.0, we find that aggregate multilingual accuracy masks substantial variation across regional knowledge types, languages, and regions. We find that frontier models perform worse on locally embedded knowledge than on widely documented facts about regions, with an average drop of ~14.5 points. We also show that for open-weight models, scale improves accuracy but does not reliably make performance invariant to whether a question is asked in English or its original language. INCLUDE-2.0 is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/epfl-nlp/include-2.0

papers.title: The Date You Didn't Set: The System-Prompt Date as a Hidden Variable in LLM Evaluation
papers.abstract: The system prompt of many instruction-tuned models carries a date, usually today's, filled in automatically for conversational and agentic requests alike, so an unchanged evaluation can send a different prompt each day. In this paper, we explore how much this hidden input changes evaluation outcomes. Across six instruction-tuned models and four benchmarks, with prompts, decoding, and configuration fixed, every model is affected: two plausible dates (2024--2026) switch a median $6.6\%$ of test items between correct and incorrect. Even rerunning the evaluation one day later flips about as many items as changing the batch size, although nothing in the setup was changed. In addition, using a grammar-constrained variant of Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) to search dates of any year, we find dates that cost the Llama-3.x models up to $36.5$ points of held-out accuracy.
