We then investigate splitting phenomena: specifically, removing a family of holes concentrating at a zero-capacity compact set (lying outside a closed set of measure zero) causes a multiple eigenbranch to split into branches of smaller multiplicity. Finally, for holes concentrating at a point, we prove that the largest eigenbranch generically detaches from the rest and becomes simple.

papers.title: From Learning Rates to Rotational Schedules: Finite-Horizon Theory on the Sphere
papers.abstract: How should step sizes be scheduled across a finite training horizon? Cosine and warmup-stable-decay (WSD) schedules are widely adopted in large-scale pretraining, yet their effect on optimization also depends on parameter norms. Normalization can make parameter groups scale invariant, so that the loss depends only on their direction, while their norms still affect how fast the parameters rotate. In this work, we formulate schedule design directly in the space of rotational motion. Working within a geodesically convex spherical setting, we derive a last-iterate convergence guarantee for arbitrary rotational schedules that separates their overall scale from their distribution over time. We derive the unique schedule that minimizes this bound and prove that it approaches linear decay as the horizon grows. Empirically, our rotational interpretation and idealized spherical analysis provide useful predictions for LLM pretraining in practice, including schedule comparisons missed by existing analyses. Our analysis predicts schedule ordering across model scales for both vanilla (Adam, Muon) and Hyperball-style (AdamH, MuonH) optimizers. Our Hyperball experiments support the predicted strong performance of linear LR decay and confirm our prediction that WSD underperforms in this setting. Accounting for parameter norm dynamics, we predict instead the strong performance of WSD for Adam and Muon shown in practice. Guided by our theoretical insights, we also derive a new LR schedule for Adam and Muon, which improves over the established cosine and WSD schedules. All in all, these results support the use of rotational dynamics to understand, predict, and ultimately guide scheduling in LLM pretraining.

papers.title: Single-Coordinate Activation Steering for Controllable Social Stance in Language Models
papers.abstract: Steering one neuron of a small language model can impose a topic or a quirk without training, yet replications show that many published single-neuron recipes are fragile or nonspecific. This paper asks whether an interpersonal stance can be controlled in this manner. The stance studied is a distant crush, a chatbot character that is guarded, intermittently warm and inconsistent. In Qwen3.5, 4B, contrasting activations on hand-written guarded and eager replies identified neuron 7515 of layer 9 as a candidate for controlling this stance. Increasing this neuron activation made the characters replies more distant. Three language models rated this change as stronger than the effects of changing randomly selected neurons, and a blind human comparison supported the finding. Changing the interventions direction between messages also shifted replies between warmer and more distant styles. This suggests that a language model conversational stance can be personalized without finetuning.

papers.title: LM2 Compiling a Language Model into Another Model Weights
papers.abstract: Deploying a conversational model and a specialist together could avoid maintaining a separate specialist service. We present LM2, which embeds a trained story generator into a larger conversational model. The larger model handles the conversation and invokes the generator for story requests. We constrain the generator arithmetic during training so its calculations can be compiled directly into added model layers. We compare this approach with QwenPU, which executes the stories260K language model on an embedded processor. LM2 requires one host token per generated character, compared with approximately 25,000 for QwenPU. However, its story generator predicts held out text less well, i.e. 1.145 bits per character versus 0.894 for stories260K, where lower is better. The Qwen3.5, 0.8B implementation occupies 18.1 GB and generates the same characters as a standalone integer implementation of the inner model in the tested runs. These results illustrate a tradeoff between host-token cost and text-prediction performance.

papers.title: Political Orientation and Participation in Prediction Markets: Large Stakes Converge, Small Stakes Diverge
papers.abstract: Prediction markets offer a way to study collective expectations and beliefs: people express their views on various events and, by putting money behind their predictions, take on the risks of their judgments. As a result, the scale of investment can reveal additional dimensions of individual behavior and beliefs. In this study, we use a complex network approach to examine the structure of user participation, drawing on roughly 1.14 billion transaction records from the Polymarket platform, covering more than 3.1 million wallet addresses and 764,000 prediction events. To do this, we build a bipartite network of users and events and analyze patterns of investment concentration, connections between topics, and the network's community structure. Our findings show a highly skewed distribution of financial participation: 1\% of events account for 64\% of total transaction volume, while 1\% of wallets account for 79.2\% of total financial participation. We also examine how investment scale and political orientation shape user participation patterns. Focusing on the 2024 U.S. presidential election, we compare users who invested exclusively in a Trump victory or exclusively in a Harris victory, grouping wallets by purchase size rather than by retail or institutional status. The results show that among large-scale investors, capital allocation patterns across topics are more similar between the two political groups; in contrast, these patterns diverge more and vary more among small-scale investors. This result holds across six different ways of representing and comparing the networks, and four of these differences are also statistically supported.

papers.title: Small-time global exact controllability of nonlinear Schrödinger equations on the circle with bilinear controls
papers.abstract: We study nonlinear Schrödinger equations on the circle with nonlinearity $κ|ψ|^{2p}ψ$, a fixed smooth real potential $V$, and bilinear controls. Using only the three control potentials $\mathbf 1,\cos x,\sin x$, we prove global approximate controllability in $H^s$ on the unit sphere of $L^2$ for all integers $s,p\ge1$, every $κ\in\mathbb R$, and any prescribed positive time. The proof combines two ingredients: the approximate controllability between nowhere vanishing states from our companion paper, and a new mechanism that steers any nonzero initial state to a nowhere vanishing state in arbitrarily small time. When $V=0$ and the nonlinearity is defocusing or sufficiently weakly focusing, adding two explicit control potentials of finite regularity gives local exact controllability in $H^2$ near the constant state, via a moment problem and the inverse mapping theorem. Together, these results imply global exact controllability in $H^2$ on the unit sphere of $L^2$, at any prescribed positive time, with five control potentials. To~the best of our knowledge, this is the first global exact controllability result for a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with finitely many bilinear controls.

papers.title: MagPot: A magnetoelastic potential generator for molecular dynamics simulations
papers.abstract: Magnetoelastic phenomena originate from the coupling between atomic displacements and magnetic degrees of freedom, and their atomistic simulation requires interatomic models in which magnetic interactions depend explicitly on interatomic distance. This paper presents MagPot, a Python program that generates Bethe-Slater parameter sets for spin-lattice molecular dynamics simulations using the SPIN package of the Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator (LAMMPS). From a compact set of material properties, the program determines the radial functions describing Heisenberg exchange and the dipole and quadrupole contributions of the two-ion Néel interaction. Version 1.0 supports simple-cubic, body-centred-cubic and face-centred-cubic lattices with ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic configurations. A central feature of MagPot is its modular architecture, which allows the magnetic contribution it generates to be combined additively with a broad range of compatible non-magnetic interatomic potentials. The parameterisation workflow is assessed through equation-of-state, Curie-temperature, volume-magnetostriction, pressure-dependent magnetocrystalline-anisotropy and anisotropic-magnetoelastic tests. By automating the construction of the magnetic contribution to the interatomic model, MagPot offers a straightforward and reproducible route from material properties to LAMMPS-ready magnetic interactions, facilitating large-scale atomistic simulations of magnetoelasticity and magnetostriction, as well as physical phenomena associated with magnon-phonon coupling.

papers.title: Radial Evolution of Correlation Anisotropy in PUNCH Observations of the Young Solar Wind
papers.abstract: Solar wind turbulence, evolving in the presence of a mean magnetic field, large-scale shear, and expansion, exhibits several types of anisotropy, including wavevector anisotropy and variance anisotropy. As the solar wind expands from the corona into the interplanetary space, the magnetically controlled outer corona transitions into the dynamic and less constrained solar wind, and fluctuations may evolve toward isotropy. This is suggestive of an evolution of anisotropy with distance from the Sun, a feature observed in earlier results using surveys of in-situ data, as well as more limited images of solar wind density from STEREO. Here we confirm and expand on those results employing data from the PUNCH mission, whose wide-field, high-cadence imaging enables anisotropy tracking at different heliospheric positions. We evaluate a two-dimensional (2D) correlation function $C(\ell_{\perp}, \ell_{\parallel})$ of polarized white-light brightness as a function of radial $\ell_\parallel$ and transverse $\ell_\perp$ scales to infer the nature of density anisotropy and its development in space. At larger heliocentric distances ($\sim 100 R_\odot$), circular contours of the correlation function indicate a transition toward approximate isotropy. The correlation structure at heliocentric distances from $30R_\odot$ to $60R_\odot$ preferentially extends along the radial direction, which might imply the possible dominance of the two-dimensional variation in the transverse plane. In this way, the very large field of view of PUNCH images reveal a fundamental transition of solar wind turbulence toward isotropy.

papers.title: Symplectizing stable generalized complex four-manifolds
papers.abstract: We explicitly describe a surgery that turns a stable generalized complex four-manifold into a symplectic four-manifold. As a consequence, we show that for $n\geq 2$, the almost complex manifold $(n^2+n+1)S^1\times S^3\#\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$ admits no stable generalized complex structures or constant type generalized complex structures. We also prove an irreducibility result for stable generalized complex four-manifolds and we show that the moduli space of generalized complex structures on an elliptic surface has infinitely many components.

papers.title: Non unitary and nonlinear quantum generative large model design and fast large-scale training without back propagation
papers.abstract: Transformer-based large models require huge computational and storage costs. Quantum computation is expected to address that due to its potential to speed up classical algorithms exponentially. Key challenges of implementing quantum large models include the linear, unitary nature of qubit evolutions contrast with the non-unitary matrices and nonlinear functions in classical Transformers, as well as the difficulty of implementing gradient back-propagation on quantum hardware. Here we propose a fully quantum large model containing all the Transformer layers, implementing the non-unitary transformations through SVD-decomposition-based quantum circuits, and approximated nonlinear activation functions through pre-trained parameterized quantum circuits. We also propose a quantum circuit training algorithm based on multi-agent Reinforcement Learning, which can train large-scale parameterized quantum circuits without back-propagation. The dependency between the inference time complexity and the model's hidden dimension has been reduced from polynomial to logarithmic, showing an exponential advantage. The inference executions on the quantum hardware verify our model's 300-1000 times speed-up, and the measurements on the sequence-to-sequence tasks shows its learning ability. The training algorithm achieves only 25% complexity of the best SOTA quantum circuit training algorithms, especially this ratio decreases fast as the parameter scale increases. Our work not only proposes a quantum large model that can significantly reduce the computational cost, but also promotes the quantum computation towards general computing.

papers.title: Finite-temperature quark dynamics in proto-neutron stars: Maximum baryonic mass and radial oscillations
papers.abstract: Finite-temperature quark dynamics can significantly alter proto-neutron star evolution even when the cold equation of state remains unchanged. We quantify this sensitivity by comparing a purely hadronic baseline with two hybrid models incorporating quark matter via the Polyakov-Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (PNJL) framework and its entanglement extension (EPNJL), which isolates the role of finite-temperature chiral-deconfinement coupling. Employing bulk Gibbs constructions for both nuclear liquid-gas and hadron-quark phase coexistence, we compute equilibrium configurations across hot neutrino-trapped, hot neutrino-free, and cold stages, alongside linear radial oscillations of selected hot neutrino-free stars. Introducing quarks lowers the maximum baryonic mass at every stage and reverses its evolutionary ordering: whereas the maximum baryonic mass increases toward the cold limit in the purely hadronic model, it decreases progressively in both hybrid models, opening mass windows for delayed collapse. Crucially, despite sharing the same cold limit, PNJL and EPNJL yield distinct baryonic-mass intervals for mixed-core survival across stages: only EPNJL permits configurations that retain mixed cores across both hot stages, whereas only PNJL allows hot neutrino-free mixed-core stars to possess cold equilibrium counterparts. All tested hot neutrino-free mixed-core stars remain linearly stable, yet their fundamental radial frequencies differ substantially. These findings demonstrate that finite-temperature quark dynamics imprints distinct evolutionary constraints and pulsation signatures on proto-neutron stars beyond cold-matter descriptions.

papers.title: Approximate controllability in Sobolev spaces of periodic nonlinear Schrödinger equations with bilinear controls
papers.abstract: We consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the torus $\T^d$ with a smooth real-valued potential and nonlinearity $κ|ψ|^{2p}ψ$, where the dimension $d\ge1$, the integer $p\ge1$, and the coefficient $κ\in\R$ are arbitrary. The controls act bilinearly through finitely many low Fourier modes. For every integer $s>d/2$, we prove approximate controllability in $H^s$ between any two nowhere vanishing states on the unit sphere in $L^2$ at any prescribed positive time. The proof combines small-time phase control, a transport approximation in $H^s$, and a construction of short uncontrolled trajectories connecting states with different winding vectors.

papers.title: Quadruples of integers whose elementary symmetric functions are perfect squares
papers.abstract: While Euler had considered the problem of finding three integers whose elementary symmetric functions are all squares, an extension of the problem to four integers has not been discussed in the mathematical literature till now. In this paper, we describe a method of generating infinitely many quadruples of positive integers whose elementary symmetric functions are all squares.

papers.title: Bayesian Calibration of Computer Experiments and Extrapolation
papers.abstract: Calibration, a fundamental inverse problem in uncertainty quantification, suffers from model identifiability issues. While the discrepancy decomposition model partially addresses this via a first-order Taylor expansion, it struggles when the approximation is biased. We propose a Bayesian modified discrepancy decomposition model that incorporates a residual process to capture higher-order discrepancy structures. By jointly inferring calibration parameters and model discrepancies within a Bayesian framework, our model recovers more physically meaningful parameters and provides reliable uncertainty quantification. Crucially, this accurate parameter recovery enables reliable extrapolative prediction, a challenge current methods largely fail to address. We validate the approach through numerical studies and a real-world industrial application: predicting the thermal stability of multilayer mirrors in extreme ultraviolet lithography. In this application, our method accurately predicts high-temperature responses far beyond the training domain, significantly outperforming existing calibration methods.

papers.title: Think Before You Forecast: Scaling Test-Time Compute for Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Test-time compute has become an important paradigm in computer vision and language modeling, where additional computation at inference time enables models to explore multiple candidate solutions and select or refine the most reliable one. However, time series forecasting models typically produce predictions through a single forward pass, leaving them vulnerable to distribution shifts and non-stationarity that frequently arise in real-world temporal data. We propose Time Test Compute for Time Series (TTC4TS), an architecture-agnostic framework that improves the predictive performance of frozen forecasting models at inference time. Given a pretrained backbone, the generator produces multiple candidate forecast trajectories using augmentation, retrieval, adapter. The synthesizer then selects or combines these candidates using aggregation, classification, or candidate-scoring and ranking methods to produce the final forecast. By increasing the number of candidates, TTC4TS scales test-time compute without retraining the forecasting backbone. Beyond improving point-forecast accuracy, TTC4TS can exploit candidate forecasts for uncertainty quantification, which supports improved interval forecasts. We also theoretically analyze when additional test-time computation improves forecasting. Experiments across diverse datasets and backbones demonstrate consistent gains in accuracy and calibration. Code is provided in https://github.com/Anoise/TTC4TS.

papers.title: Marked INAR model and the rough Hawkes--Heston limit
papers.abstract: We develop a discrete-time Monte Carlo algorithm for the rough Hawkes-Heston model based on a nearly unstable marked integer-valued autoregressive (INAR) process. We implement the algorithm with a block fast Fourier transform (FFT) scheme that evaluates the excitation convolution in $O(N\log^2 N)$ operations per path on an $N$-bin grid. We prove joint convergence in law of the spot variance, log price and common marked point measure to their rough Hawkes-Heston limits. We prove convergence of European call and put option prices, as well as convergence of arithmetic Asian and down-and-out put option prices to their continuously monitored values. For European options, the one-year implied volatility smiles computed from the grid transform approach the continuous affine reference across four roughness levels. Monte Carlo experiments on the same three grids compare arithmetic Asian and down-and-out put option prices with a finer-grid reference and demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm.

papers.title: A shock-fitting approach to high-order simulation of viscous hypersonic flows based on inviscid implicit shock tracking
papers.abstract: This work presents a framework for computing viscous, shock-dominated flows at high Mach and Reynolds numbers in which the bow shock is located by inviscid implicit shock tracking and then treated as a boundary of the viscous computation. The high-order implicit shock tracking (HOIST) method is applied to the Euler equations on a coarse, shock-agnostic mesh to produce a shock-aligned mesh and the shock geometry; the elements upstream of the shock are discarded, the post-shock domain is remeshed to resolve the boundary layer, and the compressible Navier-Stokes equations are solved on it with a high-order interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method, with the post-shock state prescribed along the shock boundary by the oblique shock relations. Because the shock structure is never resolved, the approach requires neither the extreme element compression nor the specialized formulations that fully coupled viscous shock tracking demands at these conditions; the tracking optimization is confined to the coarse inviscid mesh, and the viscous computation involves no mesh unknowns and no additional nonlinear stabilization. The framework is demonstrated on a Mach 10.6 axisymmetric blunt cone, a Mach 17.6 cylinder, and a Mach 5 sphere in three dimensions, with surface pressure and heat flux in good agreement with experimental measurements and reference computations.

papers.title: Ballistic propagation-mediated super-resolution light-element imaging: in-situ tracking dynamic hydrogen migration
papers.abstract: Transmission electrons - with few-picometer wavelengths - can theoretically resolve all atoms in solids. However, constrained by factors such as lens aberrations, Z-contrast dependence and poor temporal resolution, the scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) fails to tackle the long-standing challenge of hydrogen dynamics on atomic scale. Here, our experiment-guided simulations reveal that unlike heavy-atom imaging - governed by wave-based imaging process - ballistic propagation of particle-like electrons in Cs-corrected TEM enables super-resolution imaging (SRI) of light atoms, achieving a resolution down to 14 pm and a robust hydrogen contrast of ~24%. Our in-situ SRI study not only uncovers polymetric hydrogen aggregation in TiHx and H-LaAlO3, but also inter-site migration, rotational displacement of hydrogen species and collective hydrogen tunneling-induced polarization surge in the oxide. By exploiting the novel electron-matter interactions, our findings offer an unparalleled approach to probe hydrogen dynamics and establish accurate structure-property relationships in diverse functional materials.

papers.title: Hessian type equations with gradient source term and measure data
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of nonnegative solutions to $F_k[-u]=|Du|^q\,dx+tμ$ for some $t>0$, where $μ$ is a finite nonnegative measure on $\mathbb{R}^N$. We consider the whole space $\mathbb{R}^N$ with $2\leq k<\frac{N}{2}$ and $q>\frac{Nk}{N-k}$, and a bounded domain $Ω$ with $2\leq k<N$ and $q>k$. We also establish pointwise gradient estimates in terms of the Wolff potential.

papers.title: High order tangencies, paratangencies, and universal dynamics
papers.abstract: Our research focuses on studying the dynamics in the Newhouse domain $\mathcal N(L)$ -- open regions in the space of $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of a $d$-dimensional manifold $\mathcal M^d$ ($r=1,\ldots,\infty,ω$ and $d\ge 2$) where homoclinic tangencies to a saddle periodic orbit $L$ are persistent. We prove that diffeomorphisms with infinitely many corank-1 homoclinic tangencies of all orders are dense in such regions. If $L$ is a bi-focus, we reveal novel bifurcations in $\mathcal N(L)$ showing density of diffeomorphisms with infinitely many corank-2 homoclinic tangencies of all orders. These results entail genericity of one- or two-dimensional universal dynamics in $\mathcal N(L)$ (depending on the type of $L$). Moreover, we characterize the geometric complexity of the bifurcation sets corresponding to homoclinic tangencies. We prove that parametric families with paratangencies of arbitrarily high orders are dense in the space of parametric families intersecting $\mathcal N(L)$. If $r\le\infty$ and $L$ is sectionally dissipative, this implies density of families possessing infinitely many coexisting stable periodic orbits for some open set of parameter values.

papers.title: Discovery of Two Hyperluminous Infrared Galaxies at $z\sim6$
papers.abstract: Hyperluminous infrared galaxies (HyLIRGs) at cosmic dawn are key to understanding the formation of the first massive galaxies. We report the spectroscopic confirmation of two unlensed HyLIRGs at $z\sim6$ in the COSMOS field, AzTECC63 and S2COS-84, originally selected from single-dish AzTEC and SCUBA-2 surveys. Using ALMA and NOEMA observations, we robustly detected CO and [CII] lines in both galaxies and unambiguously confirmed their redshifts to be $z=6.092$ and $z=5.90$, respectively. Panchromatic SED fitting reveals dust-obscured star formation rates of $\approx1000$ and $\approx2300\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, ranking them among the most intensely star-forming systems known at $z \gtrsim 6$. High-resolution ALMA observations reveal an extremely compact morphology for S2COS-84, with a dust-continuum effective radius of $\approx0.3$ kpc, implying a star-formation rate surface density above the Eddington limit. The far-infrared SEDs of both galaxies, together with the compact size of S2COS-84, indicate warm dust ($T_{\rm dust} \approx 80$ K) that is likely optically thick at far-infrared wavelengths. Both galaxies exhibit an extreme [CII] deficit, with $L_{\rm [C\,II]}/L_{\rm IR} \approx 10^{-3.7}$, an order of magnitude below that of normal star-forming galaxies. Their molecular gas masses, derived consistently from both [C\,{\sc ii}] and dust, together with their IR-derived SFRs imply short gas depletion times of $\approx$40--60 Myr, making them plausible progenitors of the earliest massive quiescent galaxies found at $z\sim5$.

papers.title: A detailed verification of Neary's PCP(5) construction
papers.abstract: Neary proved that the Post correspondence problem remains undecidable for instances with five pairs of words. We give a detailed verification of his construction. We first verify the undecidability of the restricted binary tag-system halting problem used in the reduction. We then prove both directions of the reduction to the five-pair problem, using the longer closing pair proposed by Rote. In particular, we show that every solution of the constructed PCP instance yields a halting computation of the simulated tag system.

papers.title: Action Windows Are Inherently Temporal: A Benchmark for Time-Sensitive Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Vision-language model (VLM) agents have surpassed learned-policy baselines on existing robotic manipulation benchmarks. However, these agents still struggle with time-sensitive everyday tasks that existing benchmarks for VLM agents cover only partially. In these tasks, evolving physical processes create finite windows for successful intervention. These action windows are inherently temporal and impose a shared time budget on decision making and physical execution. Coordinating intervention within this budget requires agents to determine when the window opens. We introduce AWAIT, a simulation benchmark that evaluates task completion within action windows while accounting for decision and execution time. Our evaluation reveals difficulties in recognizing window onset and shows that successive decisions and movements can exhaust an action window even when each decision takes less than the window duration. Project page: https://eyja42.github.io/await-site/.

papers.title: S$2$SCORE: A Textless Unified Evaluation Metric for Speech-to-Speech Translation Systems
papers.abstract: Evaluating speech-to-speech translation (S$2$ST) systems requires assessing multiple dimensions of translated speech, including semantic adequacy, speaker similarity, and acoustic naturalness. Existing approaches are largely text-based, relying on ASR transcripts and primarily assessing semantic adequacy, while other dimensions require separate metrics. We propose S$2$SCORE, a unified text-free evaluation framework that jointly models these dimensions within a multi-task architecture and produces a human-calibrated overall quality score. S$2$SCORE is trained using supervision derived from established evaluation models, enabling scalable learning without direct human annotations. Evaluated across five language pairs, S$2$SCORE shows strong agreement with human judgments, independent reference metrics, and the training supervision metrics, indicating robust generalization. The reference-free variant, S$2$SCORE-QE, consistently outperforms S$2$SCORE-REF and achieves stronger semantic adequacy prediction than BLASER~$2.0$.

papers.title: Differentiable collision-model control for multipartite state engineering: reachability, geometry, and preparation cost
papers.abstract: We study a differentiable control architecture for multipartite state engineering in which partial-SWAP collisions, a Heisenberg exchange, are interleaved with layers of local phase rotations. Singular collision angles confine the evolution to invariant supports, impose exact fidelity ceilings, and generate an inverse-distance lower bound on the preparation time nearby. Away from them, numerical certificates show that the sampled couplings reach the whole fixed-excitation sector for sector dimensions up to 21, and optimizations reach fidelities above 0.999 for dimensions up to 1716. At generic couplings the number of rounds needed for a given Dicke fidelity, measured by the ratio of independent phase controls to the projective dimension, is nearly independent of the system size, and the quantum Fisher information spectrum is close to that of a random Gaussian Jacobian. Near full SWAP, a slow-time theory, the sharp form of the inverse-distance bound there, predicts microscopic hitting times without fitted parameters: the distance from the singular point sets the clock and its direction selects the effective control geometry. A detuning sweep along two rays shows that the Dicke horizon follows this law up to a detuning of 0.1, where it is two to five times shorter than at a generic coupling in sectors of dimension 70 to 252, while phase-uniform, random-sign, and Haar-random targets are delayed; beyond a detuning of about 0.3 all targets return to the generic cost. The slow-time value for the Dicke target is nearly the same for sector dimensions from 35 to 252. The exchange graph of the effective theory offers an interpretation of this ordering. Counted in two-qubit gates, generic-coupling preparation is costlier than known Dicke circuits; the architecture offers fixed global couplings, local phase rotations as the only control, and no measurement.

papers.title: Learning Acceptable Lotteries via Queries: Minimizing Aggregated Violation Distances
papers.abstract: When deploying an AI system, a developer can randomize over several candidate versions, sending each request to a version chosen at random, to balance the requirements of multiple stakeholders. We study a setting in which each of $n$ stakeholders reveals only whether a proposed lottery over $m$ candidates is acceptable, and each stakeholder's acceptable lotteries lie on one side of an unknown hyperplane. While previous work sought a lottery that every stakeholder accepts, such a lottery need not exist when, for instance, safety and helpfulness requirements are in conflict. We therefore minimize a power mean of the stakeholders' violations; since binary answers reveal neither the size of a violation nor how to compare violations across stakeholders, we measure each violation by a normalized distance to the stakeholder's acceptance boundary. We characterize exactly when accept/reject answers determine these distances. When they do, $\mathcal{O}(nm\log(1/\varepsilon))$ queries suffice to learn them, where $\varepsilon$ is the precision of the utilities, and this bound is tight; when they do not, a natural worst-case approach is optimal up to a constant factor, even compared with methods that make unlimited queries. For limited query budgets, we give a sampling algorithm whose number of queries for a given accuracy does not depend on $n$, and show that a deterministic algorithm cannot guarantee a small loss without querying almost all stakeholders. Synthetic experiments illustrate the resulting tradeoff between querying many stakeholders and learning each of them accurately.

papers.title: On the uniformity of definably amenable radicals and dfg-fsg decompositions in $p$-adically closed fields
papers.abstract: For definable families of groups over $p$-adically closed fields, we show that the definably amenable radicals and their dfg-fsg decompositions can be defined uniformly as the prime $p$ and the family parameters vary.

papers.title: Detecting Is Not Choosing: What a World Model Needs to Keep a VLA Policy Safe
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies complete most benchmark tasks but often violate safety constraints. Since they are stochastic, one remedy is to sample several candidate action chunks and execute one that a world model predicts is safe. We ask what such a model must do. In simulation, a lookahead safety filter with the simulator as an exact world model raises the safety rate of three VLA policies on LIBERO and of pi0.5 on LIBERO-Plus by 11.5 to 25.7 points. It also helps pi0.5 on three RoboCasa tasks. Learned critics trained on one policy's data detect dangerous states (pooled AUROC up to 0.864) but rank candidates at one state close to chance (within-decision AUROC 0.551-0.560), and the learned dynamics and video models we test do no better. When the simulator's state is perturbed, selection degrades long before detection. In the loop, a median position error of 3.18 mm removes 70% of the gain on LIBERO-Spatial, partly because the error also corrupts the displacement check. On LIBERO-10 the loss is smaller, and the intervals overlap. The median does not predict the cost: a pixel reader with a 0.56 mm median error keeps 6.5 points less of the gain than Gaussian error of a similar median. A world model for safety should thus be judged by within-state ranking, and its state must be accurate in the tail and on handled objects, not only in the median.

papers.title: Gated Payoff-Weighted Net Profit Maximization For Online Portfolio Selection With Transaction Costs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study online portfolio selection (OLPS) problems. The net profit maximization (NPM) acting upon Adaptive Online Moving Average (AOLMA), namely the AOLNPM strategy in portfolio selection, trades when forecast gain exceeds the transaction cost. In essence, this method relies heavily on calibrated forecasts. Indeed, we show that AOLMA forecasts overstate the realized relative returns. We therefore design a gate that adjusts how strongly an AOLMA forecast is used; for each asset, it learns the recent mixture proportion assigned to AOLMA from predictive likelihoods against a neutral forecast (no change). The proportion therefore estimates the extent to which the forecast is realized. We then feed the resulting forecast into the NPM portfolio rule, where the gate acts as an asset-specific cost threshold. A payoff-weighted fund combines gated NPM experts with fixed decay factors in proportion to their wealth and needs no learning rate. On nine datasets with a transaction cost rate of 0.1%, our method produces 5.9 times the wealth of AOLNPM in geometric mean and sits above AOLNPM on every dataset, with its preponderance growing with the cost rate.

papers.title: Inspect Before You Decide: Evidence-Guided Visual Search for Industrial Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable potential for industrial anomaly detection and understanding. However, reliably identifying subtle anomalies remains challenging, as existing approaches often struggle to acquire and verify fine-grained visual evidence beyond global observations. To address this challenge, we propose EVAD, an evidence-guided visual search framework that enables MLLMs to actively seek and examine diagnostically informative visual evidence for reliable anomaly reasoning. Specifically, EVAD begins with a global visual assessment to identify potentially anomalous regions for further inspection. Building upon this observation, we introduce a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-guided exploration strategy that progressively acquires visual evidence through two complementary operations: semantic refinement for fine-grained inspection and spatial expansion for contextual verification. The acquired evidence is subsequently evaluated and integrated to support more informed and reliable anomaly decisions. Extensive experiments across multiple industrial anomaly detection tasks demonstrate that EVAD achieves state-of-the-art performance in most evaluated settings, highlighting the effectiveness of active evidence exploration for fine-grained anomaly understanding and reasoning. The code will be publicly available upon publication.

papers.title: Global topology and symmetry breaking in an indefinite superlinear Dirichlet problem
papers.abstract: Motivated by the work of Fencl and López-Gómez [13] on global bifurcation diagrams, we study the connected components of positive solutions of $-u''=λu+a(x)u^p$ on $(-1,1)$ with $u(-1)=u(1)=0$, where $a$ changes sign and $p\ge2$ is an integer. For generic $\mathcal C^r$ weights, $r\ge2$, with $n$ positive intervals, simple zeros and negative endpoint values, we obtain at least $2^{n-1}$ noncompact components. Apart from the principal component, each is a curve with both ends at $λ=-\infty$. The proof distinguishes at least $2^n-1$ ends and yields bounds for branching and compactly supported cohomology. For even weights, an odd Morse index of at least $k$ on the principal symmetric component forces at least $k$ symmetry-breaking points. In particular, symmetry breaking occurs if $a(0)<0$.

papers.title: CompareDR: Benchmarking Deep Research Reports from Individual Quality to Comparative Merit
papers.abstract: Deep research systems can produce reports with different evidence, analyses, and conclusions for the same query. A reader deciding which findings to rely on needs to know how well each report meets the task requirements and which differences matter to the answer. A score for a single report can summarize its quality, but it does not identify which contributions make one report more useful than another. We introduce CompareDR, a benchmark that combines task-specific pointwise audits with guideline-based pairwise comparisons. We use passage-linked report representations to locate relevant differences and selective evidence verification to check claims that could affect the judgment. The benchmark comprises 40 Chinese and English tasks from three existing benchmarks, 360 reports from nine systems, 1,099 human-reviewed evaluation criteria, and human preferences elicited through blinded comparisons of 80 report pairs. The hybrid evaluator matches 69 of these 80 preferences (86.25%, Cohen's $κ=0.746$). The benchmark supports both comparisons of research systems and examination of the evidence and analyses behind those judgments.

papers.title: Real-Time Kinodynamic Multi-Agent Motion Planning
papers.abstract: Coordinating large robot fleets, from warehouses to quadrotor swarms, requires collision-free trajectories that satisfy dynamic constraints and stay within speed and acceleration bounds. Existing kinodynamic multi-agent planners enforce these bounds during the search or through trajectory optimization after it, which limits fleet size and speed. We present Tickwise Actions to Kinodynamic Trajectories (TAKT), a framework that accounts for the dynamics before the search and reduces planning to a lattice search for double-integrator robots. TAKT analytically bounds the clearance lost when a discrete plan is smoothed and reserves this margin on the lattice. A closed-form convolution provably converts any valid plan into dynamically feasible trajectories with continuous-time collision avoidance. For robots spanning many lattice vertices, we introduce a diamond formulation that permits one-tick sideways yielding and adapt the Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) solvers PIBT and LaCAM to it. With 50 robots, our planners run over 2,000 times faster than the strongest baseline in 2D halls and over 100 times in 3D, with comparable or lower makespan and cost. They plan about a thousand robots in seconds in 2D, and tens of seconds in 3D, and replan up to a thousand robots in real time.

papers.title: Align the Pair, Not the Sample: Representation Alignment for Faster and Better One-Step Generato
papers.abstract: Representation alignment markedly accelerates diffusion training, but one-step generators raise a question that diffusion does not: \emph{which training path should receive the loss?} A one-step generator sees two kinds of inputs. Corrupted real images come with their clean counterpart, which provides an instance-paired target. Samples generated from pure noise have no corresponding real image, yet this is where the final model operates. We study this question on Priming, which trains one-step generators from scratch by reconstructing corrupted images and then matching feature distributions with optimal transport. Aligning the generative path, the natural choice, collapses recall ($0.45\!\to\!0.15$--$0.25$) in all 17 configurations we test, including five target constructions and loss weights down to $0.05$. Aligning the paired reconstruction path with a frozen DINOv2 encoder instead helps in every setting we test. A short analysis explains this asymmetry: when the target carries no instance information about the input, the optimal aligned feature is constant within each class, so the loss pulls samples toward class prototypes. A control confirms this: aligning the paired path to a random same-class image instead of the input's own image removes most of the gain. Inside the generator, paired-path alignment creates an interface block through which post-training routes noise, and the image semantics carried through it predict sample quality across 16 models. The resulting recipe, \method, accelerates \emph{both} training stages on ImageNet $256\!\times\!256$: it matches the 160-epoch baseline with $2\times$ fewer priming epochs, surpasses its final quality with $4\times$ fewer post-training updates, and lowers FID to 1.30 (B) and 1.155 (L) at the standard budget. A joint single-stage variant trains native one-step generators and reaches FID 1.22 with 115M parameters.

papers.title: ParseGap: Testing What Coding Agents Authorize and What Shells Execute
papers.abstract: LLM coding agents authorize shell commands by parsing a command string against a policy and passing the raw string to a system shell, so the gate adjudicates one reading while the shell executes another. We present ParseGap, a differential testing framework that runs each command through an unmodified vendor checker and GNU Bash 5.2 in an isolated container, flagging a violation whenever an approved command produces policy-violating runtime effects. Across eight production coding agents, ParseGap identifies 17 root causes across three divergence boundaries: at the parse, where an upstream tree-sitter-bash defect hides a second command from Mistral Vibe and Gemini CLI; at the utility, where every checker permits read-only binaries whose arguments write files or launch programs (9-47 of 55 cases); and at confinement, where an allow rule in OpenAI Codex CLI disables its read-only OS sandbox. Live trials across two frontier models triggered policy violations in all 16 agent-model pairs (14 under configured restrictions). To eliminate the second reading, we design ShellPlan, which compiles a strict Bash subset once into a typed execution plan, validates utility arguments against positive capability specifications, and dispatches approved plans directly via execve without a shell. Over a formal operational model, we prove single-interpretation dispatch and bound touched programs and files under audited assumptions. ShellPlan admitted 0/4,174 active attacks across six static suites and 0/90 hits in a ten-model agent benchmark (62/90 unguarded) at 1.28 ms median gate latency, preserving 36/36 (100%) frontier standard-dev completion (74/100 overall) and 0/348 external over-allows outside modeled exceptions.

papers.title: SCRA-CLIP: Spherical-Contextual Representation Adaptation for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Recent advances in vision-language models have facilitated zero-shot anomaly detection (ZSAD) through transferable visual-semantic representations. However, detecting fine-grained anomalies remains challenging due to inadequate modeling of diverse anomaly patterns and their spatial context. To address these challenges, we propose SCRA-CLIP, a Spherical-Contextual Representation Adaptation framework that jointly enhances anomaly-aware textual semantics and context-sensitive visual representations. Specifically, we introduce Spherical Prototype-Conditioned Prompting (SPCP), which employs von Mises--Fisher mixtures to model the directional distributions of normal and abnormal patch features. These state-specific prototypes are incorporated into textual contexts to guide the learning of more discriminative textual representations. Furthermore, we develop Context-Deviation Guided Visual Adaptation (CGVA), which captures local feature deviations relative to multi-scale neighborhood contexts and refines patch representations through adaptive gating. By integrating distribution-aware semantic modeling with context-sensitive visual adaptation, SCRA-CLIP facilitates more discriminative cross-modal matching for fine-grained anomaly detection and localization. Extensive experiments on 11 industrial and medical benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization capability of SCRA-CLIP across diverse unseen categories and domains. The code will be publicly available upon publication.

papers.title: Comparing the $K$-theory of two versions of $\ell^p$-Roe algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that for any locally finite metric space $X$ and $1<p<\infty$, the canonical inclusion from the $\ell^p$-Roe algebra with coefficient space $\ell^p(\mathbb N)$ into that with coefficient space $\ell^p(\mathbb N;\ell^2(\mathbb N))$ identifies the former with a full multiplier corner of the latter. Consequently, the inclusion induces an isomorphism on $K$-theory, answering a question of Wang, Xie, Yu, and Zhu. Moreover, at the endpoint $p=1$, we show that the two corresponding Roe algebras are not Morita equivalent whenever $X$ is infinite.

papers.title: $μ$- and $q$-extension of special functions in quantum field theory
papers.abstract: Analytic calculations up to single-scale quantities in perturbative quantum field theory result into special numbers and functions, which are generalizations as iterative integrals over special alphabets. In this way one obtains polylogarithms, Nielsen integrals, the iterated integrals over linear denominator terms, cyclotomic letters, letters induced by quadratic forms, and square-root valued letters. The inverse Mellin transform relates special nested sums to these quantities, which are harmonic sums, generalized harmonic sums, nested sums implied by quadratic forms, cyclotomic harmonic sums, and nested sums containing central binomials. We construct the $μ$- and $q$-extensions of all these special functions. They are expected to occur in loop calculations within $μ$- and $q$-extended quantum field theories via modified (anti)commutation relations. The $μ$-extended special functions are quite different form the corresponding $q$-extended functions. While in the former case one observes class-preservation characterized by the polynomial $μ$-parameter, except for the case of root-valued letters. In the latter case new higher transcendental functions are obtained.

papers.title: Seeing vs. Knowing: Counterfactual Supervision and Correction for 3D-Aware Object Editing
papers.abstract: Rotating, translating, or rescaling an object in a photograph requires revealing unseen surfaces, preserving visible appearance, and updating shadows and reflections. Reconstructed 3D assets, rendered at the target pose as a 3D state, provide explicit geometric guidance, but their imperfect textures may conflict with the photograph, while standard paired training does not explicitly teach the editor which source to trust. To address this, we propose counterfactual state supervision, which constructs controlled photo--state conflicts through hidden-surface repainting, hidden geometry with re-rendered shadows and reflections, and visible-surface texture replacement. This teaches the editor to follow the 3D state for unseen content while preserving photograph-visible appearance. However, learning this distinction does not ensure that it is maintained during sampling. We therefore introduce symmetric counterfactual correction, which uses state-side and photo-side twins, which share the photograph and the state respectively, to construct directed latent perturbations toward condition-inconsistent targets and train recovery toward the target specified by the current condition. Both strategies operate only during training, requiring no architectural changes or additional inference steps. Experiments on OBJect and SpatialEdit-Bench demonstrate strong spatial editing performance and content preservation, while controlled ablations show improved source selection and sustained responsiveness to conditioning during sampling.

papers.title: Rank-two twists of the Fermat cubic with $3$-primary Tate--Shafarevich group $(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})^{2m}$
papers.abstract: For each integer $m\ge0$ we construct infinitely many positive squarefree integers $k$ for which the Fermat cubic $E_k\colon x^3+y^3=k$ has Mordell--Weil rank two over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\unicode{x0428}(E_k/\mathbb{Q})[3^\infty]\simeq(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})^{2m}$. Fixing $2m$ prime divisors of $k$ congruent to $-1$ modulo nine, with product $D$, we obtain $\gg_D X^{1/3}/(\log X)^6$ distinct parameters up to $X$. Two rational points on a $3$-isogenous curve come from the Stewart--Top sextic. Modulo their Kummer classes and a torsion class, the isogeny Selmer group has a basis given by the fixed primes. We realize every alternating matrix in this basis by prescribing the Frobenius classes of six primes in a fixed Galois extension. A nondegenerate matrix forces the rank to be exactly two and determines the entire primary group.

papers.title: Concentration in Hardy equations and singular heat flows
papers.abstract: We investigate the stability and loss of concentrated source data in critical Hardy equations and in singular heat flows. For the critical local Hardy form, a dyadic condition on the radial marginal characterizes admissibility and strong energy convergence under a uniform bound on angular densities. For general diffuse measures at inverse power one, strong convergence is characterized by mass convergence and condenser-capacity discrepancies. We also establish sharp moment inequalities and tightness criteria for the radial pole trace and boundary slope. At the sharp fractional $L^p$ Hardy coefficient, we identify the pole flux in a nonlinear power balance and show that finite remainder excludes nonconstant strong angular traces. For every fractional order, positive data can have finite remainder but infinite source pairing. Finally, for singular heat reactions with a positive nonincreasing factor tending to zero at infinity, we determine all attainable reaction limits of a time impulse and of data exhausted by parabolic Kato measures. A total variation estimate describes the combination of these mechanisms for countably many impulses.

papers.title: AmorphGen: A Python package for amorphous structure generation with machine-learning and classical interatomic potentials
papers.abstract: AmorphGen is an open-source Python package for generating and analyzing amorphous structures from a composition or a crystal. Chemically informed rules estimate initial densities and assign separation and coordination constraints. Three routes are available: random placement followed by relaxation, melt-quench from a crystal, and a hybrid route that anneals and quenches random structures. ASE provides access to classical and machine-learning potentials, with GPU batching for selected backends. Analysis tools compute coordination numbers, bond angles, rings, and X-ray or neutron structure factors for comparison with measurements. An optional interface to the FEFF code computes extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra. For amorphous Ga2O3, TiO2 and InGaZnO4, the cation coordination numbers are close to reference models and measurements, and the X-ray structure factors reproduce the main measured peaks. The EXAFS spectra for Ga2O3 and InGaZnO4 also capture the dominant first-shell features observed experimentally. The hybrid route reduces bonding defects in SiO2 and As and builds the first sharp diffraction peak of SiO2. By simplifying ensemble generation and standardizing structural assessment, AmorphGen makes it practical to compare amorphous models across compositions, potentials, and preparation routes, and to screen new amorphous compositions.

papers.title: STAGE: Structured Test-Time Adaptation with Global Entropic Soft-coupling for Cross-Subject Brain-to-Image Retrieval
papers.abstract: Cross-subject brain-to-image retrieval aims to identify viewed images from unseen subjects' brain signals. However, inter-subject variability hinders alignment of brain-image representations, while independent query ranking tends to concentrate predictions on a few candidates, making accurate retrieval difficult without target labels. We propose STAGE (Structured Test-Time Adaptation with Global Entropic Soft-coupling), a structured test-time adaptation framework for recovering cross-subject alignment from uncertain brain-image correspondences. Moment calibration reduces statistical discrepancies between features, while coupling-weighted initialization establishes initial alignment. Coupling-guided adaptation further refines residual feature mismatches, and soft-coupling ranking coordinates candidate competition across queries to prevent overly concentrated matching assignments. Using only unlabeled target batches, STAGE maintains consistent matching from feature calibration to image retrieval while keeping both encoders frozen. Experiments on three public datasets validate STAGE's retrieval performance. On THINGS-EEG2, STAGE achieves 68.25% Top-1 and 90.47% Top-5, improving Top-1 by 18.52 percentage points over SCORE recovery and CSLS on identical frozen NICE features. Calibrated on 200 queries and a 200-image gallery covering their identities, STAGE retains 42.05% Top-1 when ranking 1,854 images with the transform frozen.

papers.title: Exact superdiffusion exponents and hull exploration of chiral random walkers on critical percolation clusters
papers.abstract: Generalizing de Gennes' ant-in-the-labyrinth concept, we consider a chiral random walker on a percolation cluster at criticality. The fully chiral ant clings to obstacle boundaries and traces the fractal hulls of the cluster, spreading with the exact walk dimension $7/4$ until its orbit closes. Because the cluster contains holes on all scales, the ensemble spreads superdiffusively, $\langle r^2\rangle\sim t^{89/84}$, carried by a diminishing fraction of walkers whose orbits are still open. Both exponents follow from percolation geometry alone, and agree well with large-scale numerical simulations. When the walker turns chirally only with probability $χ<1$, superdiffusion gives way to the subdiffusion of the ant at a crossover time set by both exponents, with a diffusion coefficient enhanced by $(1-χ)^{-2/d_w}$. The relation between crossover time and diffusion coefficient does not depend on how chirality is realized, offering a direct test for chiral tracers in disordered media.

papers.title: Estimating Silenced Tokens in Quantized LLMs
papers.abstract: Quantization is the standard way to shrink large language models, and it is usually judged by perplexity and task accuracy. We ask a different question: after quantization, which words can the model still say at all? A token is silenced when no hidden state can make it the top choice of the output layer, so a greedy decoder can never produce it. We give a simple, scalable way to estimate how many tokens a quantized output head silences, combining three checks: a direction that lets a token win (so it is safe), an upper bound on how close a token's row is to being trapped inside the others, and an exact match that proves a token can never win. Each count is therefore a certified range: exact matches give its lower end and flagged tokens can only raise its upper end. In nearly all settings we report down to 3 bits the two ends coincide, so the counts are exact. Across three open models we find that quantization silences tokens: on large-vocabulary models it already appears at 8-bit precision, up to a few hundred previously reachable tokens on a 1B-parameter model, and grows as precision drops, while a small-vocabulary model resists until 3 bits. The loss is far from uniform across languages: on a multilingual vocabulary the silenced tokens are overwhelmingly non-Latin (Korean, Chinese, Thai, Arabic and Hebrew), even though Latin tokens dominate the vocabulary. Silencing is thus a measurable, language-sensitive side effect that standard averages miss, and it should be reported alongside them.

papers.title: A Finiteness Result for Commuting Squares and Quantitative Ocneanu Rigidity
papers.abstract: We introduce the spanning relative commutant condition (SRC) for nondegenerate commuting squares of matrix algebras. The condition requires that the second relative commutant span the next algebra in the lower row of the basic construction as a right module over the preceding algebra. We prove that if a sequence of SRC squares with fixed tracial inclusion data converges, then all but finitely many terms are isomorphic to the limit square. We also show that the standard commuting square of every finite-index inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors of depth two satisfies SRC. This gives a commuting-square proof of Ocneanu's finiteness theorem for standard invariants with a prescribed finite principal graph. We then obtain the explicit bound $B(D)=10^{7D^5}$ for the number of SRC squares up to isomorphism when the upper-right tracial algebra is prescribed and has dimension $D$. The same function bounds the number of standard invariants with a prescribed finite principal graph when $D$ is the number of closed walks of length $6\ell$ at the root, where $\ell$ is the least odd integer at least the diameter. We also characterize the Hadamard matrices whose spin model commuting squares satisfy SRC. These are precisely the matrices equivalent to character tables of finite abelian groups.

papers.title: Sixth-Order Q-Curvature of Conformally Euclidean Metrics: Improved Dimensional Thresholds, Quantitative Lower Bounds and Applications
papers.abstract: This paper studies the sign of the sixth-order \(Q\)-curvature of conformally Euclidean metrics on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) for integers \(n\ge2m\) and \(m\ge4\). Under suitable assumptions, we refine the sixfold integral estimates and prove that \(Q_g^{(6)}>0\) whenever \(2m\le n\le4m-6+[\widehat h_m]\), where \(\widehat h_m\) is the unique positive root of \(G_m\) and \(\widehat h_m\sim\frac{2\sqrt7-4}{3}m\) as \(m\to\infty\). Moreover, we strengthen this positivity result by establishing the quantitative lower bound \(Q_g^{(6)}(x)\geΘ_{m,n}\bigl(Q_g^{(2)}(x)\bigr)^3>0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), where \(Θ_{m,n}>0\) is an explicit constant depending only on \(m\) and \(n\). These quantitative inequalities also yield explicit lower bounds for intermediate Laplacians in higher-order elliptic equations. On the non-positivity side, we construct metrics satisfying \(Q_g^{(6)}(0)<0\) whenever \(n>\widetilde N_m\), where \(\widetilde N_m\sim\widetildeΛm\) as \(m\to\infty\) and \(\widetildeΛ\simeq9.74268\). These metrics extend smoothly to \(\mathbb S^n\) and are conformal to the round metric. In the same dimensional range, we further construct metrics with \(Q_g^{(6)}(0)>0\) and establish uniform positive lower and upper bounds for \(Q_g^{(2m)}\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). Our results extend the positivity range and lower the counterexample threshold obtained by Vétois and Zeitler (arXiv preprint, 2026). The sixth-order estimate also answers a question raised in our previous work on quantitative fourth-order \(Q\)-curvature bounds. These results provide new insights into Conjecture 1 of Li and Xu (J. Funct. Anal. 289 (2025), 111011) in the case \(k=3\), clarifying its validity and limitations across different dimensions.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Smooth Convex Optimization with a Comparison Oracle
papers.abstract: We study the minimization of a convex $d$-dimensional function with $L$-Lipschitz gradient when the only available information is a comparison oracle that reports which of two points has the smaller objective value. Given an initial point within distance $R$ of a minimizer, the constants $L$ and $R$, and $A = LR^2/\varepsilon$, we give a deterministic method that returns an $\varepsilon$-optimal point using $O(\sqrt{A}\,[d\log(2dA)+\log^2(2A)])$ comparisons for $A\ge1$, counting all comparisons spent in inner subroutines. The method is based on a normalized variant of Nemirovski's subspace method: each iteration performs a line search along an estimated gradient direction followed by a minimization over a two-dimensional affine subspace, and both subroutines rely on a comparison oracle and basic arithmetic operations only. With exact function values, combining finite-difference gradients with an accelerated method gives the well-known bound of $O(d\sqrt{A})$ evaluations; our bound shows that one bit per query suffices to match it up to logarithmic factors. Since two function values determine one comparison, the exact function-value lower bound of Dorn et al. implies that our bound is optimal up to logarithmic factors when $32\le A\le d^2$.

papers.title: Adaptation or Poisoning? Security Risks of Conversational Test-Time Learning in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Test-time learning (TTL) enables large language models to adapt to unlabeled inputs during deployment. The model updates a lightweight adapter by minimizing the next-token prediction loss on the input it receives. When these updates persist across conversation turns, every user query serves both as the request answered in the current turn and as adaptation data for later turns. By choosing the queries used for adaptation, an attacker can influence parameter updates and weaken safety alignment through ordinary interactions with a TTL chat service. To demonstrate this risk, we introduce Progressive Test-Time Adaptation Poisoning (P-TAP), a query-only multi-turn attack that jailbreaks the model by poisoning its session adapter through the service's own updates. A sequence of escalating adversarial queries shapes the adapter turn by turn; the final harmful request is then answered under the accumulated state without itself being used for adaptation. Across four open-weight instruction-tuned models, enabling updates raises attack success rates on average by 13.00 percentage points under greedy decoding and by 22.25 points under best-of-10 sampling, relative to matched sessions receiving the same queries without updates. Answering adversarial queries but adapting on unrelated text or on benign text about the same topic removes most of this increase. Among existing safeguards, screening incoming queries flags every attack stream before the final request, while a perplexity-based detector of unsafe adaptation flags none of the successful attacks.

papers.title: Analysis of the Cosmos 2612 - ICEYE-X36 rendezvous and proximity operation from public orbital element data
papers.abstract: We analyse the October 2026 close approach between Cosmos 2612 (NORAD 68762) and the commercial radar satellite ICEYE-X36 (NORAD 59103), both in sun-synchronous low Earth orbit, to determine whether it was a rendezvous and proximity operation (RPO) or the result of natural orbital evolution. The public general perturbations (GP) element history from April to October 2026 was propagated with SGP4, and the prediction error was measured empirically for each object. The null hypothesis of natural evolution, tested with manoeuvre-free propagations, is rejected for all 18 parameter combinations: the encounter required manoeuvres by Cosmos 2612, whereas those of ICEYE-X36 are not needed to reproduce it. Closest approach occurred on 18 October at 06:33 UTC, below 0.79 km (95th percentile), with a local relative velocity of about 0.08 m/s and 41.4 h continuously within 5 km. It was the final stage of a sequence that began in May with a plane match, followed by a phasing drift, the approach and a manoeuvred retreat, with a minimum cumulative $Δv$ of 174-180 m/s. The data cannot resolve the minimum distance below their accuracy, nor establish whether the operation was cooperative or its purpose.

papers.title: Nonvanishing of mean indices and stability of symmetric closed characteristics on symmetric star-shaped hypersurfaces in ${\bf R}^4$
papers.abstract: H. Duan, H. Liu, Y. Long and W. Wang \cite{DLLW24} conjectured that if a compact star-shaped hypersurface in ${\bf R}^{2n}$ carries only finitely many geometrically distinct prime closed characteristics, then each of them has nonzero mean index. They proved this conjecture for non-degenerate star-shaped hypersurfaces in ${\bf R}^6$. Motivated by their work, we study the symmetric counterpart of this problem. We prove that if a symmetric compact star-shaped hypersurface $Σ$ in ${\bf R}^4$ carries only finitely many geometrically distinct prime symmetric closed characteristics, and every odd iterate of them is non-degenerate in the symmetric sense, then each of them has nonzero symmetric mean index. Based on this result, we further prove that if $Σ$ carries exactly two geometrically distinct prime symmetric closed characteristics and all their iterates are non-degenerate, then both of them are irrationally elliptic.

papers.title: On-demand frequency-entangled microwave biphotons from a transmon-resonator dimer
papers.abstract: We propose a superconducting circuit QED source of on-demand frequency-entangled microwave photon pairs, with one photon emitted into each of two separate waveguides, enabling individual manipulation. The design is based on a transmon-resonator dimer, which consists of two transmon-resonator subsystems coupled through a cross-Kerr interaction. We outline a viable circuit-QED realization in which the required cross-Kerr interaction is implemented using Josephson-junction couplers. To analyze the emission dynamics, we derive and numerically solve the set of evolution equations that enable tracking the evolution of the joint spectral intensity of photons. We characterize the resulting photon-number correlations, frequency anticorrelation, and spectral entanglement. By varying the coupling strengths, we obtain biphotons with distinct joint spectral intensities and Schmidt spectra, ranging from broadly distributed multimode entanglement to states dominated by two nearly equally weighted Schmidt contributions. In the latter regime, optimizing the transmon-resonator coupling and detuning yields an output biphoton state that has fidelity $F \approx 0.956$ with a two-dimensional maximally entangled state. Restricting the local target modes to separated frequency bins yields a fidelity $F_\mathrm{bin} \approx 0.949$, indicating that the output state closely approximates a frequency-bin Bell pair. Thus, the proposed microwave biphoton source provides a route toward distributing frequency-encoded quantum resources between remote superconducting nodes.

papers.title: Some results on the isotropy groups of non-invertible simple derivations
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $2\le i<n$, and let $d_i$ be a $k$-derivation of $k[x_1,\dots,x_i]$. We study the $k$-derivation of $k[x_1,\dots, x_n]$ of the form $d_n=d_i+\sum_{j=i}^{n-1}\bigl(a_jx_{j+1}+g_j(x_j)\bigr)\partial_{x_{j+1}}$ where $a_j\in k$ and $g_j\in k[x_j]\setminus k$. Under suitable conditions on $d_i$, we show that the isotropy group of $d_n$ consists of translations and is either trivial or isomorphic to $(k,+)$.

papers.title: Diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral collisions at the LHC
papers.abstract: We compute the cross section for coherent diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral lead-lead and proton-lead collisions (UPCs) at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) within the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective field theory. We include both the exclusive production of a charm-anticharm pair and diffractive production with an additional semi-hard gluon, described in diffractive transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization. We show that the diffractive channel, although suppressed by the strong coupling, dominates at large transverse momentum, where the exclusive channel is suppressed by color transparency. Furthermore, we quantify nuclear effects at the parton level with a nuclear modification factor $R_{pA}$ at fixed photon energy, which shows a mild suppression for the diffractive channel and an enhancement growing with transverse momentum up to about a factor of 2 for the exclusive one. We also use the diffractive cross section to correct our inclusive $D^0$ predictions to the CMS event selection, which requires the target nucleus to break up, and compare them with the data. Finally, we provide predictions for inclusive $D^0$ photoproduction in proton-lead UPCs.

papers.title: Package feyn.gle for drawing Feynman diagrams, version 1.2
papers.abstract: As compared to the previous version, there is one backward-incompatible change and many new kinds of lines and other objects.

papers.title: Feedback Completion Certificates for Repeated Dwell Tasks with Time Windows
papers.abstract: An inspection robot may owe several measurements at the same station, each with a different window in which a dwell can begin. We ask what a feedback controller must retain about earlier visits to guarantee all remaining deadlines under bounded disturbances. For a common spatial predicate and dwell length, removing redundant windows orders the remaining obligations by both endpoints. On every history without an expired obligation, the served windows form a suffix. One boundary and one capped run length therefore preserve the future satisfaction of the original task. On a verified library of branching motion primitives we use this state to recover a feedback policy. For one task type a scalar threshold per run length suffices, with work linear in the number of listed branches per time layer for fixed dwell. Multiple types require a joint recursion. On a quadrotor inspection library the threshold sweep reduced the cost of constructing a reusable full-domain policy, while a sparse Boolean baseline answered a single initial query faster. In a two-station MuJoCo patrol, three task-aware filters all met every window in twelve paired runs each. Of eight initially certified runs, the completion filter retained the certificate in all eight, compared with three for safety-only filtering.

papers.title: Eight limit cycles in a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system
papers.abstract: Gyllenberg and Yan conjectured that a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system can have at least five limit cycles. We prove the conjecture by constructing a strictly competitive system in which eight distinct limit cycles coexist near a single positive equilibrium. For each $m=5,6,7,8$, we construct a weak focus of order $m$ and identify parameter directions on the Hopf hypersurface that allow us to vary the first $m-1$ focus quantities independently. We choose these quantities so that the drift of a scalar amplitude function alternates in sign on $m$ nested level curves, forcing a limit cycle between each consecutive pair. A perturbation transverse to the Hopf hypersurface creates one additional cycle inside the others. The one-turn displacement map shows that both local counts are sharp. For each $m$, we give a rigorous computer-assisted proof that an explicit rational interaction matrix yields at least $m$ distinct hyperbolic limit cycles. We thank GPT-6 Astra for helping us compare earlier constructions, identify the main obstacle to extending them, and develop the present approach.

papers.title: Survey of Compact Sources for Pulsars and Exotic Objects-II. Precision Timing of Millisecond Pulsar J1840+1102
papers.abstract: We present the timing analysis of the eclipsing millisecond pulsar PSR J1840+1102, discovered in the Survey of COmpact sources for Pulsars and Exotic objects (SCOPE) using the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT). PSR J1840+1102 has a short spin period of 1.60 ms and an orbital period of 1.68 days, with a dispersion measure (DM) of 98.8 pc cm$^{-3}$. We report timing analysis over a 2.7-year baseline, yielding a phase-connected solution with a post-fit residual RMS of 2.1 $μ$s. Enabled by the timing solution, we report discovery of pulsed gamma-rays from PSR J1840+1102, with the gamma-ray peak aligned with that of the radio profile. PSR J1840+1102 also exhibits remarkably short eclipses, lasting only around $0.4\%$ of the total orbit at 650 MHz. Based on optical searches, the orbital parameters, short eclipses, and comparison with the known binary pulsar population, we infer a Helium white dwarf (He-WD) surrounded by plasma to be the most likely companion. Furthermore, using GMRT observations covering 300 to 750 MHz, we present a study of the interstellar medium properties towards PSR J1840+1102 including refractive scintillation, DM variations and scattering, and report a very low scattering index of $1.65\pm0.15$. The low timing residuals and lack of any prominent orbital parameters or DM variations support the overall suitability of PSR J1840+1102 for inclusion in the pulsar timing array campaigns.

papers.title: Convergence of Nonmonotone Schemes to Viscosity Solutions via Local Comparison
papers.abstract: We develop a convergence criterion for nonmonotone approximation schemes for Hamilton--Jacobi and fully nonlinear second-order equations. Under stability, consistency and suitable boundary assumptions, a local comparison hypothesis replaces monotonicity and yields convergence to viscosity solutions. For a semi-Lagrangian CWENO scheme for one-dimensional Hamilton--Jacobi equations, we establish convergence for bounded uniformly continuous initial data under $h=o(τ)$, relaxing the previously required mesh condition $h=O(τ^2)$. We also prove convergence of a nonmonotone one-dimensional $Q^2$ scheme for Isaacs equations whose operator cannot be written as a monotone operator plus a perturbation vanishing uniformly on bounded grid functions.

papers.title: A Goldbach-Type Problem for Random Multiplicative Functions
papers.abstract: We study the counts of the four sign patterns of a random multiplicative function on ordered decompositions $a+b=N$ into positive integers. The main term is $N/4$ in the nonvanishing model and $F(N)/4$ in the squarefree-supported model, where $F(N)$ counts the pairs with both summands squarefree and has asymptotic main term $\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{sf}}(N)N$. Let $ρ_q$ be the probability of a negative sign at the prime $q$. Set $m_q=\min(ρ_q,1-ρ_q)$, $A_N=\sum_{(\log N)^3<q\le N}m_q/q$, and $B(N)=\sum_{q\le N}m_q/q$. In the general model with independent prime vectors, almost surely for all sufficiently large integers $N$, the error for opposite-sign pairs is $O_{\mathcal X}(Ne^{-4A_N})$, and the error for same-sign pairs is $O_{\mathcal X}(N(e^{-4A_N}+e^{-2B(N)}))$. In four specified models, if the biases of the independent basic signs are square summable, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ the error is almost surely $O_{\varepsilon,\mathcal X}(N^{1/2+\varepsilon})$. In the completely multiplicative model under the same bias condition, we prove that $C_f(N)/\sqrt{N\log N}$ almost surely has limit superior $2$ and limit inferior $-2$. Together with a known bound for the one-point sum, this gives limit superior $1/2$ and limit inferior $-1/2$ for each normalized counting error about $N/4$

papers.title: Restricted open-shell Kohn-Sham theory for arbitrary genealogical spin coupling
papers.abstract: We introduce a generalization of restricted open-shell Kohn-Sham (ROKS) theory to a single configuration state function (CSF) with arbitrary genealogical spin coupling. This CSF-ROKS theory establishes a spin-pure density functional extension of the recently developed CSF-based restricted open-shell Hartree-Fock (CSF-ROHF) theory, providing a computationally efficient route to incorporate dynamic electron correlation. The energy is expressed as a weighted sum over unrestricted determinants built from a common set of restricted orbitals, and the number of determinants grows quadratically with the number of open shells. Numerical calculations for N$_2$ and the polyacene series show that CSF-ROKS solutions retain chemically interpretable character. Exchange-correlation functionals preferentially stabilize low-seniority configurations, shifting the onset of polyradical character in polyacenes to longer chains than predicted by CSF-ROHF. Furthermore, CSF-ROKS can be used to target state-specific spin-pure excitations in the vinyl and allyl radicals, and the [Cr(ddpd)$_2$]$^{3+}$ molecular ruby. However, CSF-ROKS incorrectly predicts ferromagnetic coupling in a set of bridged transition metal dimers, indicating that kinetic exchange requires more advanced correlated methods.

papers.title: Layer-Level Control of Language Model Execution in Agent Frameworks
papers.abstract: Agent frameworks typically orchestrate language models through prompt-and-response interfaces. We propose a harness design that exposes intermediate model states and layer-level execution controls to the agent runtime. By connecting state collection, policy fitting, and execution, the design enables policies to allocate computation within and across models based on intermediate states. We demonstrate the approach with a prototype that learns stitching bridges and state-conditioned execution policies from paired model states, then applies them during inference to select among continue, exit, and stitch.
