Fine-tuning reduced every reported field mean absolute error (MAE) relative to training from scratch at the same target budget. For joint surface and volume prediction, fine-tuning on 100 truck cases matched or improved on all four field MAEs obtained by training from scratch on 200 cases. Second, an independently trained model learned a base task using 332 DrivAerML cases and was adapted to a novel task using 31 cases with a previously unseen combination of design features. Experience replay incorporated cases from the base-task training set during adaptation. Full replay lowered field errors on 45 held-out base-task designs by approximately 36% to 42% relative to adaptation without replay; retaining half the base-task training set yielded reductions of approximately 30% to 35%. Together, these findings support transfer learning and experience replay as complementary strategies for data-efficient neural surrogate development across successive engineering tasks.

papers.title: PFASST-BISICLES: A Parallel-in-Time Ice Sheet Model
papers.abstract: Efficiently simulating ice sheet dynamics on modern computational systems is essential for projecting the response of ice sheets to climate forcing and the resulting contributions to sea level change. On modern computational systems, this demands high levels of parallelism to fully exploit modern architectures. Traditionally, time-dependent simulations like ice sheet models achieve parallelism entirely by distributing the spatial domain, while remaining serial in time, as solutions are marched forward. We present PFASST-BISICLES, which combines the Parallel Full Approximation Scheme in Space and Time (PFASST) with BISICLES ice sheet model to integrate multiple timesteps concurrently. We evaluate numerical agreement and parallel performance using a fully grounded sinusoidal ice stream with adaptive mesh refinement and the MISMIP+ marine ice-sheet benchmark. For the sinusoidal stream, PFASST-BISICLES produces temporal errors approximately an order of magnitude smaller than forward Euler at the same timestep, although both methods exhibit approximately first-order convergence. Spatial scaling levels off near 16 processors, while temporal parallelism provides further acceleration, with nearly linear speedup through approximately 16 temporal processors. In MISMIP+, PFASST-BISICLES reproduces the main thickness and velocity patterns after glacier evolution of 50 years, with the largest differences concentrated near the grounding zone. Increasing the temporal processor count from one to four, with four spatial processors fixed, reduces runtime from 33.8 to 10.5 hours. These results demonstrate that temporal parallelism can complement spatial decomposition in ice-sheet modeling, reducing time to solution while maintaining agreement in the main simulated features.

papers.title: Sub-Riemannian flow matching
papers.abstract: We study sub-Riemannian conditional flow matching (SRCFM) for generative transport with prescribed velocity constraints. Training uses paths between sampled source and target points whose velocities lie in the allowed horizontal directions at each state. A neural network takes time and the full state as input and predicts the coefficients of these directions, and the horizontal frame then determines the full velocity used for generation. We describe constructions based on Heisenberg geodesics and joint endpoint equations in free step-two Carnot groups. We propose a scalable piecewise algorithm that computes horizontal paths directly from their endpoints. A straight segment sets the horizontal coordinates, and a loop in those coordinates corrects the remaining vertical displacement. We verify the algorithm's endpoint accuracy to numerical precision in high-dimensional tests. Synthetic experiments illustrate approximate distribution transport along horizontal trajectories. On resized MNIST, we use the same construction to generate images from Gaussian inputs with fewer controls than pixels.

papers.title: A Bayesian Mechanistic Model of Spatiotemporal Dynamics in Invasive Tree Species
papers.abstract: Modeling the spatiotemporal dynamics of invasive species requires frameworks that represent spread and growth mechanisms explicitly while accommodating the distributional features of ecological data. We propose a Bayesian mechanistic framework for invasive tree cover that combines an ecological diffusion--logistic growth partial differential equation (PDE) with a zero-inflated binomial observation model. The diffusion and growth coefficients are modeled as functions of environmental covariates, enabling direct inference on the ecological processes driving encroachment, and the zero-inflation component separates structural absence from low observed cover. To enable scalable Bayesian inference on satellite-resolution grids, we derive a homogenized equation for ecological diffusion with spatially varying diffusion and growth coefficients, which reduces computation while preserving large-scale spatial structure. Applied to satellite-derived tree cover in a subregion of the Nebraska Sandhills, where eastern redcedar is encroaching on grassland, the model indicates that elevation is strongly associated with where tree cover accumulates but only weakly with its local growth rate, whereas distance to the nearest stream is associated with both. Compared with a generalized additive model, a spatial hierarchical model fitted via INLA, and a regression tree, the proposed method directly estimates these processes as interpretable functions of environmental covariates and gives the best-calibrated predictive uncertainty.

papers.title: A Unified Bregman Projection Framework for Solving Multi-Split Multiple-Set Implicit Convex Feasibility Problems
papers.abstract: We study the multi-split multiple-set implicit convex feasibility problem (MSMS-ICFP), in which the constraint sets are generated by point-to-set operators and the feasibility conditions are imposed both in the original space and in several image spaces connected by bounded linear operators. We analyze the generalized proximity function, built from weighted Bregman distances and Bregman projections, introduced by Censor and Dey. For translation-type point-to-set operators, we establish the continuity and Lipschitz continuity of the corresponding Bregman projections, the continuous differentiability of the proximity function with an explicit formula for its gradient, and global and local Lipschitz estimates for this gradient. We then propose a generalized simultaneous projection gradient algorithm. In the nonconvex case, the gradient norms of the iterates converge to zero and every accumulation point is stationary. When the proximity function is convex and the solution set is nonempty, the iterates converge in norm to a solution, with an $O(1/k)$ rate for the proximity values, an $O(1/\sqrt{k})$ rate for the gradient norms, and a linear rate under a quadratic growth condition. Cyclic and block-iterative variants are also analyzed. Numerical experiments, including a cooperative sensor network localization problem, illustrate the theory and show that, in contrast with frozen-set implicit projection methods, the proposed gradient schemes remain convergent when the translation operators are expansive.

papers.title: Lean Census: A Distributional Analysis of AI-Generated Lean Code
papers.abstract: We compare two human-written and four AI-generated Lean libraries with Mathlib through the distributions of simple statistics of their code. For each library we measure inline claims in proofs, proof length, how often each declaration is used, and design choices such as instances and private declarations, and we read each against the variation among Mathlib's own areas. The AI-generated libraries have more inline claims per theorem, longer proofs, fewer instances, and more private declarations than the human-written ones. We release the code for the analysis as a package, lean-census, at https://github.com/project-numina/lean-census.

papers.title: Chiral and deconfinement thermodynamics of the Polyakov-quark linear sigma model with and without charm quark: an SU(3) versus SU(4) comparison
papers.abstract: Using the Polyakov-loop extended linear-sigma model (PLSM), we investigate strongly interacting matter at finite temperature and baryon density by comparing the three-flavor (u,d,s) and four-flavor (u,d,s,c) formulations on equal footing, with the aim of isolating the thermal contribution of the charm quark. The model describes chiral dynamics through explicit and spontaneous symmetry breaking and reproduces the vacuum spectra of scalar and pseudoscalar mesons. Confinement is incorporated through a logarithmic Polyakov-loop potential calibrated to the continuum lattice-QCD equation of state (EoS). Within the mean-field approximation, we calculate light-, strange-, and charm-quark condensates, the Polyakov loop, and bulk thermodynamic observables, including pressure, trace anomaly, and entropy density, over broad ranges of temperature and baryon chemical potential. We also determine the chiral and deconfinement pseudocritical boundaries and represent them as phase boundaries and three-dimensional order-parameter surfaces. After tuning the Polyakov sector to lattice-QCD pressure and trace-anomaly data, the resulting entropy density agrees with HotQCD 2+1(+1)-flavor results throughout the crossover region. At zero baryon density, the non-strange condensate melts at Tc = 210 MeV in SU(3) and 218 MeV in SU(4), with curvature parameters kappa=0.018 and 0.017. Because mc>>Tc, charm remains thermally suppressed across the crossover. After normalization to the corresponding Stefan-Boltzmann limits, the SU(3) and SU(4) EoS nearly coincide below T~2Tc. Charm mainly contributes through a higher ideal-gas limit, a gradual high-temperature tail, and the flavor ordering u,d->s->c. For all baryon chemical potentials accessible within mean-field theory, the hadron-parton transition remains a smooth crossover.

papers.title: Similarity preserving noncommutative maps
papers.abstract: In this note we study similarity preserving automorphisms of noncommutative (NC for short) balls. We show that every similarity preserving NC automorphism is, in fact, given by a similarity with an NC invertible function. As an application, we show that the group of automorphisms of the free semigroup algebra is generated by unitarily implemented and inner automorphisms.

papers.title: Froq: Safe Speculative Execution on Live Quantum States for FTQC
papers.abstract: Reducing execution time is critical to fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) as longer executions expose logical qubits to more opportunities for failure. However, quantum processors could frequently stall due to slow classical error-correction decoders. Recent speculative decoding accelerates this process, but its speculation remains on the classical side, leaving quantum operations waiting for confirmed decoding results. Extending speculative execution to the quantum side is fundamentally challenging. Unlike classical processor states, quantum states cannot be arbitrarily copied or checkpointed for rollback, making recovery from mispredictions difficult. In this work, we propose Froq to enable safe speculative execution on live quantum states. Froq uses compiler-assisted recovery contracts to track how mispredictions propagate through quantum operations. It further employs a resource-aware runtime mechanism to reserve recovery workspace and dynamically balance the benefits of speculative execution against the expected costs of recovery. We evaluate Froq on eight FTQC programs across 88 configurations, building on an existing speculative window decoder. Froq reduces quantum-side time by 9.81% across all 88 configurations. The reduction reaches 18.34% across the 45 configurations allowing concurrent predictions, and peaks at 31.1% at code distance d=21, under limited resources.

papers.title: When AI Should Not Decide: Evidence Sufficiency and Decision Stability in Automated Job Interviews
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to assess employment candidates, yet consistent interview scoring does not establish whether automated recommendations are supported by sufficient evidence. This study introduces the Evidence Sufficiency and Decision Stability Assessment (ESDSA), which combines criterion-level evidence classification, deterministic quotation traceability and stability checks across linguistic variants assessed as substantively equivalent. We evaluated four approaches (scoring-only, evidence-aware, traceability-based and integrated ESDSA v2) using 540 synthetic interview responses from 60 evaluated scenario families across Software Engineering, Customer Support and Operations. In held-out testing (216 responses), integrated ESDSA achieved 85.19% actionable coverage and 3.80% disagreement among actionable recommendations against AI-assisted provisional references. Evidence-aware evaluation achieved 92.59% coverage and 4.50% disagreement; scoring-only evaluation achieved 71.30% coverage and 1.95% disagreement. The integrated stability gate deferred 11 additional previously actionable decisions, ten of which had agreed with provisional references. The findings demonstrate trade-offs between evidential constraints, decision consistency and abstention, rather than overall superiority of the integrated framework. ESDSA offers a reproducible methodology for examining when automated interview recommendations should be actionable or deferred. Synthetic responses and AI-assisted references do not establish real-world recruitment validity.

papers.title: A characterization of Ramsey property with application to dynamical systems
papers.abstract: The infinitary Ramsey theorem says that in any finite partition {V^i;~i=1,2,\cdots,n} of the the family of k-subsets of N, there exists V^i having an infinite subset M of N such that any k-set from M is in V^i. This property of V^i is called the Ramsey property. We characterize this property in term of ultrafilter.

papers.title: The recoil nucleon effect in nuclear systems
papers.abstract: Nuclear excitation energies are typically in the keV-MeV range, but rare eV-scale transitions remain a puzzle for nuclear theory. This work develops a two-body recoil model to describe $β^-$ decay on the basis of classic momentum conservation. Using the final states of $β^-$ decay with a keV-scale excitation energy, the model yields eV-scale recoil energy for a single nucleon. It indicates the recoil nucleon effect in nuclear systems: a single nucleon bound in a nucleus can be excited by absorbing the recoil momentum. The observed eV-scale isomers in $^{235}$U and $^{229}$Th can be attributed to the recoil neucleon effect. This effect could spark a eV-scale energy, and provide a solid theoretical foundation for predicting such extremely small energies. The new discovery will place low-energy nuclear isomer research at the cutting edge of new-physics searches, while offers a clean and complementary alternative to high-energy accelerator experiments.

papers.title: Real-Time 250-kHz Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography Using a Jetson AGX Orin
papers.abstract: High-performance optical coherence tomography (OCT) relies on desktop workstations for data acquisition, reconstruction, and visualization, limiting integration into compact imaging systems. We evaluated whether an embedded GPU platform could sustain real-time operation of a 250-kHz spectral-domain OCT instrument without a desktop computer. A custom C++/CUDA OCT engine running on a NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB was developed and integrated with a 2048-pixel spectrometer, Camera Link frame grabber, and galvanometer scanner, and compared against an RTX A4500 workstation under the same scan protocols. Both systems maintained mean B-scan processing latency well below the corresponding B-scan acquisition intervals. Although the RTX A4500 workstation achieved lower reconstruction latency, Jetson eliminated explicit host-to-device transfer and exhibited more consistent processing latency. Furthermore, the measured active wall power was 67 W for the Jetson and 155 W for the workstation, corresponding to approximately 2.3 times greater wall-energy efficiency for the Jetson. In a separate 62.6-min GUI-enabled measurement, the Jetson processed 800,000 B-scans without frame loss while maintaining real-time reconstruction and visualization. These results demonstrate that embedded computing can support high-speed OCT acquisition, processing, and control while reducing wall-power demand and computing-platform size.

papers.title: Diurnal Warm Layer and Marginal Instability in the Ocean Surface Boundary Layer
papers.abstract: Large-eddy simulations with high near-surface grid resolution are used to investigate the diurnal modulation of the ocean surface boundary layer (OSBL) at various latitudes for Coriolis frequencies corresponding to 15-70$^\circ$N. The OSBL, which is driven here by a low wind, surface waves and a diurnally varying heat flux, exhibits a diurnal warm layer (DWL) during daytime and a convective mixing layer at night. The DWL exhibits enhanced shear leading to daytime turbulence that is found in this study to exist in a state of marginal instability (MI) over a wide range of latitudes and convective heat fluxes. The MI is characterized by an intricate balance between the momentum input by wind, stable stratification owing to solar radiation and turbulent mixing in the DWL, such that the gradient Richardson number is maintained around the critical value of 0.25 from morning to late afternoon. The enhanced shear and stratification sustained by MI leads to a substantial deviation from Monin-Obukhov Similarity Theory. Turbulent mixing induced by MI is shown to be similar to isolated local Kelvin-Helmholtz shear instability events and to share a similar range of flux coefficients and flux Richardson numbers. The impacts of increasing rotation and nightly convection on OSBL variability at the inertial and diurnal timescales are quantified through a turbulent kinetic energy analysis. The interaction between inertial oscillations and diurnal shear is an important feature of the DWL at mid and high latitudes.

papers.title: Targeted Learning for Externally Controlled Trials and Beyond
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on externally controlled trials (ECTs), which consist of a single-arm clinical trial supplemented by an external control arm (ECA). Potential data sources for the ECA can be broadly classified into three categories: (i) the control arm of a historical clinical trial, (ii) a concurrent cohort study, and (iii) external real-world data (RWD). In this paper, we consider a broad class of estimands defined through balancing weights. For a given estimand in the class, we discuss the efficient influence function (EIF) and the targeted maximum likelihood estimator (TMLE), together with practical implementation algorithms. Within the targeted learning framework, TMLE is a substitution estimator that enjoys several desirable theoretical properties and favorable finite-sample performance. Finally, the proposed framework is extended to two additional settings: (1) randomized controlled trials (RCTs) augmented with external covariate information to define a target population, and (2) indirect treatment comparisons (ITCs) that combine individual patient data (IPD) from an internal RCT with aggregate data (AgD) from an external RCT.

papers.title: Diversity over Scale: Recursive Self-Improvement with Ensembles of Small Open-Weight Models
papers.abstract: The advancement of large language models (LLMs) has significantly enhanced the capabilities of agents across various tasks. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) loops, in which a language model repeatedly rewrites a program and builds on its previous version, now perform well in machine-learning tasks, but they rely on frontier models and hundreds of calls per run. Small open-weight models are far cheaper, yet when used alone, their programs often crash and their improvements stall. We propose DiVE (diverse models evolve), an ensemble method for RSI that aims to improve creativity and diversity of generated solutions. DiVE uses three components: a shared memory, a failure log, and best-idea-wins rounds. This allows models to write candidate solutions from the same context and retain the best idea at each iteration. On 22 MLE-bench Lite competitions, an ensemble of five 8-12B open-weight models has 25.4% less test error than its average member and 16.7% less than Llama 3.3 70B, and comes within 7.1% of Qwen 3.5 122B-A10B at 75% of its cost. Diversity among small models can thus stand in for part of the scale that RSI relies on.

papers.title: Center-Aware Ordinal Learning for Prostate Cancer Grading from Histopathology Images
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer grading from histopathology whole-slide images (WSIs) is complicated by the ordered nature of ISUP grades, class imbalance, and center-dependent variations in staining, tissue preparation, and scanning. Most weakly supervised methods treat grade groups as independent categories and may therefore learn representations that do not transfer reliably across institutions. We propose a center-aware ordinal learning framework that combines a pretrained pathology encoder with attention-based multiple instance learning. The framework uses an Earth Mover's Distance loss to account for ordinal errors, an ordinal supervised contrastive objective to align same-grade slides across centers while separating grades according to disease severity, and curriculum learning to reduce the dominance of benign cases. We evaluate the framework on approximately 9,100 biopsy WSIs from the two-center PANDA dataset. The proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 0.842 and a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.958 on the held-out test set. Its main benefit is observed in cross-center transfer: when a linear probe is trained on Karolinska representations and evaluated on Radboud, accuracy increases from 0.643 to 0.823 and quadratic weighted kappa from 0.899 to 0.930. Performance remains stable in the reverse direction. UMAP projections further show improved mixing between centers while preserving an ordinal grade trajectory. These results suggest that combining ordinal and center-aware objectives produces more transferable slide representations for multi-center prostate cancer grading.

papers.title: WingBench: Benchmarking How AI Agents Search for Better Designs
papers.abstract: Design search often uses cheap learned predictions to choose which candidates deserve expensive tests, but these tests can fail, especially on the unusual designs that optimization favors. We introduce WingBench, a multifidelity benchmark in which optimizers and AI agents design transonic wings with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) inside the search. They can query a learned aerodynamic surrogate and spend a fixed budget of sequential CFD evaluations, each returning a score or a failure type. WingBench grades the design each method recommends, reporting separately whether it receives a valid score and how good that score is. Using WingBench, we contribute a study of five baseline optimizers and a comparison of three AI agent methods, which produced 6,629 CFD evaluation records. Feedback helps baseline optimizers deliver valid designs when it changes their later proposals, but the differential-evolution variant does so with lower aerodynamic quality. An open-ended research agent finds designs of similar quality to the strongest baselines over 32 CFD queries, with different prior information and unmatched total computation. In early search, our reflection and planning implementations do not consistently improve on it. We release the data, code, agent prompts, and analysis scripts for reproducibility.

papers.title: Bennett's conjecture on absolutely summing inclusions
papers.abstract: We settle Bennett's conjecture [\emph{Duke Math. J.} \textbf{44} (1977), 603--639, Conjecture~7.5] by showing that, for every $1<p<q<2$, the canonical inclusion $\ell_p\hookrightarrow\ell_q$ fails to be absolutely $(r_0,s_0)$-summing at the critical exponents he identified. As a consequence, we obtain a complete characterization of the admissible exponents in anisotropic bilinear Hardy--Littlewood inequalities over the real and complex fields.

papers.title: Belief-Driven Quantum Magnetometer Control for GPS-Denied Navigation
papers.abstract: Autonomous vehicles increasingly need to navigate without satellite positioning. Magnetic anomaly navigation (Mag-Nav) with quantum magnetometers offers a passive, unjammable fix, but the low size-weight-and-power (SWaP) sensors that small drones can carry are weak, and they are operated open loop at a fixed setting. Interferometric (Ramsey) magnetometers face a trade-off: long interrogation times are more sensitive but become ambiguous when the expected field is uncertain. The navigator's own position belief, pushed through the anomaly map, predicts that field. We close this loop. The filter's predictive field distribution sets the Ramsey phase and interrogation time at every epoch, through a closed-form rule that moves between an ambiguity limit and a decoherence limit. We evaluate it on real U.S. Air Force flight data (real tracks, inertial drift, measured fields, and a survey map tested 18 months after it was flown), with only the Ramsey sensor modelled. Against fixed-setting baselines, 63 of 72 independent flight windows favour belief driven sensing ($p = 2 \times 10^{-11}$). Error falls by 20-27% for low-SNR sensors and 30-44% for mid-contrast sensors. An ablation separates the two ingredients. Phase alignment drives the gain in steady flight, and the rule matches the best fixed setting without the hindsight tuning that setting requires. After a lost start, interrogation time adaptation is essential, cutting median error by 37-42% even against hindsight-tuned phase-aligned settings. Gains are small for high-quality sensors with accurate maps. On an IBM superconducting qubit, the rule's interrogation time stays within $1.3\times$ of the empirical optimum. Coupled with information-aware routing, belief-driven sensing lowers mission error by 15-40%.

papers.title: Essential and disjoint edge numbers for graphs and hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We study the extension to arbitrary forbidden sets of the property that every graph has a bipartition over which at least half of the graph edges are cross-edges, and obtain analogous results in the hypergraph setting.

papers.title: Neural-network-powered new-physics searches by predictive goodness of fit
papers.abstract: Model-independent searches for new physics test whether data agree with a Reference model with unknown nuisance parameters. Because the shape and location of a signal are not specified, these tests call for flexible learners (fitting procedures such as neural networks), and a likelihood ratio maximized over a neural network falls outside the standard asymptotic theory, making the calibration a major challenge. We propose a predictive alternative: the departure from the Reference is fitted on part of the data and its likelihood gain over the fitted Reference is evaluated on the rest, cross-fitted over several folds to preserve sample efficiency. The nuisance estimation error is propagated into the variance of the test statistic to first order, in the spirit of Neyman's C(alpha) test, so that the test need not be recalibrated at each nuisance value. The randomness in the fitted departure is treated by a central limit theorem for cross-validated statistics under algorithmic stability, plus a variance correction when stability is not achieved. The calibration is analytic, and no pseudo-experiments are needed. On established one-dimensional and five-dimensional (dilepton) benchmarks, the false-positive rate always stays within Monte Carlo error of nominal across different nuisances and the learners' tuning. The test's power relative to existing learned tests is mixed: higher for some signals and lower for others, depending on how well the fitted departure captures the signal.

papers.title: Geometric ergodicity of Gibbs samplers for linear mixed models with several heavy-tailed random-effect components and unknown tail parameters
papers.abstract: Linear mixed models with heavy-tailed random effects are widely used for robust Bayesian analysis of longitudinal data. We study the three-block Gibbs sampler for such models when the random effects are split into several components, such as random intercepts and slopes, each with its own scale and its own scale mixture of normals, when the tail parameters have priors on finite grids and are drawn jointly with the latent weights, and when the random-effects design is rank deficient, as when some subjects contribute a single observation. We give sufficient conditions for geometric ergodicity that attribute the rank deficiency to the components that cause it, and show that, under conditions on the gamma priors on the precision parameters, they hold for Student-t and slash random effects with individual weights, any grid of tail parameters and any design. The result extends to random-effect vectors whose coordinates share a weight, for subject-specific designs with known shape matrices. It justifies Monte Carlo standard errors for regression coefficients, log-scales and posterior probabilities of the tail parameters. Simulations show that the scale and the tail parameter can mix much more slowly than the regression coefficients, and an analysis of beta-HCG data illustrates the methods.

papers.title: Computing pro-$p$ Closures of Finitely Generated Subgroups of Closed Orientable Surface Groups
papers.abstract: Let $Γ_g$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus $g\geq2$, and let $p$ be a prime. For every finitely generated subgroup $H\leqΓ_g$ we give an algorithm which, given any finite generating set of $H$ by words in a standard generating set, outputs a finite set of words in the same alphabet that generates the pro-$p$ closure of $H$. This extends the computation of pro-$p$ closures in free groups by Ribes-Zalesskii and Margolis-Sapir-Weil.

papers.title: ScaleEvals: Scaling Generalist Policy Evaluation through Reset-Free Autonomous Play
papers.abstract: Real-world evaluation of generalist robot policies is bottlenecked by manual resets, human grading, and small fixed task suites with limited diagnostic coverage. We present ScaleEvals, a scalable reset-free protocol that evaluates policies through continuous physical play across a robot fleet. A VLM AutoPrompter generates scene-grounded tasks with difficulty estimates, language prompts, and skill tags, enabling performance analysis across diverse rollouts. A VLM AutoGrader assesses task progress, achieving 90.7% agreement with human graders. Scores are aggregated via a soft-win Bradley-Terry model, while tag-stratified ANOVA provides interpretable capability diagnostics. Across 3,000+ physical autonomous rollouts on DROID and YAM, ScaleEvals achieves 23.0 net rollouts/hr per station while reducing active human labor by 98%. By ranking five SOTA generalist policies, ScaleEvals correlates with held-out manual evaluation ranking on DROID (r=0.94, rho=0.90, p=0.018), and remains internally consistent on a second embodiment, YAM (r=0.839, rho=0.80). Beyond aggregate rankings, we observe behavioral compositionality: recombining verb-, skill-, and object-conditioned evidence predicts policy order on unseen prompts. Across 10 tasks and 240 prospective physical rollouts, we recover three-policy orderings of 96% pairwise concordance, demonstrating ScaleEvals can predict not just which policy leads, but where rankings reverse.

papers.title: An Isoperimetric Comparison for a Variational Threshold Associated with the Riemannian \(p\)-Laplacian
papers.abstract: We study a variational threshold $Λ_{p,M}(K)$ associated with a one-phase free boundary functional involving the Riemannian $p$-Dirichlet energy and a volume penalization on a bounded domain $K$ of a Riemannian manifold $M$. In the Euclidean case, this threshold is the smallest parameter for which the interior Bernoulli problem has a solution minimizing the energy; it bounds the Bernoulli constant from above, and the inequality is strict for balls. We characterize $Λ_{p,M}(K)$ as the infimum of a capacity-to-volume quotient and prove that this infimum is always attained. We then prove an isoperimetric comparison theorem: domination of the isoperimetric profile of $M$ by that of a model space implies a lower bound for $Λ_{p,M}(K)$ in terms of the threshold of a model geodesic ball. This extends a theorem of Daners and Kawohl. For geodesic balls in space forms, we give an explicit one-dimensional formula for the threshold and prove its strict monotonicity in the curvature, at fixed radius and at fixed volume. As applications, we obtain comparison results on compact manifolds with positive Ricci curvature, through the normalized Lévy--Gromov inequality, and on manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth, where the factor $\mbox{AVR}^{1/N}$ appears; a product-cylinder example shows that nonnegative Ricci curvature alone is not sufficient. Finally, we characterize the equality cases: geodesic balls in space forms, round spheres and geodesic balls in the Lévy--Gromov setting, Euclidean space and balls in the setting of Euclidean volume growth.

papers.title: Simulating Episodic Like Memory in Octopus: Breaking the Rules
papers.abstract: Episodic memory, which involves the recollection of past events, has been observed in several species including the invertebrate cuttlefish. In a subsequent experiment, episodic memory was not observed in the closely related octopus. Rather the octopus used simpler, cognitive rule-based strategies to gain access to food. Using a prior model of cuttlefish episodic-like memory, we replicated the octopus experiment. Under less challenging conditions, episodic memory and the simpler cognitive strategies all had positive gains. However, under more challenging conditions, which introduced the threat of predation, only the episodic memory model had positive gains. These results suggest that if challenged ecologically, it would be advantageous for octopus to use episodic-like memory. We discuss possible reasons for the behavioral discrepancies in these closely related cephalopods.

papers.title: The Effect of Security-Focused Prompts on Reported Findings: A Controlled Experiment on 400 AI-Generated Web Applications
papers.abstract: Agentic coding tools turn a specification into a running web application, so their defaults for authentication, sessions, input validation, and dependencies become its security posture. This study asks whether appending a fixed block of OWASP-aligned security requirements to the prompt changes what such tools produce, by how much, and with what side effects. Each of 100 frozen specifications was realized four times: two agentic tools (Claude Code, Codex CLI) crossed with two prompts sharing a byte-identical functional core, without (A) and with (B) the security block. A fixed static and dynamic pipeline scanned the 400 applications, yielding 6,721 triaged findings, analyzed with count and logistic mixed models and with a dependency diff. The block cut findings per application by a third (incidence-rate ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.60-0.71), equally through both tools, and roughly doubled the declared dependency surface, so variant-B applications carried more high-severity dependency advisories. Adjusted for that surface the advisory rate did not rise (flat per application, 18% lower in aggregate), while high-severity findings in first-party source fell by nearly half. Security-focused prompting is therefore an inexpensive and portable improvement, but it enlarges the dependency surface that has to be audited against it, an effect of library selection rather than of the security requirements themselves.

papers.title: A general triangle generation of the $d$-dimensional Genocchi numbers
papers.abstract: We establish a uniform recurrence relation for the rook numbers of generalized Genocchi boards of dimension $d\geq 3$. The recurrence for each row of the rook-number triangle is expressed in terms of the preceding row, with coefficients given by products of consecutive powers and finite sums involving Stirling numbers of the second kind. The proof decomposes the boundary of the board into blocks that correspond to the coordinates equal to 1. A coordinatewise counting argument then shows that the number of extensions of a fixed interior placement depends on a boundary partition only through the number of its blocks and the size of their union. We also express the coefficients as finite differences, recovering the previously established recurrences in dimensions three through five, and give the six-dimensional specialization. As a complementary result, we formulate an injection model that provides a direct bijective proof of a formerly established identification of the diagonal rook numbers with generalized Genocchi numbers.

papers.title: Failed Vertex Covering Graph Reconfiguration
papers.abstract: A failed vertex cover of a graph is a vertex set that leaves at least one edge uncovered. The associated token addition and removal (TAR) graph has the failed vertex covers as vertices, with two sets adjacent when they differ by one vertex. We characterize when two finite graphs have isomorphic failed vertex cover TAR graphs, allowing disconnected graphs, loops, and parallel edges.

papers.title: When Can an AI Agent Serve as a Model of Human Psychopathology?
papers.abstract: Language models and AI agents are increasingly described in psychiatric terms, such as anxious, depressed, addicted or helpless. A recent study even proposed language models as experimental systems for psychiatry and as a platform for piloting psychological treatments. We ask when an experiment on an AI agent can provide evidence about a specified human psychiatric process. A claim to such evidence has three parts. Something changed in the agent, and the agent's history caused the change. Nothing other than a process shared with people explains that change. The change matches one theory of the human process and not that theory's rivals. Psychiatry and its neighbouring fields have an evidence standard for each part, from the diagnostic manuals' rule for induced states, from clinical test scores and from animal models. We translate each standard into a criterion that a machine study can meet. For a language model the most critical alternative to a shared process is extrapolation from its training text, which already contains descriptions of how people respond to trauma and how they answer questionnaires. We show how to probe that alternative. Further, we audited forty-three published studies that apply psychiatric terms to a machine or induce a comparable state in one. Most compared the machine with an identical copy that had not gone through the history that induced the state. None excluded extrapolation from training text. Three tested a psychiatric theory against its rivals, and none of the three tests was conclusive. Until better evidence exists, a treatment pilot on a language model is best read as the model's forecast of patient response, and not as an experiment on a model organism. Evidence for a model organism will come from states induced by what happens to the machine, from experiments on its internal workings, and from tests on which rival theories disagree.

papers.title: Kinetic versus refill-zone uncertainty in predicted pr--burning of methane-oxygen rotating detonation rocket engines
papers.abstract: Rotating detonation rocket engines can lose performance when fresh propellant mixes with hot recirculated combustion products and ignites before the detonation wave arrives. Predicting this pre-burning requires fuel ignition chemistry at high pressure and in product-diluted mixtures, conditions most chemical kinetic mechanisms used in engine simulations were not developed for. With methane as our base fuel, we quantify how strongly predicted pre-burning depends on the choice of mechanism, test the mechanisms against published high-pressure ignition data, and use Bayesian methods to calibrate the most influential uncertain reaction and to assess which measurements would best improve the predictions. As the refill zone is represented by an idealized zero-dimensional model, our results should be viewed as relative comparisons rather than direct engine predictions. Five existing chemical kinetics mechanisms for methane combustion predict refill-zone ignition delays that differ by up to a factor of twenty. Mechanisms without methylperoxy chemistry, including two commonly used in engine simulations, do not reproduce the laboratory data below about 1150 K. Calibrating the CH${_3}$ + HO${_2}$ reaction against these data, while allowing for systematic differences between datasets, increases the relative importance of its chain-terminating channel, consistent with a direct rate measurement. With the data-consistent mechanisms, the remaining kinetic uncertainty in the predicted pre-burnt fraction is, in most cases, several times smaller than the uncertainty arising from the state of the refill zone: the temperature and composition of the recirculated products and the way fresh and burnt gases mix. Improved pre-burning predictions are therefore expected to depend mainly on accurately characterizing the refill zone.

papers.title: Occupancy Planar Patch: Incremental Probabilistic Bounded-Plane Reconstruction from LiDAR Data
papers.abstract: Online surface reconstruction from LiDAR scans requires observation models that respect the sensor's physical measurement geometry. Unlike unordered point sets, LiDAR returns carry anisotropic range noise along known rays, which also implicitly identify free space. We introduce the Occupancy Planar Patch (OPP), an incremental bounded planar patch representation that evaluates surface likelihoods and free space directly in range-space, allowing sensor noise, plane uncertainty, and ray clearance to be explicitly modelled during reconstruction. A single ray-to-patch association weight jointly updates plane geometry, refines surface boundaries, and blends camera imagery. The method is evaluated using six sequences from the Oxford Spires and Multi-Campus datasets. OPP achieves the highest precision and lowest reconstruction error among evaluated methods, while producing stored maps among the most compact. By conservatively admitting surfaces only where geometric evidence is certain, OPP prioritises structural precision over unconstrained completeness, which is well suited for architectural modelling. Geometric reconstruction operates in real time, requiring 81 ms per frame on a representative sequence, with texture projection adding 134 ms.

papers.title: Plan Big, Paint Small: Semantic-Aware Computation Allocation for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video diffusion streams a video chunk by chunk, but large AR models are too slow for real-time use. We ask where in an AR rollout a large model is actually needed. Pairing Krea-Realtime-14B with Self-Forcing-1.3B, which share their latent space and denoising schedule, we find that the order of the two models matters: when the 14B model generates only the first chunk and the 1.3B model continues, the rollout keeps 95\% of the 14B model's semantic advantage, whereas the reverse allocation keeps 16\% at about ten times the cost. The large model decides what the video shows; the small model only has to carry it forward. We turn this into BigSmall, a training-free planner--renderer sampler. The 14B model plans the opening chunk and sketches the chunks in which content changes, which preserves motion, and the 1.3B model renders the rest; a faster variant, BigSmall, plans only the opening chunk. A cross-model KV cache that is approximate, windowed and lazy lets the planner leave and re-enter the rollout at low cost. On VBench, BigSmall is $3.02\times$ faster than the 14B model at an unchanged semantic score and motion, and $1.55\times$ faster than SDVG, which lets the small model draft first; BigSmall reaches $3.77\times$ at the same semantic score, trading away 10\% of the motion. On minute-long videos (LoCoT2V-Bench), where the 14B model degrades when it reads its own long history, BigSmall is $3.14\times$ faster than the 14B model and scores higher ($+1.78$).`

papers.title: A Homotopic Kuratowski Theorem
papers.abstract: We prove that if a map from a graph G to a compact orientable surface, possibly with boundary, cannot be deformed so as to remove all crossings, then neither can its restriction to some subgraph of G with at most 72 vertices of degree other than two. On the sphere, this is Kuratowski's theorem; in contrast, minimal obstructions to embeddability in a surface grow with its genus. Our proof reduces the problem to planarity in a disk with order constraints, and identifies a condition under which this problem has small obstructions. Our main tool is a homotopic version of depth-first search trees, which underlie classical planarity tests and the extraction of Kuratowski subgraphs.

papers.title: Perturbed Nevo--Thangavelu maximal functions on two-step nilpotent groups
papers.abstract: Consider a step-two nilpotent Lie group $G$ identified with $\mathbb R^d\times \mathbb R^m$ in exponential coordinates. We study maximal operators associated with parabolic dilates of smooth convex hypersurfaces with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature in a tilted $d$-dimensional subspace of $G$. We focus on the low-rank regime, where the rank is determined by the group law and the tilt. When $m=1$, we determine the optimal range of $p$ for which the maximal operator is bounded on $L^p(G)$. For $m\ge2$, we characterize, in terms of a Łojasiewicz exponent, when the known necessary condition on $p$ is also sufficient.

papers.title: Data-Dependent Probability Estimation via Sample Amplification
papers.abstract: Can we estimate the probability of an event chosen after seeing the data, without using any fresh samples? Its empirical probability can be arbitrarily misleading, while learning the entire distribution to constant accuracy requires $Θ(d)$ samples on a domain of size $d$. We show that $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{d})$ samples suffice for constant mean squared error, provided the rule choosing the event is known. More generally, our estimator handles arbitrary $[0,1]$-valued queries and runs in polynomial time given evaluation access to the rule. This sample complexity matches the known lower bound up to logarithmic factors and resolves the open question posed by Feldman, Kale, Raman, Talwar, and Tewari (arXiv:2610.41244). Our estimation framework relies on a new combination of sample amplification (arXiv:1904.12053 and arXiv:2201.04315) with distribution learning via online optimization. Our estimator achieves mean squared error $O(d^{3/4}/n)$ when $d\leq n$ and $\widetilde{O}(d^{1/4}/\sqrt{n})$ when $d>n$. We complement this with a lower bound of $Ω(\min\{1,\sqrt{d}/n\})$ on the mean squared error. Using our framework, we also design an efficient estimator for data-dependent queries on Gaussian distributions with unknown mean and identity covariance. Finally, we show that a smoothed variant of the problem is much (exponentially) easier. For discrete distributions, if the sample size is chosen uniformly from $\{n,\ldots,2n-1\}$, then $n=O(\log d)$ suffices for constant mean squared error.

papers.title: Excited-state lifetime and decay mechanisms in erbium-doped ZBLAN using Variable Excited-State dual-Pump Analysis
papers.abstract: This work presents a new technique for measuring excited-state lifetimes of rare-earth ions. This technique is particularly powerful for states that are very short lived or have a low photon yield because their de-excitation pathways are dominated by non-radiative processes. The technique uses dual optical parametric oscillators, whose pulses are separated by a variable delay. It reconstructs the excited-state decay curve from a series of delayed fluorescence intensity spectra rather than directly recording the fluorescence decay as done in conventional time-resolved laser fluorescence spectroscopy. The power of the technique is demonstrated by measuring the lifetime of the short-lived $^4I_{9/2}$ level in Er$^{3+}$-doped ZBLAN, which is well-known for its low photon yield. The technique enables accurate measurement of its lifetime and suggests a new depopulating mechanism involving the $^4I_{9/2}$ level in ZBLAN glass. Its accuracy is validated by measuring the lifetime of the $^4F_{9/2}$ state achieving excellent agreement with conventional time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy measurements. The approach is well suited for measuring lifetimes ranging from the sub-microsecond to the millisecond range. It provides a versatile platform for investigating excited-state dynamics and energy-transfer processes in RE-doped materials.

papers.title: TOGO: Take One Image Editor, Get One Video Editor for Free
papers.abstract: Instruction-based image editors are trained on millions of edit pairs and follow instructions far more reliably than current video editors. We show that this ability can be transferred to video editing without any training. Our key observation is that a growing number of image editors and video generators share the same latent space. Their velocity fields can therefore be combined at sampling time: the difference between the editor's velocity under the instruction and under a neutral prompt, which we call the \emph{edit velocity}, can be added to the sampler of a video model. Added naively, however, it blurs the video, alters the background and flickers. An analysis of the edit velocity explains why. It is small and reliable only at coarse scales and high noise levels, not concentrated on the edited object, and uncorrelated across frames. From these properties, we derive a simple guidance operator that amplifies the edit velocity and restricts it in noise level, space, and time. The video model then turns the incoherent per-frame signal into a temporally coherent edit. Our method, TOGO, combines Qwen-Image-Edit with the Wan2.1 video model without training or fine-tuning. On FiVE-Bench, it raises the edit success rate from 47.0\% (the same video model without the editor) to 65.6\%, above the best published method (59.2\%). At the same time, it maintains the background PSNR and obtains the best LPIPS and SSIM of all methods. Because the video editor is assembled at inference time, it can be upgraded to any newer image editor that shares the latent space with no cost.

papers.title: Targeted In-Context Poisoning of Tabular Foundation Models: An Empirical Study
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) predict the label of a query row conditioned on a context of labelled rows, without training on them. Drawn from operational data, the context becomes an attack surface. We study targeted in-context poisoning in its simplest form: an attacker with write access to the context's source places exact copies of a target row there with the wrong label. On 30 OpenML datasets for binary classification, one such poison row flips on average 53% (TabICL) and 65% (TabPFN) of the predictions correct without attack, and three poison rows flip almost all. The same copy with the true label flips almost none, and performance on the remaining rows hardly changes. Predictions flip by two routes: in TabICL, the target row's embedding rotates towards the mean of the wrong class; in TabPFN, the poison row pulls genuine rows of the wrong class along. The TFMs thus infer soundly, but from forged evidence. Predictions of trained models flip as well: almost always for a random forest, for CatBoost as often as for the TFMs, hardly for a logistic regression. New with TFMs is not the kind of vulnerability but the timing: the data take effect at the moment of prediction, not through training, and a poison row in a live context can be deleted afterwards. Three established requirements must therefore cover the context: access control for its source, traceability per prediction, which can also deter, and validation at prediction time. A detection mechanism shows how such validation can work.

papers.title: Intertwined Magneto-Structural Criticality Driving Heterogeneous Collective-Pseudospin Dynamics in Sr2IrO4
papers.abstract: Correlated quantum phenomena arising from spin-orbit-coupled degrees of freedom provide foundational paradigms in emerging quantum technologies and spin-based functionalities. Elucidating the cooperative behaviors of these systems requires a precise probing of their intertwined magnetic and structural configurations. Using complementary resonant X-ray diffraction and high-energy total scattering measurements on single crystals of Sr2IrO4, we observe that spontaneous structural distortions scale quadratically with the magnetic order parameter. Importantly, the lattice distortion inherits the characteristic 2D XY -like critical behavior of the underlying antiferromagnetic order. X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS) reveals multiscale, temperature- and wave-vector-dependent magnetic dynamics characterized by compressed-exponential relaxation and signatures of critical slowing down near the magnetic transition. These findings suggest the role of spin-orbit coupling and local structural distortions as the possible mechanism orchestrating such unconventional dynamics.

papers.title: A Hybrid Multi-Goal Path Planning Framework for Powered Wheelchairs in Dynamic Environments: From Simulation to Real-World Validation
papers.abstract: Autonomous powered wheelchairs (PWs) operating in human-centered environments must combine efficient multi-destination path planning with continuous collision avoidance strategies in the presence of static and dynamic obstacles. This study presents a hybrid framework integrating Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP)-based global task ordering, Potential-Field (PF) guidance, and local Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) and A-star (A*) planners. PF guidance transfers global path information to local planners, helping the robot stay aligned with the global path during obstacle avoidance. Local planning is enhanced with direction-aware, extended-neighborhood A* or RRT using environment-aware sampling and two-step extension. The TSP-PF-RRT and TSP-PF-A* methods are evaluated in normal, crowded, and extra-crowded simulation environments using point-based and elliptical robot models. The elliptical model accounts for platform dimensions during collision avoidance phase. Hardware tests on the physical PW use motion capture (MoCap) for ground-truth measurements, while outside-MoCap experiments rely on onboard LiDAR and RGB-D sensing. Results show that incorporating the wheelchair geometry changes the observed collision behavior, yielding comparable collision avoidance performance between the two hybrid planners under the elliptical model.

papers.title: Expressive Shallow Networks for Physics-Informed Learning: Why Curvature-Aware Optimization and FP64 Are Not Enough
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often struggle with high-frequency and high-order partial differential equations (PDEs) due to optimization stiffness and spectral bias, despite possessing sufficient approximation capacity. Existing remedies, including modified feature representations, domain decomposition, higher floating-point precision, and curvature-aware optimizers, can improve convergence but largely act as workarounds for optimization difficulties arising from deep architectures rather than addressing their underlying source. We investigate Physics-Informed Shallow Universal Polynomial Networks (PI-SUPNs), which replace deep nonlinear compositions with learnable polynomial expansions, retaining high approximation capacity within a shallow computational graph. On a high-frequency Helmholtz benchmark, PI-SUPNs are the only architecture to successfully recover the solution, while all competing models fail even under FP64 precision and curvature-aware optimization. However, experiments on higher vibrational modes of a fourth-order Euler-Bernoulli beam reveal that architectural improvements alone are insufficient: accurate solutions require the combination of PI-SUPNs, FP64 precision, and curvature-aware optimization. Additionally, Allen-Cahn experiments show that PI-SUPNs achieve lower solution and derivative errors at reduced computational cost, with more favorable loss landscapes than competing architectures. We also establish quasi-local approximation properties and spline-based convergence bounds for SUPNs. Our results show that shallow network architectures are an important mechanism for improving physics-informed trainability, but accurate solutions to the most challenging PDEs can still require FP64 precision and curvature-aware optimization.

papers.title: Improved bounds for the binary Chowla conjecture
papers.abstract: For the Möbius function $μ$ and every fixed $0 < ε< 1$, we prove \[ \sum_{n \le x} μ(n) μ(n + 1) \ll_ε \frac{x}{(\log x)^{1 - ε}}. \] This improves on OpenAI's recent bound of $x/(\log x)^c$, where $c > 0$ is a tiny absolute constant. The proof echoes the graph expansion framework of Helfgott, Radziwill, and Pilatte on the logarithmic Chowla conjecture, earlier Fourier analytic methods of Matomäki, Radziwill, and Tao on the Chowla conjecture on average, as well as work of Teräväinen and the author for Möbius on shifted primes. This also yields an improved result, \[ \sum_{p \le x} μ(p + 2) \ll_ε \frac{π(x)}{(\log x)^{1/2 - ε}}. \] Specifically, we refine the determinant approach from the Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors. We replace the averaged prime weights of Lü-Wang-Wu with an exact partition of prime intervals. Once sieving out exceptional integers, this enables uniform cancellation with arbitrary log power savings.

papers.title: A Characterized Softmax for Distributing Standing Across Multiple Affiliations
papers.abstract: Cooperative game theory answers canonical questions on payoff allocation (Shapley, Owen), interaction attribution (Grabisch-Roubens, Faith-Shap), and coalition formation and stability. None answers a fourth question that arises whenever players carry known, overlapping group tags fixed independently of the game: how should a player's standing be distributed across the groups it already belongs to? We call this membership attribution, formalize it, and give a complete characterization of its solution. The direct, ratio-based answer is provably invalid whenever a player's group-level signals have mixed sign --- a common, structurally unavoidable case. We propose a restricted-domain softmax construction instead, and prove that, for any player satisfying a precisely defined richness condition on the group structure, it is the unique such map, up to a temperature parameter, satisfying five requirements. A sixth requirement fixes the sign of this temperature; a seventh, shown independent of the rest via an explicit counterexample, forces one shared temperature across all eligible players. A worked example on an exact cooperative game confirms the applicable requirements numerically and shows the construction degrades gracefully, valid but uninformative, when a player's evidence fails to distinguish between its groups.

papers.title: Tight Lipschitz Hardness for Solving Random Polynomial Equations
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of solving $n$ polynomial equations in $d$ real variables: $F_1({\boldsymbol x})=0, \ldots, F_n({\boldsymbol x})=0$, with unknowns ${\boldsymbol x}=(x_1, \ldots, x_d)$ satisfying the normalization constraint $\|{\boldsymbol x}\|=1$, when the polynomials are i.i.d. realization of a rotationally invariant Gaussian process. In previous work (Montanari, Subag, 2023), we developed an iterative algorithm that attempts to minimize the energy function $H({\boldsymbol x})=\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})\|^2/2$ (with ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})=(F_i({\boldsymbol x}):i\le n)$), using first and second order information (gradient and Hessian of $H$) at a sequence of query points ${\boldsymbol x}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol x}_k$. Here, we prove a lower bound on the minimum energy achieved by any algorithm that is Lipschitz continuous in the coefficients of the polynomials $F_i$. We prove that the lower bound matches the the energy achieved by the algorithm in (Montanari, Subag, 2023), hence characterizing the degree of accuracy to which the system of equations ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})={\boldsymbol 0}$ can be solved by Lipschitz algorithms. Our results imply that, for certain choices of the distribution of the polynomials $F_i$, solutions exist with high probability but Lipschitz algorithms fails to find near-solutions, even in a very weak sense. Namely, if ${\boldsymbol x}^{alg}$ is the output of a Lipschitz algorithm, then $\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}^{alg})\|^2\ge \varepsilon {\mathbb E}[\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}_0)\|^2]$ (for ${\boldsymbol x}_0$ a non-random point on the unit sphere) with high probability for some $\varepsilon>0$. The proof is based on techniques developed in the context of spin glass theory.

papers.title: On a class of affine Temperley-Lieb modules
papers.abstract: We prove that the class of all affine Temperley-Lieb modules, equipped with the recently introduced "diagrammatic" tensor product, forms a quasitensor (i.e. monoidal braided) category. When the Temperley-Lieb parameter $q$ is not a root of unity, we consider the infinite subcategory generated by the simple quotients of reducible standard modules, and we argue that it is a semi-simple ribbon category. We present some evidence that, under the fusion rules and the associativity maps, each simple module in this subcategory is equivalent to a pair of $U_q(sl_2)$ heighest-weight modules.

papers.title: Verification and Evaluation of A Comprehensive Quantum Simulation Compiler
papers.abstract: Hamiltonian simulation is a central application of quantum computing, yet most existing compilers offer no machine-checked guarantee that the circuits they produce approximate the intended evolution. The previous QBlue compiler verifies a Hamiltonian simulation compiler containing only Trotter-based algorithms. It takes a Hamiltonian written over Pauli strings, a simulation time, and an error bound, and produces a circuit or analog schedule that is proven, in the Rocq proof assistant, to approximate the ideal time evolution within that bound and proves a single end-to-end error bound that composes the errors of the individual stages; the compiler uses it to select, by resource estimation, the cheapest algorithm that meets the user's bound. This paper advances the verification efforts with two further steps. First, we extend QBlue to $\textsf{QBlue}_{\texttt{BE}}$ by verifying another important compilation method for Hamiltonian simulation: block-encoding-based (BE-based) algorithms. Second, we empirically evaluate 279 Hamiltonian simulation programs against the state-of-the-art BE-based compiler, PennyLane. For many programs, our compiler shows a $94\%$ gate reduction compared to PennyLane. Additionally, we also discover issues and bugs in PennyLane. We also compare Trotter- and BE-based algorithms, providing a practical comparison for the long-standing debate over which algorithms perform better. Our results surprisingly show that Trotter-based algorithms may gain a practical advantage, even though BE algorithms have a theoretical advantage.

papers.title: Knowing What You Carry: Scalable Physics-Anchored World Models for Robotic Planning with Liquid Payloads
papers.abstract: Payload-carrying robots, such as delivery robots and autonomous trucks, must choose motions that keep them and their payload safe, so their planners predict the outcome of each candidate motion. Modern planners compare thousands of candidates per step on a GPU, using world models such as batched simulators or learned predictors. Most of them assume a rigid payload, but a liquid payload keeps moving after a maneuver, and its state is rarely measured. Near a safety limit, small prediction errors can make an unsafe plan look safe. Coupled fluid simulations are accurate but too costly for every candidate, while low-order slosh models are cheap but accurate only away from resonance. We study this trade-off on a ground vehicle with a partly filled tank near its rollover limit. First, we build PLiMB (Parallel Liquid-MultiBody), a GPU-parallel slosh simulator that, to our knowledge, couples FLIP liquid two-way with many multibody vehicles for the first time. It provides training data and a high-fidelity reference. Second, we propose a scalable physics-anchored world model that combines a modal-slosh and roll prior, an estimate of the hidden liquid state from the vehicle's own motion history (no sensor in the tank), and a learned correction. Without simulating the fluid, it scores thousands of candidate plans in one batched pass within a 20 Hz control tick on one GPU. We judge each world model by the plans it leads a planner to choose. Near the rollover limit, planners that treat the liquid as a rigid payload or use published low-order slosh models repeatedly pick unsafe plans when a safe one exists. Ours never does in our standard tank and makes about half as many in a wide tank whose sloshing mode lies in the maneuver band. There, the liquid state left by earlier driving can change the best plan, and reading it from the vehicle's history halves our model's near-limit prediction error.

papers.title: Frequency-Domain Identification of Passive Discrete-Time Systems via Sequential Convex Programming
papers.abstract: This paper considers identification of passive discrete-time linear time-invariant systems from frequency-response data. A prescribed passivity margin and spectral-radius bound are enforced by a descriptor-form linear matrix inequality that is affine in the system realization matrices and storage certificate. A damped Gauss--Newton sequential convex programming method jointly refines the realization matrices through strongly convex semidefinite subproblems, with Armijo backtracking decreasing the fitting error while preserving both guarantees at every iterate. For unstructured identification, the number of decision variables is reduced without changing the attainable transfer matrices by normalizing the descriptor and certificate matrices and restricting the dynamics matrix to upper Hessenberg form. Numerical results on randomized passive plants show that the proposed method achieves the lowest mean frequency-response fitting error among several passivity-enforcing methods, at both full and reduced model orders.

papers.title: Multi-Epoch Batch Least-Squares Positioning on the Lunar Surface Using LuGRE GPS L1 C/A Pseudorange Measurements
papers.abstract: The Lunar GNSS Receiver Experiment (LuGRE) mission captured Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals in the lunar region, yielding position, velocity, and timing estimates. Analysis of onboard lunar-surface position estimates shows kilometer-level positioning errors due to the long propagation distances, limited measurements, and unfavorable GNSS geometry. This paper presents time-multiplexed positioning using publicly available LuGRE L1 C/A pseudorange measurements. The proposed approach accumulates measurements by exploiting the receiver's stationary position in the Lunar-Centered Lunar-Fixed frame after landing. The effects of the number of accumulated epochs, receiver altitude constraint using coarse a-priori information, straight-line tangential altitude threshold, and minimum number of measurements required per epoch are examined. Compared with single-epoch least-squares positioning, this approach substantially improves positioning performance using single-band, single-constellation signals. With selected combinations of these parameters, batches of epochs randomly selected from multiple operations yield 100-m-level accuracy at the 67th percentile.

papers.title: Louis Bachelier's Theorie de la speculation: Circulation and Reception
papers.abstract: Louis Bachelier's Theorie de la speculation (1900) introduced a probabilistic model of Brownian motion in a study of financial fluctuations, five years before Einstein's physical theory. By connecting probability distributions with the heat equation and studying speculation and option valuation, Bachelier anticipated central developments in probability, physics, and mathematical finance. How widely did the thesis circulate before its broader significance was recognized? Drawing on library correspondence, surviving copies, accession registers, provenance marks, historical catalogues, and acquisition lists, this article reconstructs its international circulation and reception in two forms: the separate Gauthier-Villars dissertation and its publication in the Annales scientifiques de l'Ecole normale superieure. It identifies thirty-eight foreign academic institutions in the official dissertation exchange network for 1900 and documents its operation. University exchanges, commercial purchases, journal distribution, and personal presentations provided complementary channels. American holdings reveal its geographical reach, including receipt at Cornell in April 1900. Contemporary reviews and subsequent uses establish selective engagement in mathematics, actuarial science, and economics, including transmission without attribution. An examination of probability composition and diffusion clarifies the thesis's place in the history of stochastic processes and its relationship to physical Brownian motion. Columbia's journal volume, accessioned in 1901 and borrowed by Mandelbrot in 1961, connects early dissemination with renewed interest. Distinguishing availability from documented reading and use, the study shows that delayed recognition coexisted with early international circulation and a dispersed readership across scientific traditions.

papers.title: Language models compress human preference geometry while political structure remains prompt-sensitive
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to construct synthetic publics. Prior work has documented errors in individual responses, population heterogeneity, and prompt robustness, but whether these failures reflect a common loss of fidelity or distinct properties of synthetic populations remains unclear. We tested this using matched pairwise policy choices from 1,991 Chilean, 843 French, and 434 Brazilian adults replayed through three open-weight model families. Across a 27-condition Chilean grid and cross-country factorial replications, no condition jointly reproduced individual choices, population heterogeneity, and political organization. The most consistent result was compression of the latent preference space: synthetic participant variance was only 0.4-10.5% of the corresponding human reference in the primary comparisons and remained below human variance in all 270 matched refits. Political structure was much more sensitive to how choices were elicited. Reversing proposal position changed 12.3-31.2% of decoded choices. Explicitly labeling the endpoints of the numeric left-right self-placement scale changed 20.5-28.1% of choices and moved an independent proposal-level measure of left-right cleavage toward the human pattern in all three settings. Yet matched agreement improved by only 3.1-4.2 percentage points and participant geometry remained compressed. In Chile, the same intervention compressed the synthetic population further. These results separate political legibility from population fidelity: language models can recover salient political divisions while failing to preserve the breadth of human preference variation. Synthetic-public fidelity is therefore a property of the checkpoint, prompt, and setting, not of a checkpoint alone, and must be evaluated separately at individual, population, and political-structure levels.

papers.title: A unipotent witness: vanishing orders of word maps on SU(2) and lengths in the lower central series
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge2$, $k\ge2$ and $1\ne w\inγ_k(F_n)$, the $k$-th term of the lower central series of the free group of rank $n$. We prove that a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$ has at least $2k$ syllables, so $w$ has word length at least $2k$; the previous linear bound, due to Malestein and Putman, is $k$. For $1\ne w\in[F_n,F_n]$ we also prove that the word map of $w$ on $SU(2)$ or $SO(3)$ vanishes at the identity to order at most $T/2$, where $T$ is the number of syllables of a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$, with equality for $[x_1,x_2]$ and for a word with six syllables. Both proofs evaluate $w$ at unipotent matrices $I+tN_i$, with $N_i$ nilpotent of rank one, and compare the degree of the trace of the resulting matrix $M(t)\in SL_2(\mathbb{Z}[t])$ with the order of vanishing of $M(t)-I$ at $t=0$.

papers.title: The JWST Resolved Stellar Populations Early Release Science Program. X. Cross-Observatory Proper Motion Measurements with HST and JWST
papers.abstract: We present the first absolute systemic proper motion (PM) of a galaxy measured by combining Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and JWST imaging. The PM of WLM, an isolated dwarf galaxy at $\sim$1 Mpc, is measured against background galaxies with Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS) F814W imaging from 2015 and 2024 and NIRCam imaging from 2022 and 2024. The two ACS epochs give a systemic PM of $(μ_α^*, μ_δ) = (+0.087 \pm 0.019, -0.079 \pm 0.017)$ mas yr$^{-1}$ from 145 galaxies over 8.93 years, which agrees with previous Gaia-based PMs to within 0.4$σ$ and is the most precise PM of WLM. For the HST-to-JWST PMs, we fit each NIRCam detector separately, match the point-spread functions with empirically derived convolution kernels, and correct biases with injected galaxies. With an F090W second epoch, the PM is $(+0.081 \pm 0.045, -0.113 \pm 0.046)$ mas yr$^{-1}$ from 43 galaxies over 7.02 years, which, like the F150W PM, agrees with HST-to-HST over the same area to within 1$σ$, while F200W differs by $\sim$2$σ$. The long-wavelength F250M and F430M PMs are consistent to within 1$σ$, though less precise. Fewer galaxies can be used at wavelengths farther from F814W. A cross-observatory systematic of $\sim$0.05 mas yr$^{-1}$ cannot be ruled out over 7 years. At equal baselines, an F090W second epoch is at least as precise as our second ACS epoch over the same area. We recommend the NIRCam filter closest in wavelength to the first-epoch filter, though the long-wavelength filters show promise for closer targets or longer baselines.

papers.title: Statistical inference under response-adaptive experimental designs: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Response-adaptive designs, including bandit-based approaches, update treatment allocation using accrued outcomes. In this paper, we systematically reviewed how studies in health and biostatistics conducted and evaluated inference under these designs. We searched six databases for studies published from January 2010 through October 2025. Of 774 records identified, 36 studies met the inclusion criteria. We summarized them using study-level counts and structured narrative comparisons, with reporting guided by PRISMA 2020. Most studies focused on methods or designs. Evidence supporting inference came mainly from theory and simulation. Among studies for which each metric was relevant, 26 of 32 numerically evaluated power, 23 of 32 type I error, eight of 35 estimator bias, and five of 12 interval coverage. These findings suggest that studies more often quantified power and type I error than estimator bias or interval coverage. Evaluations of adaptive allocation should also examine estimation and interval performance when these are relevant to the study objective.

papers.title: Beyond Relevance: An Empirical Study of Multimodal LLMs for Diversity-Aware Recommendation Reranking
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as promising rerankers for recommendation, yet most existing approaches rely on textual item descriptions and primarily focus on relevance. In visually oriented domains such as video streaming, item images provide complementary signals that may also inform recommendation diversity. This raises two questions: when does visual information improve recommendation quality, and can multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) enhance relevance and diversity simultaneously? We investigate these questions through a training-free, diversity-aware multimodal reranking framework that jointly incorporates item images, textual metadata, and user interaction histories. We conduct an empirical study across three public Amazon Review datasets and an industrial Amazon Prime Video dataset, using both open-source and proprietary MLLMs. Our results reveal substantial domain-dependent effects: adding visual information yields up to 121.9% relative improvement in NDCG@5 on Prime Video, while producing limited or inconsistent gains on product recommendation datasets. Furthermore, MLLM-based reranking improves both relevance and category-diversity-sensitive ranking quality over a sequential recommendation baseline, achieving up to 71.0% improvement in NDCG@5 and 14.1% in $α$-NDCG@5 on Prime Video. These findings highlight the conditional value of visual information and the potential of training-free MLLMs for relevance- and diversity-aware recommendation reranking.

papers.title: A scalar arterial input function does not uniquely determine the perfusion residue: Theory and phantom MRI
papers.abstract: Purpose: To relate the residue function of tracer kinetic models to blood velocity and cross-sectional tracer distributions at the arterial inlet, and show that a cross-sectionally averaged arterial input function (AIF) does not uniquely determine the residue. Theory and Methods: For steady laminar flow without radial diffusion, the residue function referenced to the cross-sectionally averaged inlet AIF was analytically derived from the velocity and inlet tracer distributions. In a straight tube with parabolic flow, two nonnegative inlet profiles sharing one measured AIF were compared for gamma-variate and rectangular arterial spin labeling (ASL) inputs. A straight-tube phantom was imaged at 3 T during gadolinium bolus passage, with uniform fills as controls. Results: In the phantom, enhancement during bolus arrival was greater near the lumen center than near the wall at all 11 stations and for all three boluses, whereas uniform gadolinium fills showed no such pattern. In the tube model, the two profiles produced tissue curves differing by up to 23.3% of the uniform-inlet peak and 0.30 s in time to peak for the gamma-variate input, and by 33.3% for ASL labels shorter than the fastest transit time. Their residues differed in initial amplitude and normalized temporal shape. Conclusion: Identical AIFs can produce different tissue concentration curves, depending on the spatial distributions of inlet tracer concentration and arterial flow velocity. Consequently, the residue-AIF tracer kinetic models may not be consistent with fluid mechanics or interpreted as tissue flow.

papers.title: Using the Tool That Replaces You: Generative AI and the Adoption Bind among Bangladeshi Platform Freelancers
