By measuring the alignment signal separately around overdensities and underdensities, we show that each of these alignments has the scale and environmental dependence of a linear response to the cosmic tidal field; a response purely quadratic in the Gaussian tidal field, as in classic tidal torque theory is ruled out.

papers.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
papers.abstract: Neural-network quantum states (NQSs) exhibit a disparity in converging to the ground state during energy minimization: while the energy converges quadratically with the error in the variational wave function, other observables converge only linearly, which limits the accuracy of physical predictions. Here we show how to close this gap by introducing a new algorithm that improves the accuracy of NQSs. Our method, termed dynamical averaging, estimates expectation values by averaging over a state (or observable) evolved in real-time. Using insights from quantum information, we prove an up-to-quadratic suppression of error in arbitrary ground state observables, thus matching the fast convergence of the energy. Importantly, this improved accuracy requires neither further energy minimization nor increased model complexity, but rather exploits the effect of randomization on quantum states. We demonstrate dynamical averaging on non-integrable spin models, where it accelerates convergence and substantially reduces errors in observables.

papers.title: Superluminal propagation in the magnetic NED reconstruction of the extremal Dymnikova black hole
papers.abstract: We reconstruct the magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics (NED) source of the Dymnikova geometry on the branch \(\Iinv>0\) and analyze its electromagnetic perturbations on the fixed background. The reconstruction does not admit a Maxwell limit. The extraordinary characteristic cone gives a transverse speed \(v_\perp^2=(3u-5)/2\), with \(u=r^3/P^3\), which becomes superluminal for \(r>r_{\rm lum}=(7/3)^{1/3}P\). The principal system is pointwise hyperbolic in the finite exterior \(r\ge r_e\), with positive local quadratic energy, but not uniformly hyperbolic up to spatial infinity. The radial effective potential admits an exact reduction, \(V_{\rm em}=f\ell(\ell+1)\mathcal{A}/r^2+ff_{,r}q +f^2(q_{,r}+\frac34q^2)\), behaves as \(V_0\proptoε^2\) near the horizon, and grows as \(27r^4/(4P^6)\) at infinity. It is numerically positive on a fine grid up to \(r=50P\). The Dymnikova reconstruction does not satisfy the hypotheses of the Tomizawa--Suzuki theorem, since it lacks a Maxwell limit, yet it still produces superluminal extraordinary photons. The reconstructed NED branch is therefore mathematically consistent as a source of the Dymnikova background, but not causally acceptable with respect to the physical metric in the asymptotic region. The global positivity of the effective potential and the quasinormal spectrum are left as open problems.

papers.title: MM-SystemOneBias: Evaluating Bias in Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models
papers.abstract: Reliable multimodal decision models must preserve semantic decisions across presentation changes, ignore irrelevant additions, and distinguish supporting from conflicting text, yet existing studies examine decision-interface biases and multimodal behavior separately without matched backbone comparisons. We introduce \textbf{MM-SystemOneBias}, evaluating 8 decision models and 5 backbones on 5,323 original instances across 9 datasets, 11 task scenarios, and 6 interventions: option order, option label, external judgment, image--text description, irrelevant information, and rating scale. Decision models remain sensitive across interventions: incorrect external judgments introduce errors in 20.14\% of originally correct responses on average, conflicting descriptions redirect decisions even when rejected in isolation, and answer probabilities on unchanged decisions show mean absolute shifts of 2.92\% to 8.97\%. Relative to backbones, decision models improve presentation, rating-scale, and irrelevant-information stability, yet face a trade-off on added text: they lose less accuracy to misleading cues while gaining less from correct judgments and often losing accuracy under consistent descriptions. These findings highlight visual grounding and probability robustness as key priorities.The code and dataset is available at https://github.com/ALIENS32/MM-SystemOneBias

papers.title: A time-domain adversarial example demonstrating the failure of $H^1$ elements in $a$-$ϕ$ electromagnetic simulation
papers.abstract: Frequently, $H^1$ continuous finite elements are used in computational electromagnetics despite it being widely known that such an interpolation is not guaranteed to furnish reliable approximations of solutions to general initial/boundary value problems. It is mathematically more natural to use $H(\text{Curl})$ elements (edge elements) than $H^1$ elements, since the former form part of a discrete complex that respects the differential-geometric structure of Maxwell's equations while the latter do not. However, most work discussing the failure of $H^1$ elements for electromagnetics is esoteric and concrete examples demonstrating the clear advantage of edge elements are generally restricted to quasi-static, frequency-domain, or eigenvalue problems. In this work, we summarize essential facts regarding $H^1$ and $H(\text{Curl})$ elements and present a physically feasible yet intentionally adversarial time-domain eddy-current example demonstrating the failure of gauge-penalized $H^1$ elements in an $a$-$ϕ$ formulation compared to explicit gauge-free mixed scalar/edge $H^1/H(\text{Curl})$ elements. The results indicate that edge elements can be used to furnish reasonable results for general loading conditions, whereas penalized $H^1$ elements fail (e.g., converge to an incorrect state) even with mesh refinement.

papers.title: Complete Test Suites for Effectful Automata
papers.abstract: Complete test suites for automata are (finite) sets of words that enable testing an implementation against a specification: when a (black-box) automaton passes the test suite, completeness guarantees that it is equivalent to the specification on all (infinitely many) words. A well-known method for constructing complete test suites for deterministic automata is the W-method, used in conformance testing and automata learning. Based on a recent categorical generalisation of the W-method, we propose a framework for~the construction and analysis of test suites for a certain class of effectful automata defined by commutative monads. By working in the Eilenberg-Moore category of the associated monad at hand, we obtain a generic notion of effectful W-method, together with a completeness theorem. We show how to apply the framework and derive complete test suites for non-deterministic and weighted automata.

papers.title: GLiDE: A Fast, Calibrated Decision Model Distilled from Reasoning Teachers
papers.abstract: Decision models score candidate answers in a single forward pass, but the intermediate reasoning that improves decision quality adds latency. We introduce GLiDE, a family of decision models from 0.4B to 27B parameters that distills reasoning into single-pass inference. Building on Qwen's hybrid architecture, GLiDE removes causal masking from full-attention layers so that context, question and candidate answers interact bidirectionally. It is trained with soft-target distillation from multiple teachers, including a reasoning model, and progressive post-training on diverse decision tasks. On the Hugging Face Decision Index, each of the five GLiDE models outscores every alternative of equal or smaller size. GLiDE V1.2 (27B) ranks first on edition 0.4.1 (22 October 2026) with a hidden-set score of 71.52, 2.0% calibration error and 92.9 ms median latency on one GPU, and shares first place on all three versions of the Artificial Analysis Decision Index. Both leaderboards are run by their maintainers on closed test sets. With checkpoint averaging and recurrent depth, GLiDE 27B reaches 73.37.

papers.title: Hereditary permutations for simple types revisited: A baby case for University Algebra
papers.abstract: It is a classical result that the definable isomorphisms of the simply typed $λ$-calculus with function types are exactly the hereditary permutations, and that they are generated by $A \to B \to C \cong B \to A \to C$ and congruence. We give a new proof of this result that stays inside $β$-normal $η$-long typed terms and uses no completeness theorem: an induction that descends through both components of an isomorphism at once. It proceeds by showing that both components are linear terms: relevance follows from one of the inverse equations, and no copying from relevance of the other component. We then go one level up and prove a coherence theorem: two derivations of an isomorphism denote the same isomorphism if and only if they are equal modulo an explicit list of equations (groupoid laws, functoriality, involution, naturality and the braid equation), so these equations present the groupoid of isomorphisms, a hereditary version of the Coxeter presentation of the symmetric groups. All results are formalised in Agda, on intrinsically typed syntax with hereditary substitution, without postulates. The work is a case study for the syntactic completeness conjecture of University Algebra, a proposed solution of Tarski's high school algebra problem using dependent types, whose semantic counterpart is open. We explain the motivation and which parts of the method we expect to carry over.

papers.title: The Rate of Convergence of Empirical $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein Distances
papers.abstract: We study empirical convergence rates for $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distances $D_{p,q}$ for arbitrary real exponents $p>0$ and $q\ge1$. Let $μ$ and $ν$ be probability measures on compact metric spaces $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$, and let $\widehatμ_n$ and $\widehatν_m$ be their empirical measures, constructed from independent i.i.d. samples of sizes $n$ and $m$. If the spaces $\mathcal{X},\,\mathcal{Y}$ are compact subsets of the Euclidean spaces $\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$, respectively, we obtain an upper bound of order $(n\wedge m)^{-(p\wedge2)/((d_x\wedge d_y)\vee 2(p\wedge2))}$ on the plug-in error of $D_{p,q}^p(\widehatμ_n,\widehatν_m)$ in expectation, up to a logarithmic factor at the critical dimension $d_x\wedge d_y=2(p\wedge2)$. On Euclidean balls, this rate is sharp up to the logarithmic factor. More generally, we show that the same upper bound holds when one space is a compact subset of a complete, connected $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold and the other has polynomial covering numbers, with $d_x\wedge d_y$ replaced by $d$. Earlier works on $(2,2)$-GW, $(2,1)$-GW and other even-order cases rely on variational representations of GW distances that are specific to their exponents. We instead reduce the plug-in error to an analysis of empirical processes through local duality, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Nonstandard quantum statistics for strongly correlated systems: Superexclusion in momentum space and comparison with exact results
papers.abstract: We analyze in detail nonstandard statistics for strongly correlated fermions, which comprise the statistical spin liquid (SSL) and model non-Fermi liquid (NFL) cases. Both of those cases are based on the total exclusion of local doubly occupancies ($the~superexclusion$) either in real space (SSL case) or in reciprocal ($\mathbf{k}$) space (NFL). The results obtained on a purely physical ground are supplemented with the exact analysis of those coming from microscopic Hubbard-like model in $\mathbf{k}$ space. Specifically, we discuss the transmutation of those statistics to that of localized magnetic moments, as well as the transformation of the Fermi liquid into a strongly correlated fermionic liquid or Mott insulating state; the latter taking place for the half-filled-band situation. The role of exclusion of double occupancies in either real or reciprocal space in the appearance of the correlated phase is stressed. Conclusions concerning the universal features of the models, independence of either the real- or $\mathbf{k}$-space representation, are also discussed. One of those is the boson to fermion statistics transmutation which in the limit of strong repulsive interboson interaction leads to the particle localization instead to the Bose-Einstein condensation. The superexclusion statistics represents the infinite-interaction limit of the $\mathbf{k}$-Hubbard model.

papers.title: FoldSim: Scaling Cycle-Exact RTL Simulation with Hierarchical Folding and Static Scheduling
papers.abstract: RTL simulation is essential for hardware design and verification, yet its execution time grows rapidly with design scale and complexity. CPU- and GPU-based simulators exploit parallelism to accelerate RTL evaluation, but achieving high simulation throughput for large designs remains challenging. FPGA-based simulators offer higher throughput by mapping RTL computations directly onto hardware, but their scalability is constrained by FPGA resource capacity. We present FoldSim, an automated framework that enables cycle-exact simulation of large RTL designs on a single FPGA through hierarchical folding. FoldSim maps instances across the design hierarchy onto shared logic while maintaining their independent state. Given foldable module classes, its compiler constructs a static schedule that coordinates their execution, reducing dynamic synchronization overhead and making state accesses predictable. FoldSim backs state that exceeds on-chip capacity with external memory and brings it to the shared circuits as needed. A configurable DRAM model separates target-memory timing from host delays. The compiler explores replica allocations and state placement to balance resource savings against simulation time. On one AMD Alveo V80, FoldSim runs an 8-SM GPU and a 1,024-node Rocket datacenter with 4,096 processor cores. The unfolded implementations require approximately 16x and 200x as many LUTs as FoldSim's, respectively. The datacenter keeps about 1.9 GB of state in HBM, while a 4-SM GPU completes a 1024x1024 GEMM in 4.24 seconds, versus 26 hours in software RTL simulation.

papers.title: A constructive inverse for the Jordan--von Neumann operator on abelian groups
papers.abstract: For an abelian group $G$ and a real Banach space $X$, we study the inhomogeneous Jordan--von Neumann equation $\mathsf{Q}[f] = g$, where $\mathsf{Q}$ is the quadratic difference operator of the parallelogram law. We characterize the functions $g$ in the image of $\mathsf{Q}$ and, under a summability hypothesis, recover a solution explicitly by an iteration on the diagonal followed by a propagation argument; neither regularity of $g$ nor divisibility of $G$ is required. As a consequence we obtain a sharp stability estimate of Forti--Găvruţa type for the quadratic functional equation.

papers.title: Splitting the action: A fully nonlinear fluid method for clustering dark energy
papers.abstract: While the background evolution of dark energy is relatively straightforward to model, its perturbations, especially on nonlinear scales, generally require significantly more sophisticated treatment. Existing simulation methods for clustering dark energy --- a large class of interesting theories which are until now not well studied --- usually rely on grid-based solvers and perturbatively derived equations, whose validity in the nonlinear regime remains unknown. In this paper, we introduce a novel fluid method based on splitting the dark energy action into two parts: a kinetic part and a potential part. The resulting fluid equations are fully nonlinear and not reliant on simplifying approximations, making them suitable to describe the small-scale evolution of clustering dark energy theories, such as $k$-essence models with small sound speeds. We demonstrate the numerical implementation of this framework through spherical-collapse simulations of two representative $k$-essence models, evolving dark matter and dark energy simultaneously. The simulations are able to follow the development of dark-energy density perturbations throughout halo collapse, to $\mathcal{O}(\textrm{1}-10)$. By investigating their dependence on the dark-energy sound speed and dark-matter halo mass, we illustrate how dark-energy clustering responds to variations in the competing effects of pressure support and gravitational pull. These results demonstrate the applicability of this new framework to study nonlinear dark-energy clustering across a range of physical conditions, providing the foundation for its future extension to fully three-dimensional cosmological simulations through particle-based algorithms such as smooth particle hydrodynamics (SPH).

papers.title: Breaking the background and linear degeneracies: Using nonlinear clustering to discriminate between dark energy models
papers.abstract: We show that the traditional approach of parameterizing the background and linear-perturbation evolutions, through the equation-of-state parameter $w(a)$ and a time-dependent sound speed squared $\bar{c}^2_s(a)$, does not fully specify the cosmological behavior of dark energy theories. Using a new, fully nonlinear fluid framework, we perform spherical-collapse simulations of two clustering dark energy models with identical $w(a)$ and $\bar{c}^2_s(a)$, finding that their central dark-energy densities differ by up to 50\% for cluster-sized dark matter halos. We identify the departure of the local sound speed from $\bar{c}_s$ as the main driver of these differences. In contrast, all other theory-specific quantities in the fluid equations can be described by their background values to a very good approximation. The results demonstrate that nonlinear structure formation encodes critical additional information about the underlying dark energy theory, opening an avenue for discriminating between models using observables on small scales.

papers.title: Improved Bounds for Directed SSSP in Sparse and Intermediate-Density Graphs
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for exact single-source shortest paths (SSSP) in directed graphs with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges, and nonnegative real edge weights. When $m=O(n)$, it runs in $O(n\sqrt{\log n}(\log\log n)^{1/4})$ time. For $m=Θ(n)$, this lowers the exponent of $\log\log n$ in the bound of Duan, Mao, Shu and Yin from $1/2$ to $1/4$. At intermediate densities, writing $d=m/n$, the same algorithm improves on the bound of Duan et al. when $d\geq 3$ and $d\log(2+d)=o(\log\log n)$. For example, when $m=Θ(n\sqrt{\log\log n})$, it runs in $O(n\sqrt{\log n}(\log\log n)^{5/8})$ time, lowering their exponent from $3/4$ to $5/8$.

papers.title: Decision Fusion in Wireless Networks: A Tutorial and Survey of Classical and Learning-Based Methods
papers.abstract: Decision fusion combines local decisions from distributed sensors to support reliable detection of phenomena in wireless networks. The effectiveness of decision fusion depends on sensing accuracy, reporting-channel reliability, and available communications and computation resources. This article surveys decision-fusion techniques for wireless sensor networks and emerging communication systems, bringing together their theoretical foundations and practical implementation requirements. We review network architectures and hard, soft, and quantized reporting strategies, and examine statistical, learning-based, game-theoretic, and heuristic fusion approaches. Advanced fusion techniques, including relay-aware combining, link-adaptive regeneration, branch selection, and likelihood approximations, are discussed with emphasis on their assumptions, information requirements, and limitations. The survey examines tradeoffs among detection performance, computational complexity, communications overhead, energy consumption, and latency. The tradeoffs are considered across representative sensing applications and emerging technologies, including massive machine-type communication, ultra-reliable low-latency communication, uncrewed aerial vehicle-assisted networks, and the massive Internet of Things. The reviewed literature highlights the importance of jointly considering sensing quality, reporting reliability, and fusion processing when selecting a suitable strategy. Finally, we identify research directions in resource-aware optimization, uncertainty calibration, and robust learning-based fusion under heterogeneous data, missing reports, and changing wireless conditions. Particular attention is given to convergence, generalization, and the costs of training and inference.

papers.title: On the feasibility of using [Eu/$α$] to identify accreted and in-situ extragalactic globular clusters
papers.abstract: The chemical abundance ratio [Eu/$α$] has been proposed as a discriminator between ex-situ and in-situ stellar populations in the Milky Way and external galaxies. Here we show with a high-quality, homogeneous dataset of integrated-light abundances for 28 globular clusters (GCs), where 21 are extragalactic and 7 galactic, that this behaviour holds in other Local Group galaxies. In particular, we find metal-rich ([Fe/H] > --0.7) M31 GCs have uniformly low [Eu/Si]$\sim-0.4$, indicating they represent an in-situ population. Lower metallicity GCs in M31 generally show high [Eu/Si] $\sim+0.4$, suggesting they originated in accreted progenitors, and these GCs lie at larger projected radii from the M31 centre. Furthermore, we compare the M31 GC abundances with similar determinations for the M31 bulge for Na, Mg, Si, Ti, Ca, Eu, Cr, Mn, Ba, Ni, and Cu. The in-situ M31 GCs and M31 bulge exhibit similar abundance trends, excepting Ba -- and possibly Cr and Ti, suggesting similar star formation processes. [Eu/Si] in the M31 bulge is consistent with in-situ Milky Way stars, but is higher than the M31 in-situ GCs. For M33 and intermediate-mass dwarf galaxies, we identify a mixture of in-situ and ex-situ GCs, while for lower-mass dwarfs, we identify primarily in-situ GCs. These results suggest that accreted GCs in massive galaxies originated, at least in part, from intermediate-mass, intermediate-metallicity progenitors. We support earlier suggestions that [Eu/$α$] is a powerful in-/ex-situ separator for extragalactic GCs, demonstrating the potential of high-resolution integrated-light abundances for extragalactic archaeology.

papers.title: Statistical Inference with Ill-Conditioned Random Weight Neural Network Sieves
papers.abstract: Random weight neural networks (RWNNs) are shallow networks whose hidden-layer parameters are randomly generated and then kept fixed, while only the output coefficients are estimated. Conditional on the sampled parameters, RWNN regression is a linear sieve problem with random approximation space. We show that such random sieves cannot remain uniformly well-conditioned as their dimension grows. For parametrized feature families satisfying polynomial covering and Lipschitz conditions, the eigenvalues of the population covariance matrix are proven to have polynomial upper bounds determined by the covering geometry of the parameter space, leading to a vanishing smallest eigenvalue. We develop approximation, estimation, and inference theory that explicitly treats the ill-conditioning. Under a $β$-Hölder source condition, we obtain both faster-than-Monte-Carlo $L^2$ approximation rates and new $L^\infty$ approximation bounds based on stratified sampling. We then derive improved consistency guarantees for ridge-regularized least squares driven by ridge effective dimension, spectral, and leverage-based stability conditions. For inference, we establish asymptotic linearity and Gaussian limits for linear functional directions while allowing the smallest eigenvalue of the population covariance matrix to vanish. Nondegeneracy is directional: we characterize it with a ridge-normalized Rayleigh quotient and extend it to smooth functionals via Riesz representation. Consistency of ridge-adjusted variance estimators is proved, yielding feasible studentized inference. Numerical experiments illustrate the deterioration of random-feature conditioning and the finite-sample behavior of the resulting estimation and inference procedures.

papers.title: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation. However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions. To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target. Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment. TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.

papers.title: EgoCaptioner: Towards Comprehensive and Fine-Grained Egocentric Video Captioning
papers.abstract: Egocentric video captioning requires fine-grained detail and accurate timing, yet current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often miss brief actions, confuse their order, or misinterpret the wearer's motion. Existing caption formats also offer limited support for combining detailed narration with precise timing. We present EgoCaptioner, which pairs a video-level overview of the setting, participants, and the wearer's overall activity with timed steps whose narration adapts to varying perceptual demands and marks key moments at specific timestamps. We develop a coarse-to-fine annotation pipeline that establishes event structure before expanding step descriptions, yielding 50,000 training examples from eight egocentric video sources. Complementary rewards assess factual accuracy and coverage, measure step-level temporal alignment, and penalize fragmented or redundant narration, guiding caption refinement through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). To improve the reliability of factual supervision, we supplement caption references with pose-derived motion facts when sensor data are available. Across five egocentric benchmarks, EgoCaptioner achieves leading performance among evaluated open-source models in caption quality, caption-conditioned question answering, and temporal alignment. It also surpasses Gemini 3.1 Pro on PhysCapBench and all evaluated proprietary baselines on Minerva-Ego under the caption-to-QA protocol. Ablations support the complementary roles of factual and temporal rewards and show that coarse-to-fine annotation provides more effective supervision than single-pass annotation.

papers.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
papers.abstract: We establish a geometric framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms that are beyond standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. We also propose a generalized class Chern character and three conjectures: (i) the finite dimensionality of independent couplings at fixed derivative order, (ii) the representation of all-order mixed RR-gauge-scalar interactions through finitely many effective even forms, and (iii) the generation of higher-derivative contact terms from finitely many primitive tensor structures. Our framework provides a systematic mathematical foundation for reconstructing D-brane effective actions and exploring their underlying geometric and cohomological structures. We also introduce a higher-class pullback operator \( P_{\infty} \) and mixed transgression operators \( \mathcal{T}_{\infty} \), emphasizing amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as key physical data. This formalism distinguishes admissible tensor structures, presenting characteristic-form aspects as conjectures alongside their validity and their constraints.

papers.title: DeepQuest: From Knowledge Gaps to Scientific Discovery in Alzheimer's Disease
papers.abstract: Automating experiments does not necessarily advance scientific understanding. Research agents must identify meaningful knowledge gaps, determine what available data can resolve, and assess whether their findings advance existing knowledge. We introduce DeepQuest, a knowledge-gap-driven AI scientist framework for Alzheimer's disease research. DeepQuest transforms unresolved questions from domain reviews into traceable, testable hypotheses and prioritizes them through data feasibility screening and groupwise Elo ranking. It couples iterative experimentation with two-level auditing that separates experimental reliability from knowledge contribution relative to two frozen literature corpora. On OASIS-3, DeepQuest produces 42 feasible hypotheses and outperforms the strongest baselines in 14 of 15 evaluator-dimension comparisons across three language-model reviewers. The full framework achieves an audit-assessed scientific finding rate of 95.24%, outperforming both general-purpose executors and domain-specific research agents. This scientific finding rate remains stable across literature corpora and evaluator model families. Representative findings concern neuropsychiatric symptoms and dementia risk, longitudinal amyloid spatial stability, and neocortical tau-associated clinical impairment, with key associations supported in independent ADNI and AIBL cohorts. These results show how aligning knowledge gaps, data feasibility, and evidence auditing can turn automated research into traceable, evidence-supported scientific discovery. Our source code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DeepQuest-3066/

papers.title: C-LiTE: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Cellular feature learning in Histopathology
papers.abstract: Characterising individual cells is fundamental to computational pathology, as cellular morphology informs tasks such as tumour grading, mitotic assessment and immune profiling. However, most pathology foundation models are trained on tissue patches and capture cellular features only implicitly, while existing cell-level models are either restricted to specific cell populations or rely on computationally expensive architectures with hundreds of millions of parameters. Applying ViTs directly to small cellular crops also presents an architectural challenge: upsampling increases computational cost without adding morphological information and may introduce interpolation artefacts. To address these limitations, we introduce C-LiTE, a lightweight foundation model for cellular representation learning in H&E-stained histopathology, with only 22 million parameters. C-LiTE employs a native-resolution tokenisation strategy tailored to cellular inputs, processing 64 x 64 px cell-centred crops using a 4 x 4 patch embedding to produce a 16 x 16 token grid without image upsampling. To transfer visual knowledge from large-scale pre-training, we adapt the patch embedding weights of a pre-trained ViT-5-S using a pseudoinverse-based transformation, enabling weight initialisation at the finer patch resolution. We further assemble a pre-training dataset of 60 million cell-centred crops from TCGA, balanced across 19 cancer types and 16 tissue types. To our knowledge, this represents the largest public dataset for self-supervised pre-training on H&E images at the cellular level. We evaluate C-LiTE on seven public datasets spanning mitotic figure recognition, nucleus and cell-type classification, and immune cell phenotyping. Under frozen-feature evaluation, C-LiTE achieves a mean macro-F1 of 0.670, approaching CytoFormer (0.682) with approximately 30x fewer parameters.

papers.title: Frontier models need only one text to unmask its human or AI author
papers.abstract: Given a single text and a simple zero-shot prompt (no web access, tools, candidate lists, or writing samples), frontier models can answer "who wrote this?" at three increasingly specific levels: (1) whether an AI or human wrote it, (2) if an AI, which lab, and (3) if a human, often exactly who. The latest models (Claude Fable 5.2, GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Carbon) match trained detectors like Pangram while also explaining their predictions in natural language, and Opus 5.5 names the correct lab for 98% of texts generated by models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google. Most strikingly, Fable 5.2 correctly names the author of 55% of 15K anonymous ICML 2020 reviews that were never made public, and identifies the username behind 69% of comments from active Redditors (with >500 posts over the last year). Accuracy depends on exposure to an author's writing in pretraining data and on reasoning effort, and simply asking a model how familiar it is with someone predicts whether it can identify their writing. For anyone who has published enough writing online, frontier models present a greater threat to anonymity than commonly assumed, and defenses are limited.

papers.title: FlexVSR: Continuous-Scale Super-Resolution for Streaming Video Generation
papers.abstract: Real-time streaming video generation has gained rapid momentum in live content creation and interactive media. Deploying such systems in practice requires flexible scaling factors to accommodate diverse source resolutions, target displays, and computational budgets. However, extending fixed-scale generative video super-resolution (VSR) to varying target scales poses two challenges: downsampling from a larger fixed scale incurs redundant cost, while re-optimizing the diffusion transformer (DiT) is costly and alters the shared generative prior. To address both, we propose FlexVSR, a decoupled framework for continuous-scale streaming generative VSR with supervision at only a few scales. Our key insight is that naively resampling fixed-scale latents onto a new target grid induces scale-dependent input mismatch, which can be effectively addressed through parameter-efficient, scale-aware adaptation of the latent interface without updating the DiT. To this end, FlexVSR introduces ReLSA (Refined Latent Scale Adaptation), a lightweight latent adapter that constructs and refines target-grid latents before they enter the DiT, enabling a shared frozen VSR prior to generalize across continuous scales with only 0.274M trainable parameters and an adaptation cost of 7.3 H100 GPU-hours, while introducing no additional temporal dependencies and preserving the native causal streaming protocol. Extensive experiments demonstrate competitive or superior reconstruction and temporal quality, lower latency than most native-scale streaming baselines and offline methods, and effective generalization to unseen continuous scales, filling the continuous-scale gap in real-time streaming generative VSR.

papers.title: Products of Distinguisher Hulls
papers.abstract: The distinguisher hull of two distributions is the convex hull of the pairs of acceptance probabilities of tests in a specified class. We study its behavior under independent products for size-bounded Boolean circuits. We derive a geometric consequence of Dwork and Tankala's supersimulator theorem (FOCS 2026), giving a substantially different proof of approximate product containment for distinguisher hulls. In particular, our construction uses nonadaptive sampling in place of adaptive score corrections.

papers.title: GDNShift: Live Migration and Joint State Scheduling for Gated DeltaNet Inference
papers.abstract: Live migration of a streaming Gated DeltaNet (GDN) request requires rebuilding its recurrent state at the correct token boundary on a replica with identical weights. We propose a cross-replica recovery protocol based on compact update logs and implement and numerically validate exact catch-up. Compact logs stream a base state and ordered updates while the source continues decoding. Exact catch-up uses native single-token decode and releases the source once the destination has what it needs to continue independently. Across 120 complete pure-GDN configurations on three dual-GPU deployments, compact logs reduced the mean exact handoff gap from 790.8 to 149.5 ms relative to a background snapshot. Exact catch-up reduced mean source release time from 818.0 to 42.7 ms. In a prospective cross-host evaluation with relaxed arithmetic, a sealed selector chose the minimum-gap path in 39 of 40 configurations and reduced mean gap by 2.17% over a frozen network lookup. In nine whole-request migration paths for hybrid Qwen3.5-0.8B, the KV transfer ranking changed with the GDN path in 51 of 90 configurations. Per-configuration hindsight selection among the evaluated exact paths reduced mean gap by 34.7% over the best measured KV transfer paired with a GDN snapshot. In a separate held-out replay on 30 configurations, a locally calibrated selector reduced the exact gap by 15.4% over frozen network lookup.

papers.title: Power topologies and uniformities on bistochastic operators
papers.abstract: We prove that the set of invertible Koopman operators attached to the usual interval probability space is dense (and hence dense $G_δ$) in the space of bistochastic operators in the polynomial weak topology. This extends the non-polynomial analogue (due to Brown / Vershik / Ryzhikov / Eisner). We also show that the plain and polynomial weak topologies are distinct on bistochastic operators, confirming the distinction between the two results. Furthermore, the power topologies on the space of bistochastic operators recording weak convergence in powers up to $k+1$, $k\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ are all distinct, as are the analogous power uniformities on the automorphism group of the standard non-atomic Lebesgue probability measure.

papers.title: Optimal Patrol Widths in the Infinite-Corridor Barrier-Guarding Game
papers.abstract: A guard of speed at most one and capture radius $r$ patrols an infinite corridor. An intruder knows the patrol and can follow any path of speed at most $q$ from one end to the other. We determine where the maximum width permitted by straight wall runners can be guarded against all such paths. Write $W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ for the supremum over patrols with bounded longitudinal excursion and $F(q)=2r\sqrt{1+(3q^2+2q-1)^{-1}}$ for the wall ceiling on $1/3 < q < 1$. A four-leg bowtie attains $F(q)$ exactly for $q_a\le q < 1$, where $0.457892036651 < q_a < 0.457892036652$. For every $1/3 < q < q_a$ the supremum is strictly smaller. As $q$ approaches $q_a$ from below, $F(q)-W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $r(q_a-q)^2$. The lower estimate controls near-optimal patrols uniformly in their period. A rescaled bowtie gives the matching upper estimate. We also prove that periodic patrols give the same supremum as bounded-excursion patrols. For $q\ge1$ the one-way optimum is $r\sqrt{4+q^{-2}}$, a transverse sweep. This sweep is optimal against transit in both directions for $q\ge1/2$. At low speeds, $qW_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)/r$ tends to two, and an explicit ten-leg patrol guards width greater than $(2/q-1.235353)r$ throughout $0 < q\le1/40$. Rational spacetime and flux certificates give finite-speed bounds, including $6.944691333740r < W_{\mathrm{opt}}(1/4)\le8.10r$.

papers.title: Tight Bounds for Distance-Unbiased Sorting
papers.abstract: We study elitist randomized local search for sorting permutations. In this model, each iteration considers a possible exchange of two positions. The entries are exchanged if and only if they are in the wrong order. We introduce \emph{distance-unbiased} selection rules, which may choose an arbitrary distribution over exchange distances but sample uniformly among all pairs at each chosen distance. For static rules, we prove that the optimal worst-case high-probability runtime is $Θ(n(\log n)^2)$. This establishes the asymptotic optimality of the harmonic sorter within this class and partially resolves an open question of Olesker-Taylor. We then allow the distance distribution to change either according to a predetermined schedule or adaptively using the current permutation and the entire history. Matching upper and lower bounds show that both classes have optimal runtime $Θ(n(\log n)^2/\log\log n)$. Thus, scheduled adjustments of the distance distribution improve the optimal static worst-case runtime by a factor of $Θ(\log\log n)$, while full-information adaptation provides no further asymptotic improvement.

papers.title: Running-Time Lower Bounds under FPT $\neq$ W[1]
papers.abstract: We revisit running-time lower bounds historically based on the Exponential Time Hypothesis. We survey bounds that can be recovered from earlier work under FPT $\neq$ W[1] and prove seven lower bounds for graph problems and set systems under the same assumption. The new proofs encode clique choices in few bits and control the target parameter in terms of the encoding. This lets us turn a sufficiently fast algorithm for the target problem into a fixed-parameter algorithm for Clique or Multicolored Clique. In several cases, the new bound matches the function of the parameter in the historical exponent, with the additional requirement that the cutoff for any prescribed saving in the exponent be computable.

papers.title: AI agents can redesign engineering parts with more than a thousand CAD parameters and nonlinear simulations
papers.abstract: Simulation-driven design of real engineering components has to meet three conditions at once. It runs on few solves, since a nonlinear finite-element simulation of a 3D part takes hours; its design space has many values, the hundreds to thousands of values of the part's CAD model; and a better design often needs a redesign, coordinated changes of the part's proportions rather than local polishing of its surface. Automated optimisers meet at most two of these conditions. Classical optimisers, Bayesian or derivative-free, need a person to cut the design down to a few parameters, and on all the values they need far more solves; industrial shape optimisers move every surface node of the mesh in one solve per cycle, but only in small steps that polish rather than redesign. We ask whether a general-purpose large language model (LLM) can meet all three by joining what it knows with what the simulation shows. GPT-6 Astra edits a magnesium stent through a CAD geometry parametrisation of about 1,650 values, with a budget of 15 simulations; every proposal is built in CAD, meshed and simulated with large-deformation plasticity and contact, and the LLM reads the full results of every solve. Within that budget it lowered the objective, a high percentile of the strains in the stent's bends, by 32%; on the same budget, the industrial shape optimiser Tosca improved the original design by a tenth and then stopped improving. An earlier GPT-6 Astra design, 25% lower in the same objective, was checked in an independent, higher-fidelity model of the full deployment with crimping and damage: it was 14% less strained than the original after the full chain, and its most damaged spot began to fail later and carried 63% less damage at full expansion. LLMs can thus join their learned knowledge with simulation data to adjust more than a thousand design values and reach valid designs with real improvements.

papers.title: Holographic Tessellations Tensor Networks $\{p,q\}$ from Entangled Quantum Tetrahedron in Loop Quantum Gravity
papers.abstract: The relationship between spin network states in loop quantum gravity and bulk--boundary duality is further explored using the tessellated holographic tensor network. We develop a holographic tensor network construction based on quantum entanglement between tetrahedra in loop quantum gravity (LQG). This construction relates four-valent intertwiner spaces and Bell states dressed with $SU(2)$ holonomies to effective tensors on hyperbolic $\{p,q\}$ tessellations. For the $\{5,4\}$ tessellation, six tetrahedra are assembled into a single effective cell with five network legs and one logical index. Provided that the microscopic transfer map has full row rank, a right inverse and a completion on the kernel space are employed to construct an isometric embedding, yielding an effective tensor proportional to a perfect tensor. The construction is generalized to the $p=2k-1$ family, with local dimensions supporting absolutely maximally entangled states. On finite networks satisfying a radial orientation condition, an appropriate normalization produces an isometric bulk--boundary map. For cuts satisfying the isometry condition on both sides, the boundary entropy decomposes into a link contribution $\sum_{\ell}\log(2j_{\ell}+1)$ and the bulk entropy, thereby providing a discrete realization of the quantum Ryu--Takayanagi structure. Applications to the black hole interior are formulated via postselection-based non-isometric encoding. Assuming additional Haar statistics, this framework is used to analyze the preservation of overlaps on average and the competition between entropy branches underlying the Page Curve. These results establish a constructive link between the geometric degrees of freedom of LQG and holographic codes, while clarifying the conditions required to connect them to geometric area in LQG, the location of the quantum extremal surface, and evaporation of black hole.

papers.title: Asymptotic Bounds for Codes in Toroidal Distance
papers.abstract: The toroidal distance naturally describes the geometry of codes over \(\mathbb Z_q\), where distances are measured modulo \(q\). In this paper, we study asymptotic bounds for codes in \(\mathbb Z_q^n\) under the toroidal metric. We first derive an explicit asymptotic lower bound from the classical Gilbert--Varshamov bounds for the Hamming and Lee metrics, which serves as a baseline for comparison. We then develop a saddle-point approach for the toroidal metric, which yields an asymptotic Gilbert--Varshamov lower bound and an asymptotic Hamming-type upper bound. For \(3\mid q\), we embed ternary Hamming codes into \(\mathbb Z_q^n\) and obtain another asymptotic lower bound for the toroidal metric. In addition, we derive an asymptotic lower bound for Maximum Toroidal Distance (MTD) codes. We compare these lower bounds with the baseline and prove that they are nontrivial in the corresponding parameter ranges. Finally, we compare the asymptotic bounds numerically.

papers.title: Learning optimal gaits and styles for terrain-adaptive quadruped locomotion
papers.abstract: Animals use many different gaits to locomote at different speeds across varying terrains. A longstanding question in biology and robotics is: which gait is best? This question is most often addressed from an energy-efficiency perspective on flat terrain, leaving open how the answer depends on terrain and on the criterion optimized. Here we show that gait optimality is determined jointly by terrain, performance metric, and velocity. We use deep reinforcement learning and networks of abstract oscillators, modeling spinal central pattern generators, to learn 11 quadrupedal gaits across diverse challenging terrains, together with the locomotion style (base height, foot ground clearance, foot offsets) that each requires. A second policy then selects among them to optimize a user-specified criterion such as cost of transport, base stability, or joint smoothness. Across these performance metrics and within this repertoire, every gait is optimal under at least one terrain-metric-velocity combination. The framework adapts zero-shot to gait couplings and styles never seen during training, to terrains far beyond the training distribution, and to larger quadrupeds five times the training mass. With a single additional pitch-tracking reward term, the same gait couplings also support bipedal-mode locomotion. Our method provides a general and systematic way to produce expressive locomotion and to select the gait best suited to a given terrain and criterion. Project page: https://guillaume10.github.io/terrain-gaits.

papers.title: GaussTrans: A Gaussian Interface Framework for Multi-Layer Refractive Transport
papers.abstract: We investigate surface modeling of multi-transparent interfaces to achieve accurate light transmission. The interplay of errors in geometric structure, light paths, and observation results during the reconstruction of transparent media with a high number of layers makes this a challenging problem. Some existing techniques address the reconstruction of transparent scenes by reducing the number of layers or simplifying light paths; however, this limits their direct applicability to high-order transparent scenes. We propose GaussTrans, a compact framework for light transport in high-order transparent scenes, consisting of three components: Gaussian-Field Hybrid Surfaces, Transport-Coupled Refinement, and Primitive-Guided Implicit Intersection. Gaussian-Field Hybrid Surfaces use a hybrid approach combining Gauss surfaces and fields to reconstruct different interfaces. Transport-Coupled Refinement reduces coupling errors by evaluating the entire light path. Primitive-Guided Implicit Intersection combines primitive support regions to reduce errors in the intersection of interfaces and rays. In experiments on datasets such as RefRef, GaussTrans achieves significantly higher accuracy with relatively low spatial storage requirements.

papers.title: On the solution of a question for meromorphic functions sharing three values IM and a fourth value CM in the complex plane
papers.abstract: In 1926, Nevanlinna (Acta Math. {\bf 48} (1926), no. 3-4, 367-391) proved that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ CM in the complex plane, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ are four distinct complex values in the extended complex plane, then $f$ is a Möbius transformation of $g$, two of the shared values, say $a_1$ and $a_2$, are Picard exceptional values, and the cross ratio $\left(a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4\right)=-1.$ Later on, Gundersen (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. {\bf 277} (1983), no. 2, 545-567. Correction: {\bf 304} (1987), 847-850) proved that if two non-constant meromorphic functions share two values CM and share two other values IM, then the functions share all four values CM. In 1992, Gundersen (Complex Var. Elliptic Equ. {\bf 20} (1992), no. 1-4, 99-106) proposed the following famous question: if two non-constant meromorphic functions share three distinct values IM and share a fourth value CM, then do the functions necessarily share all four values CM? This question is a long-standing question in the studies of the Nevanlinna's value distribution theory of meromorphic functions, and has not been completely resolved by now. In this paper, we completely resolve the question, and prove that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ IM and $\infty$ CM, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ are three distinct and finite complex values in the complex plane, then $f$ and $g$ also share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ CM.

papers.title: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models
papers.abstract: Latent world models predict the outcomes of action sequences, but comparing candidate plans through recursive rollout remains expensive at test time. We introduce Fast-JEPA, a latent world model planning framework that advances the success-latency Pareto frontier of predictive search. Fast-JEPA reorganizes predictive computation to support effective action-sequence search at low planning cost. It constructs a goal-directed plan to guide search and directly predicts the outcomes of complete candidates for efficient comparison, avoiding recursive state rollout during refinement. Across PushT, Reacher, Cube, and TwoRoom, Fast-JEPA achieves 96.50% average success rate with 2.41x faster planning than INTACT. Search-budget sweeps show that its competitive success and low latency extend across candidate counts and refinement depths. We further introduce DynaGoal, a benchmark for evaluating world-model planning under dynamic out-of-distribution conditions, execution deadlines, and controlled response delays. Fast-JEPA achieves average success rates of 73.83% on DynaGoal-Shift and 87.67% on DynaGoal-Deadline, demonstrating the practical value of low-latency predictive planning under changing control conditions and execution-time constraints. Our project page is available at https://deepcybo-physai.github.io/Fast-JEPA.

papers.title: ROAM-GRPO: Enforcing Reasoning Diversity in GRPO via Routed Off-mode Approach Mining
papers.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) paired with Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has become the dominant recipe for post-training LLMs on complex reasoning tasks, but has been shown to collapse the policy into a low-diversity mode. Repeated LLM outputs are nearly identical, and pass@k accuracy converges or degrades as a result. We propose ROAM-GRPO (Routed Off-mode Approach Mining for GRPO), an augmentation to the GRPO algorithm which incentivizes exploration of distinct reasoning strategies and aims to increase output creativity during evaluation. ROAM-GRPO detects well-solved problems during training and transfers them to an "off-mode" track. The model is prompted to produce distinct solution strategies to such problems, which are verified for logical validity and distinctness by an LLM judge and subsequently self-distilled into the policy. Training Qwen3.5-2b on a 1,000-problem subset of the MATH lvl5 dataset, ROAM-GRPO implementation increases peak pass@16 by 4.7 percentage points and correct embedding cosine distance by approximately 1.5-2x on a difficult evaluation set.

papers.title: momipy: A time-resolved momentum microscopy data analysis workflow
papers.abstract: Photoemission momentum microscopy is an emerging approach to photoelectron spectroscopy that is transforming electronic band structure mapping at both laboratory-based and large-scale facilities. Its extension to time-resolved measurements has recently enabled major advances, ranging from the femtosecond imaging of exciton wavefunctions to dark-field photoelectron microscopy of light-induced dynamics and strong light-matter interactions. However, the rapid acquisition of high-dimensional data sets (including electron in-plane momenta $k_x$ and $k_y$, kinetic energy $E_\mathrm{kin}$, time $Δt$, and more) poses substantial challenges for data handling and analysis. A typical workflow encompasses data acquisition, exploratory visualization, calibration and targeted feature extraction, with data management ideally guided by FAIR principles. Here, we present momipy, a Python package that streamlines the momentum microscopy data analysis workflow efficiently and at low computational cost. Among other features, momipy provides interactive 4D data visualization, energy and momentum calibration, space-charge correction, and a broad selection of multidimensional data analysis routines, including binning, momentum-map extraction and time-, energy- and momentum-resolved model fitting. momipy is accompanied by a selection of interactive example scripts, supporting adoption of momipy by both experienced researchers and users new to momentum microscopy.

papers.title: Polynomial spaces are locally Paley-Wiener: local spectral geometry, sampling, and interpolation
papers.abstract: We identify the local Paley-Wiener structure of multivariate polynomial spaces on centrally symmetric convex bodies and apply it to sampling and interpolation. For a Bernstein-Markov measure with a positive continuous density in the interior, the normalized reproducing kernel at scale $1/n$ converges to the Fourier transform of the uniform probability measure on the dual unit ball of the Baran metric. We call this set the local spectral body. It describes the frequencies available to polynomials near each point. By recovering local bandlimited functions together with their $L^2$ norms, we obtain bulk universality and Christoffel asymptotics uniformly on compact subsets of the interior. This connection allows us to use Fourier methods to study polynomial sampling. If weighted sampling is uniformly stable with asymptotically one node per polynomial coefficient, almost every local spectral body must admit an exponential Riesz basis. Combining this result with Ortega-Cerdà's theorem for smooth spectra, we show that in dimension $d\ge2$, a $C^2$ boundary with everywhere positive curvature forces a positive proportion of extra sampling nodes. This rules out uniformly stable complete interpolation on such bodies. The same lower bound on the number of nodes applies to positive cubature exact through degree $2n$, since such a rule preserves the squared $L^2$ norm of every polynomial of degree at most $n$. The corresponding local-to-global problem remains open. If the local spectral body at every interior point admits an exponential Riesz basis, can one choose exactly as many nodes as polynomial coefficients at each degree so that sampling and interpolation are uniformly stable on the whole body?

papers.title: RAVEN: A Self-RAG Based Agent for Threat Classification and Response
papers.abstract: Security event analysis in large enterprises can be overwhelming, as each alert typically requires manual in- spection by human operators. This process is time-consuming and prone to inconsistencies, especially in high-volume Secu- rity Operations Center (SOC) environments. In this work- in-progress paper, we present RAVEN: Retrieval-Augmented Vulnerability & Event aNalysis, an agentic framework designed to support SOC analysts by automating the initial stages of alert investigation. The proposed system leverages a Self- Reflective Retrieval-Augmented Generation-based approach to provide an initial classification of security events and enables interactive refinement through analyst-in-the-loop queries. Un- like traditional approaches that rely on generic mitigation strategies, RAVEN generates context-aware remediation sug- gestions by incorporating knowledge of the target enterprise infrastructure. We implement an early-stage prototype and report preliminary results on three balanced test sets of 400 curated web payloads each (SQLi, XSS, SSTI) and a qualitative case study of mitigation generation; an evaluation on IDS- generated alerts and a user study are ongoing and outlined as remaining work.

papers.title: ALIoTh: Orchestrating Multi-Agent LLMs for Autonomous IoT Penetration Testing
papers.abstract: Penetration testing in Internet of Things (IoT) environments, especially those composed of various different devices, e.g., smart plugs, smart cameras, and smart doors, presents great challenges across the phases of information gathering, attack surface enumeration, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. This paper introduces ALIoTh, a multi-agent, workflow-driven penetration testing framework that integrates Large Language Models agents within a Self-Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Self-RAG) architecture to autonomously identify and exploit vulnerabilities in IoT and Industrial-IoT (IIoT) environments. By leveraging state-of-the-art language models and orchestrating specialized agents via the LangGraph framework, ALIoTh dynamically plans and executes a full-spectrum offensive pipeline. This includes network, devices, and service enumeration, vulnerability assessment, payload generation, reverse shell deployment, and privilege escalation on each device. The Self-RAG mechanism equips expert agents with contextual access to IoT security knowledge, e.g., related documentation, tool manuals, and known attack techniques, enhancing their reasoning capabilities in scenarios involving multiple device exploitation and group policy manipulation.

papers.title: Language models represent more about emphasis than they can tell you
papers.abstract: Prosodic prominence can largely be predicted from text, but part of it depends on how the speaker reads the sentence. We examine how much information about emphasis language models recover from text, whether they can report it when asked, and what the speech signal adds. Using English speech data with automatically derived word-level emphasis labels, we compare frozen and fine-tuned text models, prompted large language models (LLMs) and speech models on the same words. The text models end within about one point of each other, at best 68.8% on the 3-way task, and make many of the same errors. With the prompts we tested, the LLMs do no better than a word-majority baseline, even with 500 examples. While LLM responses contain some contextual information, they contain less than linear probes find in the model representations, and the gap does not close when the answers are recalibrated or the question is asked differently. The best speech model reaches 84.7%. We argue that text determines only part of the emphasis, and that the rest has to be heard. LLMs encode what the text determines, but prompting reveals only part of it: LLMs represent more about where the emphasis falls than they tell us.

papers.title: The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers -- A simple Introduction
papers.abstract: The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here. We give an elementary introduction to the subject.

papers.title: A Simple Proof of Koray's Theorem
papers.abstract: In this note, I provide a direct and self-contained proof of Koray's (2000) theorem, by which a neutral and unanimous social choice function is universally self-selective if and only if it is dictatorial. Koray's (2000) original proof relies on results by Sen (1970) and Houthakker (1950) to construct a social welfare function for each alternative set. He then shows that these functions are Paretian and independent of irrelevant alternatives, allowing him to apply Arrow's (1950, 1951) impossibility theorem. Instead, I construct a cyclic preference profile and show that the voter who ranks the chosen alternative first is the dictator on every finite nonempty alternative set.

papers.title: CACO: Coverage-Aware Coordinated Optimization for Continuous Generative Retrieval
papers.abstract: Continuous generative retrievers powered by flow matching and diffusion sample multiple queries in item embedding space for approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search under fixed budgets. However, existing generative retrievers can suffer from retrieval overlap under uncoordinated sampling, whereas explicit diversity guidance to broaden the candidate set may induce relevance drift as it lacks direct feedback on the value of additional items. We introduce CACO (Coverage-Aware Coordinated Optimization), a self-supervised post-training framework coordinating queries from frozen flow-matching and diffusion retrievers toward complementary item coverage with negligible latency overhead. Using empirical retrieval frequencies across sampled reference queries as a relevance proxy, CACO formulates a label-free coverage objective that improves recall across all 30 backbone-dataset settings in offline experiments. To avoid the overhead of sampling reference queries at inference, CACO employs a coordinated query adjustment network combining inter-query bidirectional attention with gated relative directions, updating queries via bounded tangent-space projection and spherical retraction. During training, CACO applies tangential antithetic perturbations and counterfactual single-query replacement to measure each query's marginal gain, yielding an unbiased gradient estimator of smoothed set coverage across non-differentiable ANN search. On eight public benchmarks and an in-house 24-partition streaming industrial dataset, CACO improves Recall@100 and Recall@400 by up to 23.7% and 23.9% over the strongest baseline, cuts inter-query overlap by 53.3%-64.9%, and adds only 0.5%-3.0% inference latency.

papers.title: Fourier Bases from Optimal Eigenfunctions of Paley Graphs of Square Order
papers.abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and consider the Paley graph $P(q^2)$ on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. A well-known optimal eigenfunction of this graph is supported on the norm-one subgroup, where it takes the values $1$ and $-1$ on the two cosets of its subgroup of index two. Its support has the minimum possible size $q+1$. Starting from this eigenfunction, we construct a family of multiplicative translates and prove that they form a basis of the space of complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^{\times}$. After extending these functions to the whole field, the translates indexed by squares form a basis of one nonprincipal eigenspace of the Paley graph, while those indexed by nonsquares form a basis of the other. In particular, both nonprincipal eigenspaces admit bases consisting entirely of optimal eigenfunctions. The main ingredient is a multiplicative Fourier analysis of the shifted eigenfunction. We determine the moduli of all its Fourier coefficients and, in particular, show that none of them vanishes.

papers.title: LIFT: Lifting Language-Controlled Image Fusion to Free-Viewpoint 3D Scenes
papers.abstract: Multimodal image fusion traditionally generates a single fused image from paired observations at a specific viewpoint, limiting comprehensive scene perception and adaptability to diverse perceptual objectives. To overcome these limitations, we present LIFT, a novel framework for our proposed language-controlled 3D image fusion (L3D-IF) paradigm that extends multimodal image fusion from 2D images to free-viewpoint 3D scenes, enabling language-guided fusion tailored to diverse perceptual objectives. First, LIFT formulates Semantic Modality Binding (SMB), which interprets language instructions to identify semantic targets and their associated modality preferences and grounds these targets in corresponding regions of a shared Gaussian scene, establishing persistent semantic-to-spatial correspondences for consistent fusion control across viewpoints. Second, Language-Conditioned Gaussian Appearance (LCGA) is developed to achieve scene-wide multimodal appearance modeling by combining adaptive multimodal blending with language- and viewpoint-conditioned appearance refinement, enabling spatially adaptive realization of diverse fusion appearances while preserving source fidelity at pure-modality endpoints. Finally, we construct a Multi-View Language-Supervision (MVLS) dataset that associates language instructions and calibrated viewpoints with modulated fused images, providing effective supervision for learning instruction-dependent fusion from finite multi-view observations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LIFT achieves coherent multimodal fusion across continuous viewpoints, accurate semantic target localization, and consistent regional fusion control under diverse language instructions.

papers.title: TipDex-VTLA: Learning to Refine Actions with Visual Reliability and Tactile Feedback for Dexterous Manipulation
papers.abstract: Changes in illumination can induce action drift in dexterous manipulation even when the physical state remains unchanged. Although existing vision--tactile--language--action (VTLA) policies incorporate tactile feedback, when and how touch refines actions under changing visual conditions remains challenging. We introduce \textbf{TipDex-VTLA}, a VTLA policy that combines estimated visual action reliability and tactile forecast verification to regulate execution-time refinement. Specifically, Visual Action Sensitivity Estimation (VASE) learns visual reliability from a frozen reference policy's action sensitivity to illumination perturbations. Tactile Anticipation and Correction during Execution (TACE) compares predicted and measured touch at matched times and combines the resulting discrepancy with visual reliability to gate bounded feature corrections for unexecuted actions. This effectively helps to refine actions under challenging unseen visual conditions. We evaluate TipDex-VTLA on four real-world dexterous manipulation tasks and the UniVTAC simulation benchmark. TipDex-VTLA trained on data collected under normal visual conditions, achieves average full-task success rates of 87.5% (resp. 73.8%) under normal (resp. challenging unseen) lighting in real-world tasks, significantly outperforming some state-of-the-art methods. We will release the collected data and source code.

papers.title: Correctable Enrollment and One-Transaction Seed Proofs for Ethereum's Post-Quantum Migration
papers.abstract: A quantum computer running Shor's algorithm can extract the private key of every Ethereum account whose public key is published, and accounts exposed by their own transactions hold 54.6% of execution-layer ETH. As the first such machine may stay secret, a migration cannot wait for visible thefts, and once keys are extractable, legacy signatures no longer tell owners from attackers. We design a migration in which owners enroll post-quantum keys cheaply with their existing signatures before ECDSA is retired at a scheduled time, while a zero-knowledge proof of the wallet's BIP-39 seed can correct any such enrollment until a common deadline afterward; an account nobody enrolled stays frozen and recoverable by seed proof without a deadline. Each proof binds the new key, a nonce and a fee cap, so neither a paying sponsor nor a reordering block builder can redirect or replay it. Validators switch to hash-based keys first, at a finalized checkpoint and under a stated bound on the attacker's voting power. We prove the account guarantees under explicit assumptions, model-check the rules, and implement the design in go-ethereum and a Lean consensus client. A three-layer recursive hash-based STARK yields a seed proof of about 190 KB that fits one transaction, verifies in 38 ms and takes a median of 111 s to generate on a laptop; four proofs aggregate into one. In a ten-node simulation with mainnet-derived accounts and fee demand, block space rather than proving sets the duration: the 4.45 million accounts with at least 0.1 ETH would migrate in 29.4 days if all enroll before ECDSA is retired and in 235 days if all recover after it in batches of four. In a mass enrollment, an enrollment waits a median of 19.1 minutes in the public mempool, longer than published estimates for a fast quantum computer to extract its key, so owners with a seed and an unexposed key should migrate by seed proof.

papers.title: Invariants of subfactors associated to Petrescu's Hadamard matrices of order 7
papers.abstract: Petrescu's sixth-root $7 \times 7$ Hadamard matrix defines an irreducible, hyperfinite subfactor $N \subset M$ with Jones index 7. It is built from the spin model commuting square obtained from the Hadamard matrix by iterating Jones' basic construction. We prove that the standard invariant of this subfactor is minimal, i.e. the higher relative commutants consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Thus, the principal graphs of the subfactor are the Coxeter-Dynkin graph A$_\infty$. This solves a long-standing open problem. The main new idea is a congruence for the profile of the Hadamard matrix that restricts the order of rotation on the lowest-weight spaces in Jones planar algebra description of the standard invariant. Together with a uniform trace bound, this gives bounded annular multiplicities on a subsequence, which forces the principal graph to have norm at most two. We also show that the same result holds for most Hadamard matrices in Petrescu's one-parameter family. Specifically, the associated subfactors have Temperley-Lieb standard invariant at every transcendental phase and at every algebraic phase with residue $\pm1$ at a prime above three. In each fixed degree the exceptional set is finite and consists of algebraic numbers. Our methods apply to several other families of Hadamard matrices of order $q >4$ as well, and we show that the associated subfactors have A$_\infty$ principal graphs. These include real Hadamard matrices of order $q\equiv4\pmod8$, Hadamard matrices over $\Q(i)$ of order $q\equiv2\pmod4$ and cube-root matrices of order $q$ with $3\mid q$ and $9\nmid q$. For order six Hadamard matrices, we obtain the same result at every transcendental phase in Diţă's family through Haagerup's matrix and at every algebraically independent pair of phases in Karlsson's two-parameter family.

papers.title: Tenon: A Unified Programming Framework for Retargetable PIM Compilation
papers.abstract: Processing-in-memory (PIM) is emerging as a building block of heterogeneous systems for memory-bound workloads, and commercial prototypes now span near-bank SIMD engines, bank-level GDDR accelerators, programmable DRAM cores, and bit-level in-SRAM processors. Their programming stacks are fragmented: no abstraction or compiler is shared across vendors, and per-device models range from instruction sequences to C-like languages. Data layout further complicates the problem: tight compute-memory integration makes data layout a first-order optimization, yet existing PIM compilers lack a unified way to represent and optimize it. A key observation is that PIM compilation targets can be modeled as nested grids of compute and storage units connected by legal data-transfer paths. We present Tenon, a unified programming framework for retargetable PIM compilation. It decouples workload, compilation target, and cost specifications, so a workload is expressed once and compiled through a unified programming framework. Tenon generalizes the $\mathbb{F}_2$ linear layout algebra from GPU compilers to map logical work and data onto these compute and storage grids. It automatically constructs a minimum-movement data layout given a workload and a target specification. We evaluate Tenon on six PIM backends: five commercial backends and AttAcc, a state-of-the-art academic HBM-based PIM architecture. Across the commercial backends, it matches or outperforms vendor, expert, and compiler baselines, with geometric-mean speedups of up to $1.20\times$ and individual speedups up to $3.65\times$. For end-to-end GPT-13B decoding on AttAcc, Tenon-compiled workloads run $1.2$--$1.3\%$ faster than those compiled by DCC, a state-of-the-art PIM compiler, across all three batch-4 configurations. Together, these results demonstrate Tenon's performance portability across diverse PIM target families.

papers.title: LoopedWAM: Looped World Action Models for Elastic Inference
papers.abstract: World action models (WAMs) couple generative video modeling with robotic action prediction but typically require large video and action transformers, limiting deployment efficiency. We present LoopedWAM, a compact WAM that recurrently applies a shared six-block core in each expert, executing 30 transformer layers while storing only 12 blocks per expert. To account for their asymmetric inference costs, the video and action experts can operate at different depths: visual features are computed once per query, whereas action computation repeats at every sampling step. We further propose elastic self-distillation, which trains a single elastic checkpoint, LoopedWAM-E, across action-depth and sampling-step budgets. With only 0.58B policy parameters and no robot pretraining, LoopedWAM achieves 96.1% success on LIBERO, 91.9% on RoboTwin 2.0, and 52.2% on RoboCasaGR1, while using $7.4\times$ less peak GPU memory than Fast-WAM under matched inference measurements. On LIBERO, LoopedWAM-E achieves 96.0% success in 27.6 ms or 95.2% in 24.7 ms on an H100, providing multiple accuracy-latency operating points from a single checkpoint; with two sampling steps and four action loops, it stays within 0.5 points of LoopedWAM on all three benchmarks. Ablations demonstrate that weight-shared depth preserves competitive performance, while aggressive action-depth reduction requires explicit budget-aware training. On a real AgileX PiPER arm, LoopedWAM succeeds in 71.3% of 80 trials across four tasks.

papers.title: Technology-Enabled Fuel Supply Chain Resilience: An Integrated Information System for Real-Time Monitoring and Decision Support
papers.abstract: This study evaluates and extends the transactional information system described in an earlier fuel logistics study, focusing on data reliability, monitoring, and decision support. An author-led re-evaluation examined available Delphi and SQL code and compared a reconstructed source-derived baseline (R0) with a revised SQL Server system (R1) across twelve evaluation scenarios. Synthetic transactions and public US energy data were used for technical assessment, while organizational processes and supply delays were simulated. R1 improved data integration and reporting accuracy in controlled SQL Server tests and introduced stock-movement records, automated alerts, and recovery controls. On comparable data feeds, integration defect rates decreased from 2.90 to 3.46 percent in R0 to 0.14 to 0.49 percent in R1. For national weekly demand forecasting, selected methods did not significantly outperform the previous-year mean. Process and disruption simulations suggested improvements in manual workload and replenishment delays, although these outcomes depended on modelling assumptions and were not observed in operational settings. The study presents a revised transactional architecture for fuel logistics and distinguishes experimentally measured information-system performance from simulated organizational outcomes. Its findings highlight the potential of traceable inventory records, early exception detection, and recoverable information systems to support supply chain resilience.

papers.title: Mesh-Free Keypoint Learning for Category-Level 6D Object Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: Category-level 6D pose estimation relates partial RGB-D observations of unseen instances to a canonical frame shared across a category. Object-aware reconstruction helps adaptive keypoints retain the geometry of the visible surface. Common reconstruction targets select observed points by their distance to a registered instance surface. We present MORSE-Pose, which derives this support directly from standard pose and metric-size annotations.
